2327429.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Holds High-Level Economic Engagements in Berlin to Strengthen India–Germany Trade and Investment Ties
2327429.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Holds High-Level Economic Engagements in Berlin to Strengthen India–Germany Trade and Investment Ties
Shri Piyush Goyal and German Federal Minister Katherina Reiche Discuss Industrial Cooperation and India–EU FTA
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal held a series of high-level engagements in Berlin on October 22nd to strengthen India–Germany trade, investment and industrial cooperation. The engagements included a bilateral meeting with German Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy Ms. Katherina Reiche, the inauguration of the India Centre at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), an India–Germany Business Roundtable and participation in the Berlin Global Dialogue.

During the bilateral meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal and Ms. Reiche discussed opportunities for closer industrial collaboration and the potential of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) to expand bilateral trade and investment. The two Ministers jointly inaugurated DGAP’s India Centre in Berlin, which is intended to promote policy research and dialogue on India–Germany relations.

The Union Ministers also co-chaired an India–Germany Business Roundtable organised with DGAP and the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business (APA), with participation from German CEOs and business leaders. In their keynote addresses, Shri Goyal addressed accelerating growth and forging a new trade era, while Ms. Reiche spoke on transforming the FTA into industrial reality. The subsequent interaction focused on translating the prospective India–EU FTA into concrete trade and investment opportunities.

At the Berlin Global Dialogue, Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the panel discussion titled “New Era, New Alliances: The Third Path?” alongside Personal Representative of the German Chancellor for Investment, Mr. Martin Blessing; Singapore’s Minister for Manpower and Minister-in-charge of Energy and Science & Technology, Dr. Tan See Leng; and Chairwoman and CEO of Marcegaglia Steel, Ms. Emma Marcegaglia and the session was moderated by Prof. Dr. Lars-Hendrik Röller. Shri Goyal highlighted the importance of trust, complementary economic strengths and resilient supply chains in international partnerships.

Shri Goyal also held individual meetings with Member of the Board of Management of Bayer AG, Mr. Stefan Oelrich, and President of its Pharmaceuticals Division; Mr. Murat Akyildiz, Managing Partner of Knauf Group; and CEO of Fresenius SE & Co. KGaA, Mr. Michael Sen, to explore opportunities for business and investment cooperation.

Shri Goyal is accompanied on his visit to Germany and the Netherlands by a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups. The Berlin engagements form part of ongoing efforts to deepen the India–Germany Strategic Partnership, particularly in trade, investment, technology and industrial cooperation.

***

2327414.title: ARI promotes scientific waste management and sustainable gardening under swachhata special campaign 6.0
2327414.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
ARI promotes scientific waste management and sustainable gardening under swachhata special campaign 6.0
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Special Campaign 6.0, the Agharkar Research Institute (ARI), Pune, is promoting scientific organic waste management, nutrient recycling and sustainable maintenance of green spaces across its campus. The Institute produces approximately 6,000 kg of compost annually from fallen leaves and garden waste and utilises it in its gardens. This initiative converts organic waste into a valuable soil amendment, promotes resource conservation and demonstrates the practical application of circular economy principles by returning organic matter and nutrients to the soil.

Fig 1: Fallen leaves and palm fronds decomposing on the ARI campus, returning organic matter to the soil.

At ARI, fallen leaves and other garden residues are collected, crushed into smaller pieces and placed in a designated compost pit for in-house composting. The material is mixed weekly to facilitate aeration and microbial decomposition. Mature compost is harvested after approximately three to four months and used in the Institute’s gardens. During composting, microorganisms break down complex organic materials into more stable organic matter.

Fig 2: Compost pits at ARI, Pune, where fallen leaves and garden residues are composted in-house.

At ARI, a mixture comprising 80% compost and 20% soil is used for gardening helping improve soil structure, enhancing water-holding capacity, contributing to soil organic matter and supporting nutrient availability for plants. The annual production and on-site utilisation of compost facilitate the productive reuse of locally available organic resources and help reduce the need for externally purchased gardening inputs. It also reduces the volume of garden waste requiring disposal and supports more resource-efficient campus management. On-site composting may further reduce waste transportation and the environmental impacts associated with landfill disposal.

ARI maintains approximately two acres of gardens and green areas, contributing to plant diversity, biodiversity conservation and the environmental quality of the campus. The Garden Section maintains approximately 308 trees representing more than 100 species, 39 medicinal plant species, 2,300 ornamental plants and 800 seasonal flowering plants, along with a variety of vegetables. The Institute’s Orchidarium supports the conservation and display of orchid diversity and facilitates specialised plant conservation and educational activities. The maintenance of diverse trees, medicinal plants and ornamental vegetation strengthens the campus’s green infrastructure and promotes awareness of plant diversity and conservation.

Complementing its waste management initiatives, ARI promotes nutrition-sensitive horticulture through its 6×6 Nutrition Garden Model. Designed for a compact area of 6 × 6 metres, the model demonstrates the cultivation of 23 types of vegetables through systematic crop planning and efficient utilisation of available space. Developed with the nutritional needs of a family of five to six members in mind, the model illustrates the potential of home gardening to improve access to fresh vegetables and promote dietary diversity and household nutrition security. The planned cultivation of diverse vegetables can support more varied diets and reduce dependence on externally sourced produce, subject to seasonal conditions and actual yields. The model offers potential for replication in urban, peri-urban and rural communities, particularly where land availability is limited. It integrates scientific crop planning, sustainable horticulture and household nutrition within a compact growing area.

Fig 3: Nutrition Garden Model demonstrating scientific crop planning and efficient utilisation of garden space.

ARI’s initiatives demonstrate how scientific approaches to organic waste management, soil improvement, biodiversity conservation and nutrition-oriented gardening can contribute to a cleaner and greener institutional campus. By converting garden residues into compost and reusing the resulting material on-site, the Institute promotes waste minimisation, nutrient recycling and responsible resource management. These efforts reinforce the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0 by extending the concept of cleanliness beyond waste removal to include the scientific management and productive reuse of resources. ARI’s initiatives highlight the role of scientific institutions in translating environmental sustainability principles into practical campus-level action.

2327410.title: Unveiling the impact of black hole spin on flickering of light emitted from matter around the black hole
2327410.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Unveiling the impact of black hole spin on flickering of light emitted from matter around the black hole
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

Scientists have uncovered a pivotal mechanism explaining why the matter around rapidly spinning black holes, also called accretion disk may emit highly oscillating X-rays.

The study which zeroes in on a single physical mechanism to produce these flickering of X-rays across a broad range of frequencies reduces randomness in theoretical modeling of these exotic astronomical objects.

Black hole, the most compact object in the Universe, with massive gravity that prevents even light from escaping, can spin about its axis. Matter pulled toward a black hole by its strong gravity is called an accretion flow and it falls inward at high speed, producing non-thermal radiation.

This radiation often shows nearly regular variations in brightness, called QPOs. In black hole X-ray binaries, these oscillations can have frequencies ranging from less than one cycle per second to several hundred cycles per second.

Previous studies could either explain the low frequency oscillations, or had to invoke other exotic process to explain high frequency oscillations.

In order to fill the gap, Scientists from the Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), an autonomous institute of Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India took up the task of explaining how the oscillations of accretion shocks around a spinning black hole produce this wide range of frequencies. 

They used a computer simulation developed by the Numerical and Theoretical Astrophysics Group at ARIES to model the behaviour of viscous accretion flows around black holes. Scientists from Nicolaus Copernicus Astronomical Center, Poland and MJP Rohilkhand University, Bareily were also involved in this work led by Mr. Sanit Debnath and Dr. Indranil Chattopadhyay from ARIES.

The simulation follows the movement of matter while ensuring that important physical quantities such as energy, mass, and momentum are conserved. This helped the researchers understand how these rapidly moving flows behave and how their oscillations can produce the observed variations in radiation from black holes.

Fig :Time series of luminosity for two different 𝛼=0.01, 0.035, and their corresponding power density spectrum (PDS) is shown for the model A91.2. We assume black hole mass is 10M⊙.

Their findings were recently published in the Journal of High Energy Astrophysics (JHEAP). The researchers found that when the viscosity of the accretion flow becomes higher than a certain critical value, the normally stable shock in the disc becomes unstable and starts to oscillate. These oscillations in the accretion disc can produce the regular variations in emitted radiation, observed as nearly periodic flickering of light know as quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs).

The study also revealed that the spin of a black hole has a strong influence on the movement of the shock and the frequency of QPOs. In slowly spinning black holes, viscosity pushes the average position of the oscillating shock farther away from the black hole, resulting mainly in low-frequency QPOs.

In contrast, rapidly spinning black holes pull the shock closer to the black hole, producing QPOs over a much wider range of frequencies. For black holes with very high spin the predicted QPO frequencies can exceed 100 Hz for a black hole about ten times the mass of the Sun, similar to the high-frequency variations observed in black hole X-ray binary systems.

The simulations also show that as the black hole spins faster, the shock moves closer to the black hole and its oscillations become more pronounced. Interestingly, the study found a clear relationship between the QPO frequency and the gradient of photon flux with the frequency or in other words the photons index, providing another useful clue for understanding the energetic environment around spinning black holes.

These findings provide a clear physical explanation for why rapidly spinning black holes in X-ray binary systems can produce high-frequency QPOs. According to the researchers, this is the first numerical study to simulate an accretion flow in presence of internal friction or viscosity and where the thermodynamic relations of a relativistic fluid has been implemented. This simulation demonstrates how the black hole’s spin can influence the frequency of QPOs, in the most realistic scenario.

The results can help scientists better understand the origin of the rapid variations in X-ray emission observed from these systems.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214404826001059

2327413.title: INS TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT LISBON, PORTUGAL
2327413.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INS TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT LISBON, PORTUGAL
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Trishul concluded her port call at Lisbon, Portugal, on 21 Oct 26. The visit provided an opportunity for professional interactions, knowledge-sharing and the exchange of Best Practices with the Portuguese Navy, contributing to a better understanding of shared maritime interests and strengthening operational synergy between the two Navies.

During the port call, the ship’s Commanding Officer called on the Commander of the Portuguese Navy and held productive discussions focused on enhancing operational synergy and interoperability, as well as exploring avenues for further collaboration. The interactions reflected the continued engagement between the two Navies and their shared interest in strengthening maritime cooperation.

The ship was open to visitors, including members of the Indian diaspora and Portuguese naval personnel, who had the opportunity to visit and interact with the crew. The Ambassador of India to Portugal, HE Puneet R Kundal, also visited the ship and interacted with the officers and crew.

A cultural exchange was hosted onboard, providing an opportunity to foster camaraderie and promote mutual understanding. The event was attended by the Ambassador of India to Portugal, envoys of other countries, Rear Admiral Paulo Silva Pereira, Deputy Fleet Commander and Flotilla Commander of the Portuguese Navy, officers of the Portuguese and Brazilian Navies, and members of the Indian diaspora. The gathering reflected the close people-to-people connections and friendly relations underpinning maritime cooperation between India and Portugal.

The port call formed part of INS Trishul’s overseas deployment and provided a valuable opportunity to engage with the Portuguese Navy and the Indian diaspora. The visit reinforced India’s commitment to maritime cooperation, professional engagement and camaraderie with friendly maritime forces, while contributing to the enduring maritime partnership between India and Portugal.

2327376.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES PUBLIC PROGRAMME AT JAGDALPUR, CHHATTISGARH ON THE OCCASION OF BASTAR DUSSEHRA
2327376.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES PUBLIC PROGRAMME AT JAGDALPUR, CHHATTISGARH ON THE OCCASION OF BASTAR DUSSEHRA
LET US DRAW VALUABLE LESSONS FROM THE NATURE-NURTURING LIFESTYLE OF THE TRIBAL COMMUNITY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 4:29PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced and addressed a public programme at Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh today (October 23, 2026) on the occasion of Bastar Dussehra.

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Bastar Dussehra serves as a vibrant symbol of Chhattisgarh’s cultural pride and collective faith. The manner in which the entire community participates in the Bastar Dussehra festival is truly extraordinary. Various rituals of this festival foster a deep sense of connection and kinship among different sections of society.

The President said that Chhattisgarh has long endured the scourge of Naxalism. Through the coordinated efforts of the central and state governments, the region has been freed from the menace of Naxal violence and is now advancing rapidly along the path of progress. She was happy to note that in recent times, initiatives to provide financial support to tribal entrepreneurs and connect them with markets have been further accelerated. She expressed confidence that these efforts will prove instrumental in achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047 through equitable and inclusive development.

The President added that tribal communities worship nature which is life-giving. In the journey of development, we should draw valuable lessons from the nature-nurturing lifestyle of the tribal community. She underlined the importance of preserving and nurturing the nature.

Before the public programme, the President interacted with the local Manjhi and Chalki in the Muriya Darbar. She also visited the Rangoli and Dussehra exhibition at Jagdalpur.

Earlier, the President performed darshan and pooja at Maa Danteshwari Temple at Jagdalpur.

2327362.title: India moves to development phase of national action plan for inland small-scale fisheries
2327362.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2327362.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
India moves to development phase of national action plan for inland small-scale fisheries
India sets target of 30 million tonnes in fish production in next 5 years, says Union Fisheries Secretary
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi

India has moved into the development phase of a separate national action plan for inland small-scale fisheries, with a focus on livelihood improvement, enhanced coordination and better management of freshwater resources.Dr Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India  on Friday formally launched India’s development phase of the National Plan of Action (NPOA) for small-scale inland fisheries. The plan is being developed under the framework of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's (FAO). The initiative is being led by the Union Department of Fisheries in collaboration with the Bay of Bengal Programme Inter-Governmental Organisation (BOBP-IGO).

A two-day national workshop in Bhopal identified key priorities for developing the action plan, including a proposed programme of consultations with fishing communities and other stakeholders. Experts from fisheries institutions and stakeholders prepared a framework for the activities to be undertaken in the development phase.  Addressing the gathering, Dr Abhilaksh Likhi called for a mission-mode outreach programme to take India's proposed national action plan for sustainable inland small-scale fisheries to fishing communities across the country. “The document must translate into practical improvements in livelihoods rather than remain confined to government offices”, he said, adding that the proposed plan must prioritise sustainability amid climate crisis, and strengthen value chains to improve fishers’ income.

*30 million tonnes fish production in next 5 years*

Dr Likhi further said: “India has set a target of 30 million tonnes in fish production over the next five years, while seafood exports are expected to rise to Rs 1.25 lakh crore”. Highlighting the sector's current status, he said India had achieved an annual fish production of 19.7 million tonnes, with inland fisheries contributing approximately three-fourths of this output, while seafood exports had crossed Rs 70,000 crore.. However, Fisheries Secretary stressed that production and export growth must go hand in hand with securing the livelihoods of small-scale fishers.On sustainability, Dr Likhi flagged climate change and deteriorating water quality as major concerns for inland fisheries, pointing to challenges such as declining oxygen levels in water bodies. He said the plan must incorporate measures to build climate resilience, drawing on the experience of fishing communities who directly confront these challenges.

Diversity

“India's diverse inland fisheries sector, with its varied ecosystems, fishing communities and region-specific challenges, could serve as a model for the FAO to collaborate, pilot region-specific approaches and take the learnings to wider geographies.  The experiences of fishing communities across the country could help shape context-specific approaches to sustainable fisheries management and livelihood development, offering valuable lessons for wider application”, Secretary Likhi added. The proposed plan covers fisheries in rivers, canals, reservoirs, lakes, floodplain wetlands, tanks and cold-water systems.

“The development phase is expected to address issues relating to fishing rights and resource management, employment and decent work, gender equality, value chains and post-harvest trade, as well as disaster risks and climate change”, said Dr P Krishnan, Director of BOBP-IGO. The plan will be finalised through stakeholder consultations before its public launch next month and subsequent implementation.

Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Secretary Swantantra Kumar Singh, Joint Secretary  Dr Gunjan Krishna and FAO Project Officer Giulia Gorelli also spoke on the occasion.

2327353.title: CONCLUSION OF INDIA-RUSSIA BILATERAL NAVAL EXERCISE (INDRA 2026)
2327353.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
CONCLUSION OF INDIA-RUSSIA BILATERAL NAVAL EXERCISE (INDRA 2026)
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Sahyadri departed Vladivostok, Russian Federation, on 20 Oct 2026, following the successful conclusion of the bilateral naval exercise INDRA 2026, conducted between the Indian Navy and the Russian Federation Navy (RuFN).

The exercise comprised two phases: Harbour and Sea. The Harbour Phase featured key leaders’ interactions, cross-deck visits, Subject Matter Expert Exchanges, operational synchronisation activities, sports fixtures and cultural exchanges. These engagements facilitated professional interaction and the exchange of views and operational practices between personnel of the two navies.

The subsequent Sea Phase involved coordinated manoeuvring, integrated communications, helicopter operations and medical evacuation drills. These activities enabled participating units to practise coordinated procedures at sea, enhance communication and strengthen operational coordination and interoperability.

Sports and cultural interactions further fostered camaraderie and strengthened bonds between personnel of the Indian Navy and the RuFN, complementing the professional engagements and reinforcing longstanding naval ties between the two countries.

The successful conclusion of Exercise INDRA 2026 reaffirmed the enduring defence and maritime partnership between India and Russia. The exercise underscored the importance of sustained naval engagement, professional cooperation and interoperability in furthering mutual understanding and contributing to maritime security. It also reflected the shared commitment of the two navies to a secure, stable and peaceful maritime environment.

2327349.title: ICAR-CIRCOT Signs MoU for Technology Transfer of Protective Gloves for Cotton  Picking Workers
2327349.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR-CIRCOT Signs MoU for Technology Transfer of Protective Gloves for Cotton Picking Workers
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi

The ICAR–Central Institute for Research on Cotton Technology (ICAR-CIRCOT), Mumbai, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with M/s. Trust ARS Rubber Private Limited, Chengalpattu, on 22 October 2026, for the technology transfer of "Protective Gloves for Cotton Picking Workers."

This technology transfer is expected to facilitate commercialization and ensure wider availability of the gloves, directly benefiting cotton farmers and agricultural workers. By promoting the adoption of suitable protective equipment, the initiative aims to reduce hand injuries, improve working conditions, and foster safer harvesting practices, contributing significantly to the overall well-being of agricultural labourers.

The technology was developed to enhance the safety and protection of cotton-picking workers during harvesting operations. The specially designed gloves protect workers’ hands against injuries caused by sharp cotton bracts while ensuring flexibility and comfort. Additionally, their reusable and durable construction makes them well-suited for repeated use under demanding agricultural field conditions.

The collaboration marks an important step toward strengthening industry–research partnerships and translating ICAR-CIRCOT’s technological innovations into practical solutions for the agricultural sector. Through this partnership, ICAR-CIRCOT reaffirms its commitment to developing and transferring need-based technologies that address field-level challenges, enhance occupational safety, and improve livelihoods across the cotton value chain.

2327341.title: Chief of the Air Staff Undertakes flying sortie with Air Wing NCC Cadet
2327341.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Chief of the Air Staff Undertakes flying sortie with Air Wing NCC Cadet
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Chief of Air Staff (CAS), Air Chief Marshal AP Singh undertook a flying sortie with Senior Wing (SW) Cadet Jakkula Tejasvi Reddy of National Cadet Corps (NCC), on October 20, 2026 at the Air Force Academy, Dundigal. The sortie took place before the Air Chief’s final flying sortie with his first flying instructor.

As part of the pre-flight preparations, the cadet underwent cockpit familiarisation, safety briefings, ejection-procedure familiarisation and medical checks. Before boarding the Kiran aircraft, the CAS briefed her on its specifications, major components, engine functioning, cockpit procedures and safety mechanisms. During the sortie, he explained various flight manoeuvres, flight angles and steep turns. He also gave the cadet an opportunity to practise manoeuvres under his guidance.

The sortie provided Cadet Tejasvi with practical exposure to aviation and encouraged to pursue her aspiration of becoming an aviator. It also highlighted the opportunities available to NCC Air Wing cadets to gain experience in aviation and explore careers in the Defence Forces.

The National Cadet Corps continues to expand its training activities to develop skills, confidence and leadership among cadets. In line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, it aims to provide the youth with opportunities to develop their abilities and contribute to nation-building.

2327340.title: Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to Boost Investment, Value Addition and Exports from Inland Fisheries
2327340.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2327340.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to Boost Investment, Value Addition and Exports from Inland Fisheries
Madhya Pradesh Releases Fisheries Investment and Export Guidelines, 2026; Integrated Cage Culture Units Inaugurated Virtually
Department of Fisheries, Government of India issues Inland State Export Potential SOPs
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Government of Madhya Pradesh, in association with the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India (GoI) & NFDB, organised the Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 in Bhopal on 23 October 2026 to strengthen investment, processing, value addition and export opportunities in inland fisheries.

The Conclave was graced by Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; and Shri Narayan Singh Pawar, Hon’ble Minister, Department of Fishermen Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh, Dr Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India, Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, Shri Ashok Barnwal. Investors, exporters, fish farmers, entrepreneurs from India and abroad along with senior officials of the Central and State Governments and other stakeholders across the fisheries value chain, were also present.

 
 

The Conclave brought together investors, exporters, fishers, more than 1,000 fish farmers from across Madhya Pradesh, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs), entrepreneurs, start-ups, processors, financial institutions, research organisations and other stakeholders across the fisheries value chain.

India's fish production reached 197.75 lakh MT in 2024–25, of which inland fisheries contributed 151.60 lakh tonnes, accounting for nearly three-fourths of the country's total fish production. India's seafood exports were valued at ₹73,890 crore in 2025–26. The Conclave focused on connecting this production base with processing, cold-chain infrastructure, quality assurance, market access and exports.

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India, and Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, released the Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Investment and Export Guidelines, 2026, and the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) of Inland State Export Potential. These aim to facilitate investment across hatcheries, fish seed and feed, reservoir and cage fisheries, aquatic animal health, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, logistics, value addition and market development. Madhya Pradesh has been notified by the Central Government as a Reservoir Fisheries Cluster.

The programme also featured the virtual inauguration of integrated cage culture units and the handover of administrative approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in Madhya Pradesh.

Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh handed over the Administrative Approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs in Madhya Pradesh, under the Union Budget Announcement 2026–27, to the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh. The initiative envisages the development of 49 reservoirs in the State at an approved project cost of ₹8755.60 Lakh, and 5 Amrit Sarovar at an approved project cost of ₹69 Lakhs.


The initiative aims to harness the fisheries potential of reservoirs, enhance fish production and productivity, strengthen infrastructure, generate livelihood and employment opportunities, and improve the socio-economic well-being of fishers and fish farmers in the state.

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India, and Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, distributed certificates to beneficiaries under various fisheries-related initiatives, including the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) for fisheries, fisheries cooperatives, fisheries start-ups and the Performance Grant under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY).

  
 

Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, highlighted the fisheries sector’s growing potential as a driver of investment, entrepreneurship, industrial development and exports, noting the increasing participation of investors, exporters, entrepreneurs and start-ups. Emphasising water resource management, he stated that the State’s irrigation potential had increased to 60 lakh hectares over the past two and a half years, with a target of 100 lakh hectares by the end of the State Government’s tenure. He highlighted the Ken–Betwa and Parvati–Kalisindh–Chambal river-linking projects, alongside efforts to develop reservoirs and conserve traditional water bodies, to strengthen water availability and create opportunities for fisheries.

Announcing three key initiatives, he outlined the integration of fisheries with the food processing industry to promote processing, value addition, packaging, cold-chain infrastructure and distribution; support and incentives for fisheries enterprises under the MSME framework, including land and other facilities; and the launch of the Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Policy 2026, providing for land allocation and facilities for fisheries enterprises. These measures aim to attract investment, generate employment and unlock the State’s fisheries and aquaculture potential.

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India, noted that India exports fish to 130 countries, but inland states contribute only 2% of total fisheries exports, despite a 147% increase in fish production in these states. He emphasised the need to develop reservoirs and large ponds through scientific cage and pen culture, improve productivity and connect fish farmers with investors, processors and exporters. Welcoming the Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Investment and Export Promotion Policy 2026, he stressed that fisheries must be recognised and developed as an industry to attract investment, generate employment and enhance incomes.

He underscored the importance of quality fish production, efficient logistics, value addition, ready-to-cook products and reliable supply chains to meet international market demand. Highlighting traceability as essential for export competitiveness, he referred to the National Framework for Aquaculture Traceability 2025 and the National Fisheries Digital Platform, which support digital documentation across the aquaculture value chain. He also noted that MPEDA would support inland-state exporters with market intelligence.

Outlining five priorities for export promotion, the Union Minister called for identifying export-suitable freshwater fish species and target markets; developing fish collection centres and large-scale processing hubs; strengthening partnerships among farmers, cooperatives, investors and exporters; ensuring quality certification and traceability from the outset; and maintaining continuous engagement with international buyers and clear export targets.

He further urged stakeholders to follow the SOP released at the conclave, which provides guidance across the value chain, from fish seed stocking and production to export requirements. He called upon the State Government and industry stakeholders to work in a coordinated manner to position Madhya Pradesh as a leading contributor to India’s inland fisheries exports.

Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, GoI emphasising Madhya Pradesh’s vast inland fisheries potential, noted that the State’s extensive river network, reservoirs and favourable water quality provide significant opportunities for fisheries development. He highlighted the potential of Indira Sagar Reservoir for large-scale cage culture, noting that the development of one lakh cages could set a unique example for the country.

The Minister observed that the creation of an independent Department of Fisheries in 2019 had accelerated the sector’s growth and strengthened its development vision. He emphasised that inland fisheries, which account for approximately 75% of India’s fish production, offer substantial opportunities for investment, exports and livelihood generation. He underlined the important role of inland states, particularly Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar and Chhattisgarh, in driving the next phase of fisheries sector growth.

 Shri Narayan Singh Panwar, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Department of Fishermen Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh, highlighted the State Government’s efforts to transform fisheries from a livelihood activity into a growth-oriented sector driven by modern technology, investment, entrepreneurship, employment and higher incomes. In this direction, the Integrated Fisheries Industry Policy 2026 has been launched to enhance fish production through better utilisation of water resources and large-scale promotion of modern cage culture in suitable districts.

Emphasising the importance of translating investment and technology into local benefits, he noted that increased production would enhance incomes and create employment opportunities for fisher families. With the support of the Government of India, the Sardar Sarovar, Indira Sagar and Vindhyavasini clusters are being developed, with efforts to replicate successful models across other districts and establish an integrated system from production to market.

He further stated that the Department would act as a facilitator and partner, connecting investors, fish farmers and fishing communities to enable viable investments at the grassroots level. Inviting investors and entrepreneurs to participate in Madhya Pradesh’s inland blue economy, the speaker reaffirmed the State’s commitment to increasing production, attracting investment, generating employment and ensuring the prosperity of fisher families.

Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India, highlighted the untapped export potential of inland fisheries. He noted that freshwater species such as Pangasius and Tilapia currently account for only 2% of seafood exports, with a target to increase their share to 10% over the next five years. States such as Madhya Pradesh can play a key role by utilising reservoirs, ponds, lakes and rivers, alongside investments in infrastructure, cold chains, certification and export market access.

Dr Likhi further highlighted the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for cargo handling, prepared by the Government of India with MPEDA’s support, to facilitate inland fish exports. The Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Investment and Business Promotion Policy 2026 was also noted as an important initiative. Over the next five years, a cluster-based approach under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), in collaboration with State Governments, will support training, value addition, packaging, branding and export logistics for inland fish and seafood, he added.

Shri Ashok Barnwal, Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, highlighted the State’s ambitious plan to increase fish production from 4.5 lakh tonnes to 10–11 lakh tonnes over the next two to three years through the adoption of modern fisheries technologies under the Blue Revolution.

He stated that the proposed expansion could generate an estimated ₹5,000 crore in additional annual income for the fisheries sector, benefiting at least 50,000 people. Emphasising the sector’s transformation from a supplementary livelihood activity into a driver of investment and full-time employment, he invited investors and industry stakeholders to partner with Madhya Pradesh in developing fisheries exports, processing and backward linkages.
 

The Conclave highlighted the need to move beyond a production-oriented approach towards integrated fisheries value chains that connect production with processing, value addition, branding and markets. Stronger cold-chain connectivity, quality standards, certification and logistics can help inland fish products reach wider domestic and international markets.

The discussions and initiatives are expected to strengthen collaboration among Central and State Governments, investors, exporters, financial institutions, research organisations, fisheries cooperatives and entrepreneurs, translating Madhya Pradesh's inland fisheries potential into investment opportunities, stronger value chains and improved livelihood opportunities for fishers and fish farmers.

Background Note

  • Madhya Pradesh has 4.50 lakh hectares of inland water area, including 3.75 lakh hectares of reservoirs, providing a substantial production base for inland fisheries and aquaculture. Major species produced in the State are Rohu, Catla, Mrigal, Tilapia, Pangasius, Common Carp and Grass Carp.
  • Under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has accorded approvals to Madhya Pradesh at a total project cost of ₹910.81 crore, with a Central share of ₹305.50 crore, and released ₹301.27 crore, equivalent to about 98.61per cent of the approved Central share. As a result, fish production in Madhya Pradesh increased from 2.00 lakh MT in 2019-20 to 4.45 lakh MT in 2024-25, registering an increase of about 123 per cent.
  • The major production-related interventions approved under PMMSY include 78 hatcheries, 1,157 RAS and biofloc units, expansion of pond area by more than 5,700 hectares and one Integrated Aquapark.
  • Under the Budget Announcement 2026-27, integrated development of 49 reservoirs and 5 Amrit Sarovars are approved to Madhya Pradesh with an investment of Rs. ₹88.25 crore. Madhya Pradesh has established 316 cages in Halali Reservoir notified as a Reservoir Fisheries cluster. The Integrated Cage Culture units being inaugurated during this programme will further support planned production and marketing of fish.
  • Under FIDF, five projects have been approved in Madhya Pradesh:(i) fisheries training centre at a cost of ₹5.00 crore, (ii) cold storage at a cost of ₹1.21 crore, (iii) two innovative Projects at a cost of ₹0.44 crore and (iv) Establishment of Disease Diagnostic lab at a cost of ₹ 0.27crore. so far out of 5 projects 1 project related to fisheries training centre is ongoing while 4 yet to start.

2327336.title: Capacity Building Commission was conceptualised by PM Narendra Modi ji who had initiated a series of governance reforms soon after he took over in 2014, says Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
2327336.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2327336.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Capacity Building Commission was conceptualised by PM Narendra Modi ji who had initiated a series of governance reforms soon after he took over in 2014, says Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Says, Mission Karmayogi Marks Shift from Rule-Based to Role-Based Governance; Calls Training Institutions Key to Civil Services Transformation
At Lucknow, Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Yogi Adityanath ji Joins Dr. Jitendra Singh at Sadhana Shrinkhla Regional Workshop
Modi Govt’s Administrative Reforms Aim to Build a More Responsive, Citizen-Centric Governance System, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr Jitendra Singh lauds Uttar Pradesh for leading iGOT Karmayogi Participation with Over 19 Lakh Officials Registered:
Training Institutions Must Evolve into Centres of Excellence to Strengthen Civil Services Capacity Building: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that Mission Karmayogi represents a fundamental shift in governance from a rule-based system to a role-based approach, equipping government officials with the competencies required to discharge their responsibilities effectively.

Addressing the third regional workshop of Sadhana Shrinkhla 2026 at Lucknow, the Minister said, Capacity Building Commission was conceptualised by PM Sh Narendra Modi ji who had initiated a series of governance reforms soon after he took over in 2024, and added that capacity building is central to the civil services transformation, with the ultimate objective of improving governance and public service delivery. He also lauded the Yogi Government for effective implementation of these governance reforms in Uttar Pradesh.

The two-day workshop, organised by the Capacity Building Commission in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh on October 23-24, brings together representatives from eight States and four Union Territories of the Northern Region to deliberate on transforming government training institutions into modern, competency-driven Capacity Building Institutions.

The workshop was graced by the presence of Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath. The programme was also attended by S. Radha Chauhan, Chairperson, Capacity Building Commission; Alka Mittal, Member, Capacity Building Commission; Shashi Prakash Goyal, Chief Secretary, Government of Uttar Pradesh; Devaraj, RUPAAM Director General Devaraj, Director Galong with senior officials of the Uttar Pradesh Government and representatives from various States and Union Territories.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the administrative reform journey initiated under Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2014 has focused on simplifying procedures, strengthening public trust and making governance more accessible. Citing the removal of the requirement for gazetted officers to attest documents and the discontinuation of interviews for certain government recruitment processes, he said these measures reflected confidence in citizens and a commitment to fairness in public administration. He also referred to Rozgar Melas, CPGRAMS and Digital Life Certificates as examples of reforms that have simplified procedures and improved the delivery of public services.

Referring to CPGRAMS, the Minister said that annual public grievance registrations had increased from around two lakhs in 2014 to approximately 25 lakhs, reflecting greater public confidence in the grievance-redressal mechanism. With around 95–97 per cent of grievances being disposed of in a time-bound manner, citizens increasingly expect their concerns to receive a response. He also spoke about Digital Life Certificates, including the use of biometric and facial-recognition technologies, which have eased compliance for pensioners and reduced the need for cumbersome physical procedures.

The Minister said that the Capacity Building Commission represents an important institutional step in this reform journey. Capacity building must prepare government employees to move beyond routine file processing and develop the competencies required to perform their roles effectively. The objective, he said, is to create a civil service that is equipped to take responsibility, adapt to changing requirements and deliver tangible improvements in governance.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that government training institutions must become central to this transformation. Traditionally custodians of institutional knowledge and experience, they need to evolve beyond delivering conventional training programmes and become Capacity Building Institutions that respond systematically to the competency requirements of government.

A structured framework can help them strengthen institutional governance and faculty capabilities, improve curricula and pedagogy, build partnerships, adopt technology and assess the outcomes of their interventions. Over time, this would enable institutions to develop specialised expertise and emerge as Centres of Excellence.

Referring to the principles of Tradition, Technology and Tangible Outcomes, the Minister said that these three elements provide a practical direction for strengthening capacity building under Mission Karmayogi. Training institutions represent tradition through accumulated knowledge and institutional experience; iGOT Karmayogi enables technology-driven learning at scale; and Human Resource Management Systems can connect competencies with the professional journeys and deployment of officials.

Integrating these elements can help government align the competencies required for a role with the learning undertaken by an official and the responsibilities subsequently assigned, giving practical meaning to the shift from rule to role.

The Minister congratulated Uttar Pradesh for its performance in implementing capacity-building initiatives. He said that more than 19 lakh officials and employees from the State had registered on iGOT Karmayogi, contributing to national participation of approximately 1.7 crore.

He also drew attention to the popularity of courses on Yoga and Artificial Intelligence among learners from Uttar Pradesh, describing this combination as an example of how traditional knowledge and modern technology can advance together. He commended the State administration for its efforts and said its performance could inspire other States.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also appreciated Uttar Pradesh’s contribution to UNNATI, the Unified New Age National Training Initiative, which connects training institutions to facilitate collaboration, resource sharing and alignment with government’s capacity-building requirements.

Referring to the figures cited during his address, he said that more than 370 training institutions from Uttar Pradesh had joined the initiative, against around 110 institutions nationally. He said that a stronger network of training institutions would support the exchange of expertise and good governance practices across States.

The Minister said that the success of capacity-building initiatives must ultimately be measured by their impact on the ground, rather than merely by the number of training programmes conducted or officials trained. Their contribution should be reflected in the competencies developed, institutional leadership nurtured and improvements achieved in government performance.

He added that training institutions should increasingly serve as centres of learning, mentorship and leadership development, working with academic institutions, industry and practitioners while remaining focused on citizen-centric governance.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also commended Uttar Pradesh for its contribution to good governance initiatives, recalling the State’s participation in the Good Governance Index and regional efforts to disseminate effective administrative practices. He expressed confidence that, under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh would continue to serve as a model for sharing good governance practices with other States and Union Territories.

The Minister expressed gratitude to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for his support and for facilitating the Sādhana Śhrinkhla workshop in Uttar Pradesh. He said the initiative provided an opportunity to bring together States and Union Territories to advance the transformation of government training institutions and strengthen the capacity of civil servants to deliver effective, accountable and citizen-centric governance.

2327334.title: 202nd Victory Celebration and Birth Anniversary of Rani Chennamma Celebrated with Grandeur at Prerana Sthal, Parliament Premises
2327334.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
202nd Victory Celebration and Birth Anniversary of Rani Chennamma Celebrated with Grandeur at Prerana Sthal, Parliament Premises
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:13PM by PIB Delhi

The birth anniversary of Kittur Rani Chennamma and the 202nd Victory Celebration were commemorated with great grandeur today at Prerana Sthal in the Parliament premises, New Delhi, under the leadership of Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti and Member of Parliament from Tumakuru, Shri V. Somanna.

 

 

The programme was graced by Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla, Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C.R. Patil, MP Shri P.C. Mohan, Dr. Sudhakar, former ministers Shri Murugesh Nirani, Shri Basanagouda Patil Yatnal, former Special Representative of Karnataka in New Delhi Shri Shankargouda Patil, Pujya Shri Basava Mrutyunjaya Swamiji of Kudalasangama, Shri Shankarananda Swamiji, Shri Siddharoodha Matha, Aluru, Bidar, Shri Atmaram Swamiji, Shri Gurudeva Ashrama, Kakkamari, Shri Vinayak Swamiji, Shri Siddharoodha Matha, Chalakapura, and a large number of Kannadigas from different districts of Karnataka and from Delhi who paid floral tributes to Rani Chennamma.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister V. Somanna extended his heartfelt greetings to the people of the country on the occasion of the birth anniversary of the nation's unparalleled woman warrior, the brave queen of Kittur, Rani Chennamma and her 202nd victory celebration against the British.

He expressed gratitude on behalf of all Kannadigas to Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla and Union Minister Shri C.R. Patil for gracing the occasion and adding grandeur to the programme.

"Kittur Rani Chennamma was not just a queen who fought a war; she challenged an imperial power and remains in history as an immortal symbol of resistance. It is a matter of great joy that we have got an opportunity to celebrate the achievements of such a brave woman," the Minister said.

"The valour, courage and fire of Veera Vanithe Rani Chennamma at this sacred place of the Indian Parliament is an inspiration to the bravehearts who protect the country today. It is a matter of pride for all of us who have love for our land and language. Let us all gather here every year and remember such great personalities," he appealed.

He thanked Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on behalf of the people of the state for permitting this programme every year and being an inspirational force for all.

He also thanked Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla, officials of Lok Sabha and Ministry of Railways, and Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw for granting permission and cooperation.

Pujya Shri Basava Mrutyunjaya Swamiji, who spoke on the occasion, expressed great happiness about the initiative of Union Minister V. Somanna in organizing such a programme every year at Prerana Sthal in Parliament.

2327332.title: In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the work to establish a vibrant Civil Defence Network in the country is set to begin
2327332.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the work to establish a vibrant Civil Defence Network in the country is set to begin
Three-day specialized training for Civil Defence Master Trainers to be conducted in 12 States/UTs in the first phase
In 1st phase, 600 Civil Defence Master Trainers, 50 from each participating State/UT, are proposed to be trained by the second week of November 2026
Following the specialized training, each Master Trainer will impart further training to 100 Civil Defence Volunteers in their respective State/UT
The initiative seeks to enhance the preparedness of Civil Defence personnel to respond effectively to emergencies
The training will cover three broad areas: Threat Awareness, Protection and Emergency Response and Communication and Coordination
A key feature of the initiative is its multiplier effect through a structured Master Trainer Model
Initiative marks a significant step towards combining the Indian Army’s operational expertise with the Civil Defence volunteer network
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi

In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India to build a vibrant Civil Defence Network with first-of-its-kind Joint Training Initiative with the Indian Army. A three-day specialized training for Civil Defence Master Trainers to be conducted in 12 States/UTs in the first phase.

In his address to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on 15 August 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced the vision of building a vibrant Civil Defence network, equipped with modern systems, technologies and contemporary preparedness capabilities to address emerging security challenges. In furtherance of this vision, the Directorate General of Fire Services, Civil Defence & Home Guards (DGFSCDHG), Ministry of Home Affairs, in coordination with the Indian Army, is undertaking a first-of-its-kind pilot initiative to strengthen Civil Defence preparedness through specialised training of Civil Defence Master Trainers by Indian Army.

In the first phase, a total of 600 Civil Defence Master Trainers, with 50 from each participating State/UT, are proposed to be trained by the second week of November 2026 through a three-day specialised training programme at designated Indian Army training establishments. The participating States/UTs are Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Delhi, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

The initiative seeks to enhance the preparedness of Civil Defence personnel to respond effectively to contemporary security threats, hostile situations and emergencies. The training will cover three broad areas:

  • Threat Awareness: Modern and hybrid warfare, drone awareness and air-raid threats.
  • Protection and Emergency Response: Critical infrastructure protection, fire safety, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) awareness, casualty management, search and rescue.
  • Communication and Coordination: Emergency communication, cyber hygiene, digital resilience, civil-military coordination and incident command.

A key feature of the initiative is its multiplier effect through a structured Master Trainer model. Following the specialised training, each Master Trainer will impart further training to 100 Civil Defence Volunteers in their respective State/UT. This cascading mechanism has the potential to extend specialised preparedness skills to 60,000 Civil Defence Volunteers across the 12 participating States/UTs, thereby significantly expanding the reach and impact of the initiative.

The initiative marks a significant step towards strengthening civil-military coordination and institutional preparedness by combining the Indian Army’s operational expertise with the Civil Defence volunteer network. It will enhance preparedness for emerging threats, coordinated emergency response and critical infrastructure protection. Based on the outcomes of the pilot phase, the initiative is envisaged to be expanded to the remaining States/UTs in a phased manner, furthering the Prime Minister Modi’s vision of a robust, responsive and future-ready Vibrant Civil Defence network.

2327317.title: Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) Establishes Sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE) At IIT (BHU), Varanasi to Advance Next-Generation Telecom Technologies
2327317.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) Establishes Sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE) At IIT (BHU), Varanasi to Advance Next-Generation Telecom Technologies
MoU aims to create a dedicated platform for collaborative research, technology development and capacity building in emerging communication technologies
CoE to focus on 5G Advanced/6G, AI, Quantum Technologies, Cybersecurity and Advanced Wireless Systems
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier telecom R&D centre of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi, a leading institution of national importance, for establishing C-DOT’s sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE). The partnership brings together C-DOT, a market leader in indigenous telecommunications research and development with the academic and research strengths of IIT (BHU), Varanasi, to strengthen India’s telecom innovation ecosystem.

The collaboration between C-DOT and IIT (BHU) is aimed at bridging academic research with real-world technology requirements, creating opportunities for innovation while building a strong pipeline of skilled professionals for the evolving telecommunications sector. It will bring together researchers, faculty, students and technology experts from C-DOT and IIT (BHU) to undertake joint research and promote sustained knowledge exchange. The initiative will strengthen academia and industry to support development of native technologies in areas critical to nation’s digital and communication infrastructure.

CoE will focus in technologies such as Wireless Communications, Quantum Technologies, Cybersecurity and AI-driven Communication Systems. It will undertake advanced research in emerging areas including 5G Advanced/6G Technologies, very large-scale Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, Integrated Sensing and Communication, AI-Native Communication Networks and devices, and Quantum and Post-Quantum Communication Technologies.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Dr. Pankaj Kumar Dalela, EVP, C-DOT, and Professor Amit Patra, Director, IIT (BHU), Varanasi, along with faculty members from IIT (BHU) and senior officials from C-DOT. The signing ceremony was followed by the inauguration of the Centre of Excellence dedicated to advancing communication technologies through collaborative research and innovation.

Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT, highlighted the importance of the collaboration and said, “This Centre of Excellence is more than a research platform, it is an investment in India’s future technology capabilities. The next generation of communications will be shaped by advances in AI, quantum technologies, advanced wireless systems and intelligent networks. Through this CoE, C-DOT and IIT (BHU) are creating a collaborative ecosystem to explore these frontiers and accelerate the development of indigenous technologies for India’s digital future.”

Prof Amit Patra, Director, IIT (BHU), said, “The collaboration with C-DOT will provide a strong platform for translating academic research into impactful technological solutions. It will enable our students and researchers to engage with real-world challenges in telecommunications while contributing to India’s journey towards self-reliance in advanced communication technologies.”

The establishment of the CoE further expands C-DOT’s national network of Centres of Excellence to six, building on its existing collaborations with IIT Kanpur, IIT Gandhinagar, IIT Roorkee, IIT Hyderabad and IISc Bengaluru through FSID. Together, these Centres serve to contribute to the development of future-ready communication technologies, promote knowledge exchange and nurture specialised talent.

2327280.title: Prime Minister  Shri Narendra Modi  inaugurates Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan
2327280.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan
The Chinmaya Mission has spent decades serving communities and sharing India's spiritual wisdom with the world: PM
Chinmaya Mission is not just an institution; it is a profound 'Chinmaya' thought, established by a 'Chinmaya' sage; Its decades-long journey has been brimming with 'Chinmaya' resolves; and that which is 'Chinmaya', is naturally immortal and full of eternal nectar: PM
Our nation is the cradle of our culture; This very nation is the foundation of our existence: PM
Driven by the efforts of the Chinmaya Mission, millions of youth today are serving as India's cultural brand ambassadors; These youth are passing on Indian values to the new generation: PM
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister described his participation as a deeply spiritual experience born of the saints' affection and blessings. Emphasizing that the Chinmaya Mission is not a mere institution but an immortal consciousness founded by a sage and driven by decades of sacred resolutions, he noted the profound aptness of the celebration's title.

Reflecting on how modern technology heightened the emotional resonance of the event through a Holobot interaction with Revered Gurudev Swami Chinmayananda, the Prime Minister shared that the experience transported him 33 years back to his 1993 meeting with the spiritual leader in Vadodara. Recalling Gurudev’s warmth, conversation, and blessings as if standing in his direct presence once more, he expressed heartfelt gratitude to the Mission’s members for creating such a moving tribute."For me, this is a very emotional experience,” remarked PM Modi.

Recounting his February-March 1993 visit to invite Swami Chinmayananda to Chicago for the centenary of the Parliament of the World's Religions,marking 100 years of Swami Vivekananda’s historic address,the Prime Minister noted how Gurudev tirelessly rallied people across America for the event before passing away in San Diego on August 3. Remembering how deeply Gurudev's absence was felt at the Chicago gathering on September 11, he recalled their final conversation, which centered on cultivating youth power."Its main essence was the building of youth power, and building a strong and capable India through youth power!” affirmed Shri Modi.

Tracing his 25-year journey of continuous service as a head of government since becoming the Chief Minister of Gujarat a few years after that meeting, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's youth have remained at the heart of his policies. He lauded the young volunteers of the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav for shouldering major responsibilities and covering 40,000 kilometers over 300 days to engage with over one lakh young citizens."I congratulate the entire team for this wonderful effort as well,” lauded PM Modi.

Invoking the Upanishadic dictum “Vayam Amritasya Putrah” (We are the children of immortality), the Prime Minister explained that India has endured for millennia as a seeker of knowledge and light because its consciousness and wisdom are immortal, which inspired him on the 75th anniversary of Independence to call for an Amrit Mahotsav that serves both as a launchpad for a Viksit Bharat and a revival of India's millennia-old concern for humanity. Noting how numerous spiritual, cultural, and social bodies have since taken sacred pledges at key milestones, he celebrated the Chinmaya Mission’s integration into the nation's Amrit Kaal campaign. "This indeed is the real proof of our being Amritasya Putrah,” asserted Shri Modi.

Citing the Vedic call "Vayam Rashtre Jagriyama Purohitah" to awaken and elevate the nation, the Prime Minister highlighted how Swami Chinmayananda spoke as vocally on national priorities as he did on spirituality, teaching that because the nation is the cradle of our culture and existence, spiritual growth must fuel personal growth and national progress. To instill national self-respect, Swamiji launched the Gita Gyana Yagna to bring the Upanishads, Vedanta, and scriptures to the masses, resulting today in lakhs of Chinmaya Mission youth passing on Indian values as cultural brand ambassadors."This contribution of Revered Gurudev is an important chapter in India's cultural and spiritual renaissance,” affirmed PM Modi.

Recalling the release of a commemorative coin during Gurudev’s birth centenary in 2015, the Prime Minister described Swamiji’s life as a remarkable confluence of Gyana, Karma, and Bhakti that fulfilled his Guru Swami Sivananda’s blessing to “Go, roar like a lion.” He noted that Swamiji's inner conviction left an indelible mark on listeners, while his 'Art of Man Making' radio program guided countless lives."The self-confidence that was in his voice, the inner strength that was there, used to leave an imprint of his thoughts on everyone's heart,” remarked Shri Modi.

Observing that the mission of great personalities endures well beyond their lifetime, the Prime Minister highlighted the expansive education network established by the Chinmaya Mission. He pointed out that over 100 Chinmaya educational institutions are currently shaping the future of lakhs of students across the country."They are getting modern education in these institutions, and they are also imbibing Indian values,” noted PM Modi.

Aligning contemporary governance with the post-independence vision of thinkers like Swami Chinmayananda, the Prime Minister stated that the country is actively fulfilling its duty to modernize academics for a New India. He highlighted the introduction of the National Education Policy, which integrates the Indian knowledge tradition, education in the mother tongue, modern science, and technology. “In this new education policy, importance has been given to all of these,” asserted Shri Modi.

Spotlighting Swamiji’s lifelong dedication to preserving Indian heritage, the Prime Minister recalled how Gurudev stood firmly behind Eknath Ranade’s resolve to build the Vivekananda Rock Memorial in the sea at Kanyakumari and donated the very first financial contribution toward the project. He noted that the monument now serves as a beacon of inspiration for millions globally."Another mission of Swamiji's life was pride in Indian heritage, and its preservation!” observed PM Modi.

Detailing the sweeping cultural renaissance spanning the nation from North to South and East to West, the Prime Minister pointed to the grand revitalization of Kashi Vishwanath Dham, the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya, Ujjain’s Mahakal Mahalok, Kedarnath, and Badrinath, alongside the inclusion of cultural sites on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Contrasting previous eras when stolen Indian antiquities were sold abroad without resistance, he highlighted the repatriation of heritage artifacts over the last dozen years."In the past 12 years, we have also brought back more than six hundred and fifty such ancient idols,” noted Shri Modi.

Drawing a parallel between Swamiji taking Indian philosophy to the world and International Yoga Day uniting the globe with India today, the Prime Minister emphasized that the nation's renewed pride in its heritage and liberation from a colonial mindset prove it is advancing on the path envisioned by ancient sages and patriots. He stressed that their intellectual legacy remains the country's greatest strength on this journey."This self-confidence of pride in our heritage and this assurance of freedom from the mentality of slavery is proof of the fact that the country is now moving forward on that path,” asserted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that while various organizations pursue distinct goals, all paths ultimately converge on the singular destination of national development and glory, the Prime Minister noted that just as Swami Chinmayananda tailored his resolutions to the challenges of his era, today's generation must address modern societal distortions and challenges. He called for proactive efforts to unite society against divisive forces, promote self-reliance, and connect every citizen with the 2047 Viksit Bharat goal."Today, we have to unite society against divisive forces,” asserted Shri Modi.

Pointing out the historic convergence in 2047 when India’s centenary of Independence will coincide with the centenary period of the Chinmaya Mission, the Prime Minister stated that both journeys share identical goals and must advance in tandem. Expressing full faith that the Mission's global family of Acharyas, seekers, and volunteers will leverage Gurudev's legacy and decades of experience to help build a Viksit Bharat,  and offered his final festive greetings."Meaning, the centenary journey of the Chinmaya Mission and the journey of a Viksit Bharat will move forward together,” affirmed PM Modi.

2327274.title: C-DAC and Bank of India Join Hands to Advance Indigenous Quantum Technologies for Banking Applications
2327274.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
C-DAC and Bank of India Join Hands to Advance Indigenous Quantum Technologies for Banking Applications
MoU to Drive Joint Research, Proofs of Concept, Technology Demonstrations and Capacity Building for Future-Ready Banking
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 1:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), an autonomous scientific society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and Bank of India (BOI), signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on quantum financial innovation and the adoption of emerging technologies in banking on 22 October 2026.

The MoU establishes a framework for C-DAC and BOI to explore joint research, development, pilot implementations, technology demonstrations and capacity-building initiatives across technologies of strategic relevance to the banking and financial services sector.

The collaboration brings together C-DAC’s capabilities in High Performance Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Technologies, Blockchain, Cybersecurity and indigenous technology development with Bank of India’s banking domain expertise, nationwide presence and high-volume technology environment.

A key focus of the partnership will be the development of a Quantum Ecosystem for Financial Innovation, aimed at preparing banking systems for the opportunities as well as emerging security challenges associated with quantum technologies. The two organizations will jointly explore quantum-inspired and quantum-safe technologies that can strengthen security, trust, resilience and decision-making in banking.

The collaboration will seek to identify a prioritized portfolio of banking use cases, demonstrate Proofs of Concept in secure sandbox environments, assess technical feasibility and potential banking value, benchmark emerging approaches against existing systems, and develop roadmaps for further development, pilots or adoption.

Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary IAS, MeitY, congratulated Bank of India for its contribution to technological advancement and appreciated its collaboration with C-DAC to foster indigenous innovation. He emphasised the need to build a quantum-resilient financial ecosystem in an era of growing cybersecurity concerns and emerging technological threats, preparing the banking sector for the challenges and opportunities of the quantum era.

Commenting on the MoU, Shri E. Magesh, Director General, C-DAC, said, This collaboration with Bank of India is an important step towards translating India’s indigenous quantum and emerging technology capabilities into practical banking solutions. Through joint research and development and capacity building, C-DAC aims to support a secure, resilient and future-ready financial ecosystem.

Commenting on the collaboration, Shri Rajiv Mishra, Executive Director, BOI, said, “Quantum technologies have the potential to reshape several aspects of banking, from cybersecurity to complex financial decision-making. Through our collaboration with C-DAC, we aim to explore and evaluate these emerging possibilities in a structured manner, while building the knowledge and capabilities required to prepare Bank of India for the next generation of technology”

Beyond quantum technologies, the MoU provides a framework for collaboration in Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technologies relevant to financial services. Potential areas include intelligent document processing, customer and employee assistance, fraud analysis, credit and financial analytics, secure AI platforms, responsible AI, smart contracts, digital identity, secure data sharing and other applications relevant to banking.

The partnership will also focus on developing a future-ready talent ecosystem through training and capacity-building programmes in areas including Quantum Computing, Quantum Security, Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain and other emerging digital technologies.

The MoU was formally exchanged by Shri Aditya Kumar Sinha, Executive Director, C-DAC Mumbai and Shri Satyendra Singh , CGM IT & CIO, Bank of India , in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, IAS, Secretary, MeitY; Shri Rajiv Mishra, Executive Director, Bank of India, Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, Joint Secretary, MeitY, Shri E. Magesh Director General C-DAC, along with other senior officials from MeitY, Bank of India and C-DAC.

Through the collaboration, Bank of India and C-DAC Mumbai aim to create a structured pathway for translating indigenous research and emerging technologies into practical banking applications, while contributing to a secure, resilient and technologically future-ready financial ecosystem.
