2326836.title: 1, 87,305 Candidates Trained and Placed 96,162 During 2020-21 to 2023-24 under PM-DAKSH Scheme
2326836.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
1, 87,305 Candidates Trained and Placed 96,162 During 2020-21 to 2023-24 under PM-DAKSH Scheme
From 2024-25 onwards, PM-DAKSH Merged with PMKVY Scheme of MSDE
Evaluation Study Reports Over 90% of Beneficiaries Found Training Aligned with Career Goals and Local Labour Market Needs
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH), a Central Sector Scheme, was launched during 2020-21 to provide skill training to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), De-notified Tribes (DNTs), and Safai Karamcharis, including Waste Pickers, through empanelled training institutes to encourage self-employment and wage-employment for their socio-economic development.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the scheme was implemented by three Corporations of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), namely, the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

The Official said that from 2024-25 onwards, it was decided to merge PM-DAKSH with the PMKVY Scheme of MSDE. As PM-DAKSH was an additionality to PMKVY and all job roles for providing skill training were taken from the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) portal, which were also covered under PMKVY, PM-DAKSH was subsumed under PMKVY to avoid duplication, she added.

The Official said the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment releases funds to the Corporations, which reimburse training costs to institutes empanelled under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), as per the scheme guidelines and work order.

She said after training completion, institutes are required to provide wage-employment and/or self-employment to at least 70% of trained candidates. If this requirement is not met, the third instalment, amounting to 30% of the training cost, is forfeited. Training institutes are also mandated to maintain collaboration with relevant industries to facilitate employment opportunities for trained candidates. The three Corporations extend loan facilities and assistance to eligible youth from the target group in setting up their projects by providing handholding support, the Official added.

Against the total funds allotted for PM-DAKSH from 2020-21 to 2023-24 amounting to ₹276.47 crore, actual expenditure of ₹309.5 crore had been incurred till date. During 2020-21 to 2023-24, 1,87,305 candidates were trained and 96,162 candidates were placed, the Official said.

The Official further said the evaluation study of the PM-DAKSH Scheme shows strong relevance and learning effectiveness, with over 90% of beneficiaries reporting alignment of training with their career goals and local labour market needs, as well as achievement of intended learning outcomes. Impact results indicate non-material gains such as improved confidence, self-esteem and social recognition, particularly among women and marginalised groups. Sustainability outcomes are largely positive, with most beneficiaries continuing to use the skills acquired, expecting long-term income growth, reinvesting in development and feeling capable of maintaining improvements independently, the Official added.

2326832.title: AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
2326832.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
2326832.body_html:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
Day 2 Highlights State Leadership, Next-Gen Technology, and Blended Finance Mechanisms
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of the AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026 accelerated cross-sectoral engagement across state policy leadership, technological innovation, private sector engagement and climate finance solutions.

A dedicated ministerial track, co-organised by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) and the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), brought together State Ministers of Energy and Agriculture from Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Bihar to present state-level approaches for accelerating agrivoltaic deployment. The session served as a platform for states to showcase investment opportunities, highlighting innovative land-use models, state-level tariff incentives, and adaptation of the PM-KUSUM scheme to local agricultural conditions and crop profiles. Discussions underscored the growing role of sub-national governments in creating enabling environments for agrivoltaic investments.

Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Minister of Energy, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the state’s vast agricultural base, diverse cropping patterns and expanding solar infrastructure as key advantages for agrivoltaics. He emphasised that generating solar power alongside cultivation would optimise land use and create an additional income stream for farmers. Highlighting Uttar Pradesh’s progress in rooftop solar and grid infrastructure, he noted that Green Energy Corridor-III would further strengthen power evacuation for renewable energy projects. He also stressed the need for financing models and technologies suited to small and marginal farmers, who account for nearly 80% of agricultural holdings in the state. Inviting investors to explore these opportunities, he said, “The potential for agrivoltaics is enormous. Those who wish to be associated with agrivoltaics need to look towards Uttar Pradesh.” He also assured investors of the state’s support for grid connectivity and power evacuation.

Shri Surya Pratap Shahi, Minister of Agriculture, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the state’s plan to solarise all 16 lakh agricultural tubewells whose electricity bills have been waived, supported by dedicated grid infrastructure. He emphasised that farmers’ land ownership rights must be protected and called for structured training on crop selection and agrivoltaic practices. He proposed leveraging Krishi Vigyan Kendras, agricultural universities and technical institutions to build farmers’ capacity, while integrating agrivoltaics with agricultural diversification and existing farmer-support initiatives. Highlighting the central role of farmers in the state’s economy, he said, “The agriculture of Uttar Pradesh and its farmers are, in a way, the lifeblood of our economic system.” He also assured farmers that ownership of their land would remain protected.

Shri Rakesh Shukla, Minister of New and Renewable Energy, Madhya Pradesh, highlighted the state’s efforts to advance agrivoltaics, solar deployment and battery storage as part of its farmer-welfare agenda, with 2026 being observed as the Year of Farmer Welfare in Madhya Pradesh. He noted that cultivation beneath solar panels had begun at several locations and that the state was progressing with battery-storage projects, for which the tendering process had been completed. He also highlighted Madhya Pradesh’s wider renewable energy infrastructure, including the Omkareshwar project. Emphasising the state’s progress in agrivoltaics, he said, “In the agricultural sector, we have some plants where farming takes place beneath solar panels. Such projects have begun at a few locations in Madhya Pradesh, and we are continuously progressing in this direction, including in battery storage, for which we have also completed the tendering process.”

Shri Shailesh Kumar Mandal, Minister of Energy, Bihar, highlighted the state’s efforts to strengthen agricultural electricity infrastructure through feeder separation and solarisation. He noted that Bihar had advanced work on approximately 2,700 agricultural feeders, with the state government approving financial support for their solarisation. Emphasising Bihar’s longstanding familiarity with solar energy and its commitment to expanding renewable energy access, he said, “Solar energy and sunlight are not new concepts in Bihar; this tradition has existed there for centuries.” He reiterated the state government’s commitment to taking forward agricultural feeder solarisation through an innovative approach.

Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha, Minister of Agriculture, Bihar, highlighted agrivoltaics as an opportunity to enhance farmers’ incomes, promote crop diversification and generate rural employment. He emphasised the need to strengthen research, farmer awareness and training through collaboration among agricultural institutions, financial institutions and energy enterprises. He also highlighted Bihar’s contribution to the country’s workforce as an opportunity to support wider adoption and implementation of agrivoltaics. He said, “A large pool of workers comes from Bihar and contributes to the workforce across the country. Many states rely on this workforce from Bihar.”

Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Deputy Chief Minister, Odisha, announced that the state is finalising its dedicated Agrivoltaics Policy 2026, with a target of 1 GW by 2030. The proposed policy will require at least 90% of project sites to remain cultivable, safeguard farmer consent and crop insurance, and allow farmers to own projects or lease their land while continuing cultivation. To attract investment, Odisha plans to provide 25-year power purchase agreements through GRIDCO, grid connectivity and investment incentives. Highlighting the policy’s importance for investors, he said, “It gives investors certainty: 25 years of PPA with GRIDCO, an offtake guarantee, grid connectivity and the freedom of open access and competitive use.” He also announced that Odisha is finalising its dedicated Agrivoltaics Policy 2026, positioning the state to establish a policy framework specifically for agrivoltaics.

 The Agrivoltaics Pitch-Hub was curated by the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) where early-stage innovators and start-ups pitched bankable, dual-use agrivoltaic solutions before an expert jury comprising national institutes (NISE, NIBE), venture capitalists, and industry leaders.

Fraunhofer ISE and Sunseed APV demonstrated next-generation solutions, including advanced solar tracking systems, dynamic panel tilting, semi-transparent photovoltaic (PV) modules, and micro-climate soil sensors engineered specifically for tropical and arid conditions.

Hosted by the Indo-German Chamber of Commerce, the dialogue brought together Indian and international developers, including NTPC Green Energy, First Solar, and leading European firms to discuss supply chain localisation, standards development, and market certainty.

An executive roundtable convened representatives from multilateral development banks, financial institutions, and commercial lenders, including the World Bank, KfW, European Investment Bank, and IREDA.

Participants examined financial mechanisms needed to accelerate agrivoltaic deployment, including risk-mitigation instruments, concessional lending facilities, and blended finance structures capable of mobilising private investment at scale.

Bringing a vital youth perspective to the global stage, acclaimed actress and UNDP India Youth Champion Sanjana Sanghi joined the Conference for an exclusive fireside chat. Sanghi advocated for youth-led community strategies and spotlighted the intersection of food security, renewable energy, and youth mobilisation. She emphasised how agrivoltaics contributes to multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while directly empowering and securing livelihoods for rural youth.

The day concluded with an interactive Digital Poster Gallery, showcasing operational agrivoltaic projects and lessons from global case studies, providing participants with practical insights into implementation and scale-up strategies.

2326831.title: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Invites Polish Firms to ‘Build, Innovate and Grow with India’
2326831.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2326831.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Invites Polish Firms to ‘Build, Innovate and Grow with India’
Sonowal proposes Startup Bridge, Innovation Corridor & AI-Quantum Dialogue to link India and Poland
At “India-Poland Business Forum” with PM Donald Tusk, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal offers “India's Scale, Skills & Trust for Joint Growth”
Sonowal pitches India's growth story to Polish business leaders calls for “trusted supply chains”
Let us invest, innovate and develop together: Sonowal at India-Poland Business Forum
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal urged Polish companies to “build, innovate and invest in India” rather than only sell to it, as he pitched the country's growth story to business leaders from both nations.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal delivered the keynote address at the India-Poland Business Forum here today which was also attended by Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Sonowal recalled that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Poland in August 2024 lifted ties to a strategic partnership.

“When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Poland in August 2024, he and Prime Minister Tusk elevated our relations to a Strategic Partnership. They did so with a clear conviction: the India-Poland relationship must not only be strong in diplomacy; it must also be strong in business, technology, investment and innovation,” said Sarbananda Sonowal. The aim now, he said, is for the relationship to be as strong in business, technology, investment and innovation as it is in diplomacy.

"India offers the scale of a large and growing market, the skills of a young and talented workforce, and the trust of a democracy committed to reform, enterprise and openness," Sonowal said.

Sonowal argued that the two economies fit together. Poland, he said, has strengths in engineering, machinery, mining technologies, transport, environmental solutions and advanced manufacturing. India has the market, talent and manufacturing base to give those capabilities scale. "My message to Polish companies is: do not only sell to India. Build in India. Develop solutions in India. Find Indian partners. And, use India as a platform for growth," Sonowal said.

Sonowal cited that India, under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has set an ambitious target to generate 500 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030, to put forth a strong Climate Action step by the country. He put the investment needed at roughly 280 billion to 300 billion euros, with openings for equipment makers, storage, power grids, green hydrogen, recycling and environmental technology. Poland's experience in mining, critical minerals and clean energy could help, Sonowal said.

On technology, Sonowal noted that Indian IT companies have made Poland a base for their European operations and employ about 10,000 people there. He said the next step should go beyond IT services, into artificial intelligence, quantum computing, 5G applications, digital infrastructure, smart manufacturing and space.

The Union Minister proposed a Startup Bridge, an Innovation Corridor and an AI and Quantum Dialogue to link businesses, researchers and innovators in both countries. Trade between the two countries has reached $6.36 billion, and Indian investment in Poland exceeds $3 billion, Sonowal said. Polish companies are also active in India in packaging, manufacturing, waste-to-energy and electric mobility. He said the ambition should be larger than doubling trade by 2030.

"We should create together. We should innovate together. We should invest together. We should build trusted supply chains together. And we should succeed together," Sonowal said.

He urged business leaders to see the India-EU free trade agreement as more than a trade pact. "View it as a partnership multiplier," he said. It opens a larger window into the Indian market for Polish firms, he said, and widens European opportunities for Indian ones.

Sonowal concluded by describing India’s philosophy of “Power to Empower”, stating that beyond the power to compete lies the power to collaborate. “India’s growth can create opportunities for Poland. Poland’s capabilities can add strength to India. And together, our businesses can create solutions for the world,” he said.

2326828.title: CAQM Reviews Air Pollution Control Measures in Punjab and Haryana, Calls for Prompt Ground-Level Action
2326828.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2326828.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM Reviews Air Pollution Control Measures in Punjab and Haryana, Calls for Prompt Ground-Level Action
Focus on prevention of Paddy Stubble Burning, effective utilization of CRM Machinery, stronger Enforcement and control of other key Pollution Sources
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, held separate review meetings with the Governments of Punjab and Haryana in Chandigarh today to review the measures being undertaken for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning and abatement of other key sources of air pollution, calling for prompt action(s) on the ground.

The meeting with the Government of Punjab focused on implementation of the State Action Plan for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning in accordance with CAQM Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026. The Commission reviewed on-ground enforcement measures, District-level preparedness and monitoring mechanisms in place for effective paddy stubble management.

The availability, deployment and effective utilization of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery at the District and farmer levels were reviewed, along with the identification of gaps in machinery utilization and arrangements for the collection, transportation and utilization of paddy straw through in-situ and ex-situ management. The Commission emphasized the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure effective utilization of available machinery during the peak harvesting period.

The meeting also covered field validation of burnt-area assessment through satellite-based fire alerts, along with District-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring stubble-burning incidents. Compliance with CAQM Direction No. 92, mandating the use of paddy straw-based biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns, and progress towards prescribed targets for biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also reviewed.

The meeting with the Government of Haryana covered a broader range of air pollution sources, including paddy stubble burning, abatement of vehicular pollution, dust from roads and open areas, dust from construction and demolition (C&D) activities and industrial pollution, along with other identified sectoral measures.

With regard to paddy stubble burning, the Commission reviewed implementation of the State Action Plan, including on-ground enforcement, deployment and utilization of CRM machinery, crop-residue supply-chain management, field validation of burnt-area assessment and the use of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring burning incidents. Compliance with Direction No. 92 regarding biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns and progress on biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also taken up.

The review of vehicular pollution covered installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system at fuel and CNG stations for enforcement of requirements relating to valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs), action against end-of-life vehicles, adoption of cleaner mobility measures and progress towards phasing out diesel-operated auto rickshaws in NCR Districts.

Measures for dust mitigation from roads and open areas, including road-dust control and mechanized road sweeping, were also reviewed. The Commission further examined measures for controlling dust emissions from C&D activities and implementation of prescribed dust-mitigation measures. The review also covered industrial pollution control, including compliance with applicable norms and monitoring and enforcement measures relating to industrial units and other identified sources.

The Commission emphasized the need for time-bound implementation of State Action Plans, its enforcement and continuous field-level monitoring, supported by close coordination among the concerned State Departments, District Administrations and enforcement agencies. The States were advised to address implementation gaps on priority and ensure timely corrective action across the respective sectors. The Commission emphasized on greater facilitation of farmers with in-situ crop residue management machinery and strengthened ex-situ mechanism. State Governments of Haryana and Punjab were also advised to implement IEC Action Plans on-ground more effectively.

The Commission emphasized that paddy stubble management should be pursued not merely as a measure to prevent burning, but as an opportunity to improve the well-being of citizens while fostering a robust industrial ecosystem of a circular economy, with greater utilization of paddy straw as a resource. The Commission called for prompt action at the ground level and further cautioned the District Administrations that any laxity that leads to rise in stubble-burning incidents shall be viewed seriously.

CAQM reiterated that sustained and coordinated efforts by the State Governments and all concerned agencies are essential for effective prevention of paddy stubble burning and comprehensive abatement of air pollution, particularly during the critical winter period.

2326787.title: At CII conference, Union Environment Minister calls for coordinated efforts by Government, Industry and Urban Local Bodies to advance India’s Circular Economy
2326787.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2326787.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
At CII conference, Union Environment Minister calls for coordinated efforts by Government, Industry and Urban Local Bodies to advance India’s Circular Economy
Government translating Policy Intent into Meaningful Action through Clear Policies and Regulatory Reforms: Shri Bhupender Yadav 
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today addressed the Circular Economy Conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in New Delhi. He highlighted India’s efforts to translate policy intent into meaningful action through clear policies, regulatory reforms, digital compliance systems and a whole-of-government approach to advance the circular economy.

Addressed the @FollowCII Circular Economy Conference in Delhi today. Elaborated on how India under the leadership of Hon'ble PM Shri @narendramodi ji has adopted a 'whole of government' approach in creating an enabling platform for all stakeholders to push circular economy. With clear policy, directions like Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 and EPR framewor, the focus now is on translating policy intent into meaningful action. Happy to note that as of October 12, 2026, more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers are registered under various EPR frameworks. Through these collective efforts, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with over 435.043 lakh metric tonnes covered through EPR certificate generation.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) October 22, 2026

In his address, Shri Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Union Government had progressively strengthened the legal framework governing waste management by introducing sector-specific rules for nine waste streams: plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, waste tyres, used oil, end-of-life vehicles, construction and demolition waste, non-ferrous scrap metal and solid waste. These rules focused on waste prevention, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing and resource recovery across the product lifecycle. The Minister also highlighted that as on date, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers registered under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks.  

Highlighting the role of EPR, the Minister said that the framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to ensure environmentally sound management of products at the end of their life. The transfer of EPR certificates provided financial incentives to recyclers, encouraging capacity expansion, technological advancement and increased recycling, while contributing to job creation and livelihoods across the recycling value chain. Shri Yadav emphasised that regulation alone could not create a circular economy and highlighted the importance of Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative, which calls for mindful and deliberate resource utilisation instead of destructive consumption. 

On Industry concerns regarding digital compliance, EPR market operations and transaction timelines, Shri Yadav invited stakeholders to continue sharing practical problems and suggestions. He said the Government is working on a market-based approach and urged industry representatives to engage openly to resolve outstanding issues. On plastic waste management, the Minister called for greater coordination between producers and recyclers to address concerns over the availability of recyclable material and recycling capacity. He said the objective went beyond issuing certificates to creating jobs, strengthening local industry capacity, promoting knowledge-sharing and advancing technology.

While talking about Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, Shri Yadav stressed the need for technology adoption, capacity building, online monitoring, stronger accountability and financial sustainability of urban local bodies. The Minister also highlighted the importance of four-stream segregation of solid waste – wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste – and public participation. Shri Yadav concluded by emphasising that effective implementation of the SWM Rules would help control legacy waste and strengthen urban systems. He called for coordinated efforts by the government, industry and urban local bodies to advance the circular economy. He further called for stronger recovery of critical minerals from e-waste and batteries, and greater industry participation in developing secondary raw-material markets and strengthening supply-chain traceability.

IT IS OUR COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY TO RESPECT FOOD, ACKNOWLEDGE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF OUR FARMERS, AND PROTECT OUR NATURAL RESOURCES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced ‘Seva Samman Parv’ and ‘Yuva Prabodhan’ on the occasion of the Nuakhai festival in Raipur, Chhattisgarh today (October 22, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Nuakhai Milan Samaroh is not merely a cultural celebration; it is a tribute to our rich traditions, social harmony and unity. Such occasions provide us with an opportunity to reconnect with our roots, take pride in our cultural heritage, and pass on the life values to future generations.

The President stated that the Nuakhai festival is a celebration of our agricultural traditions, an expression of gratitude toward nature and a testament to the spirit of community. This festival reminds us that food is not just a means to satisfy hunger; it is a symbol of the hard work of our farmers, the generosity of Mother Earth and the invaluable gifts of nature. She underlined that it is our collective responsibility to respect food, acknowledge the contributions of our farmers, and protect our natural resources.

 Addressing the youth present in large numbers, the President said that circumstances may vary, and challenges may differ; yet, youth should possess a deep-seated drive to innovate, to create something better, and to establish their own unique identity. She said that when they align their individual endeavours with collective and national goals, they pave the way for the nation’s progress. She advised them to dream big, broaden their horizons, uphold the highest standards of conduct, and place service to society and the nation at the centre of their endeavours. She encouraged the youth to pursue every endeavour with honesty, integrity and sensitivity. She emphasised that nation-building is not accomplished through major decisions alone, but also through the small, sincere efforts of millions of citizens. She urged them to combine knowledge with humility, ambition with ethical values, and success with a spirit of service, highlighting that these qualities would strengthen their contribution to the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

The President was happy to note the participation of a large number of women in the Nuakhai Milan Samaroh. She said that the nation is moving forward with the goal of a Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. To achieve this goal, the equal participation of women is absolutely essential. She urged all women to participate actively in the affairs of the nation and society. She said that when they progress, the benefits will extend not only to them or their family but to the entire society and the nation. She urged men, especially the youth, to provide an environment for their sisters and daughters in which they can realize their dreams without any barriers. She said that respect for women should not merely be expressed in words; it must be reflected in their behaviour, mindset, and daily conduct.

The President was happy to note that through the efforts of the central and state governments, combined with their own strength of will, the youth of Chhattisgarh have moved away from the path of Naxalism and joined the mainstream. The light of development is now replacing the darkness of terror. She said that this transformation is leading to the well-being of the young people and their families while accelerating the development of the state and the country.

2326711.title: Indian Railways Sets All-Time High Coal Loading Record in October 2026 (Till 18th)
2326711.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Sets All-Time High Coal Loading Record in October 2026 (Till 18th)
87 More Coal Rakes Dispatched per Day Compared with October 2025
430 Coal Rakes Dispatched Daily to Thermal Power Plants in First Half of FY 2026-27, Registering 7.1% Growth Over the Corresponding Period Last Year
Indian Railways Coordinating with Ministries of Coal and Power to Ensure Reliable Coal Supply to Meet the Country’s Energy Requirements
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has achieved an all-time record in coal loading, registering a 22.5% growth in October 2026 up to 18th October compared with the corresponding period last year. Coal loading during this period increased by 87 rakes per day over October 2025, reflecting the continued efforts to ensure reliable coal supplies to thermal power plants across the country.

During the first half (H1) of FY 2026-27, Indian Railways dispatched an average of 430 coal rakes per day to thermal power plants, registering a 7.1% increase over the corresponding period last year. The momentum continued in September 2026, when coal rake dispatches increased by 14% per day compared with September 2025.

The sustained pace of coal transportation comes amid rising energy consumption and increased demand for coal-based power generation due to higher industrial production and deficient rainfall in some parts of the country.

Consistent coal evacuation has helped maintain steady coal stocks at thermal power plants, supporting reliable power generation across the country. Indian Railways is working in close coordination with the Ministry of Coal to ensure efficient coal evacuation. It is also coordinating with the Ministry of Power to sustain coal transportation and supply, helping maintain adequate coal stocks at thermal power plants and meet the country’s energy requirements.

2326662.title: FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON ARRIVES IN MALDIVES
2326662.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON ARRIVES IN MALDIVES
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:57PM by PIB Delhi

Ships of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS) – INS Tir, INS Sujata and Indian Coast Guard Ship Sarathi – arrived off Malé, Maldives, on 21 Oct 2026 as part of the Squadron’s Long Range Training Deployment. The Squadron received a warm welcome from the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF), reflecting the strong maritime partnership and close regional ties between the two nations.

During the port call, the Senior Officer, First Training Squadron, called on the Chief of Defence Force, MNDF, and the Commandant, MNDF Coast Guard. Discussions focused on sustained engagement and multifaceted maritime collaboration between the Indian Navy and MNDF. The Senior Officer 1TS also called on Shri G Balasubramaniam, High Commissioner of India to the Maldives. As part of the training exchanges, trainees of 1TS visited the Girifushi Training Centre.

Cross-deck visits, sports fixtures, social interactions and outreach activities are also planned during the visit to foster camaraderie and mutual understanding between the two forces.

The ongoing visit reaffirms enhanced interoperability between the Indian Navy and MNDF, and underscores the growing maritime cooperation between the two nations, in line with the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

2326655.title: Secretary, DARPG Reviews Implementation of Special Campaign 6 at Field Offices of Railways and Finance Ministries in Mumbai
2326655.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2326655.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Secretary, DARPG Reviews Implementation of Special Campaign 6 at Field Offices of Railways and Finance Ministries in Mumbai
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi

 Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, visited field offices of the Ministry of Railways and the Ministry of Finance in Mumbai on 22 October 2026 to review the implementation of the ongoing Special Campaign 6. The visits focused on assessing progress in cleanliness, space management, disposal of obsolete records and materials, and initiatives aimed at promoting efficient and sustainable workplace management.

As part of the visit to the field office of the Ministry of Railways, the Secretary visited Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), where she reviewed passenger amenities and initiatives undertaken to enhance passenger convenience. As part of the initiative under Special Campaign 6, she participated in Rail Jan Samvad in which she interacted with commuters and reviewed facilities and arrangements at the station, the main line platforms, ticketing facilities and the heritage building. The visit provided an opportunity to assess initiatives undertaken at the field level to improve public-facing services and maintain clean, organised and passenger-friendly railway premises. Additional Secretary, DARPG Shri Puneet Yadav, Shri Rajeev Srivastava, GM, Central Railways and other senior officers of Ministry of Railways were present during the event.

Subsequently, the Secretary visited the State Bank Bhavan, Corporate Centre, Mumbai, where she held a meeting with the top management of the State Bank of India (SBI). A presentation on Special Campaign 6 was made by the Bank Officials, highlighting initiatives and progress under the campaign. As part of the Campaign, the Secretary and the Chairperson of the SBI Shri CS Setty launched an e-book on Cyber Fraud Awareness, an initiative aimed at promoting awareness about cyber fraud and encouraging safe digital practices.

During the visit, the Secretary also viewed ‘Punarnava’, the e-waste-to-art sculpture installed at the entrance of State Bank Bhavan. The installation reflects the potential of repurposing discarded electronic materials through creative reuse which is one of the objectives of the Special Campaign. She also visited the SBI Auditorium, which has been renovated as part of the Special Campaign 6, reflecting the campaign’s focus on the optimal utilisation of existing office spaces and the transformation of underutilised infrastructure into functional facilities.

The Special Campaign 6 underscores the importance of institutionalising cleanliness, clearing obsolete records and materials, reclaiming underutilised office space, and ensuring the scientific disposal and recycling of waste, including electronic waste. The campaign promotes a culture of efficiency, environmental responsibility and sustainable resource management across government offices and public institutions.

The visits reaffirmed the importance of translating the objectives of Special Campaign 6 into tangible outcomes at the field level through regular monitoring, effective implementation and the adoption of sustainable workplace practices.

2326657.title: NHAI Strengthens Air Pollution Control Measures Across Delhi-NCR through Intensified Dust-Control Measures and Faster Decongestion of National Highways
2326657.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Strengthens Air Pollution Control Measures Across Delhi-NCR through Intensified Dust-Control Measures and Faster Decongestion of National Highways
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi

To strengthen air pollution control across National Highways and Expressways in Delhi-NCR ahead of the winter season, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has deployed around 60 water sprinklers and tankers, 14 anti-smog guns, 23 Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs), two tractor-mounted broomers and over 900 workers to support dust mitigation efforts. In addition, 13 MRSMs are operating across 157 km of National Highway stretches within Delhi NCR.

Shri Alok Deepankar, Member (Technical), NHAI, reviewed the pollution-control measures and directed field teams to ensure full deployment of equipment, manpower and water sprinkling, regular operation of anti-smog guns and daily mechanical sweeping. He also emphasised strict compliance with norms established by Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) in Delhi-NCR, which includes covering of construction materials, maintenance of dust-free road surfaces and intensified measures as per applicable GRAP stages. NHAI officials have been directed to monitor activities daily and submit progress reports with geo-tagged photographs.

As part of its environmental initiatives, NHAI has planted around 9.80 lakh plants in NCR during FY 2025-26 against a target of 9.52 lakh, achieving survival rates of over 90 percent. Further, around 13.58 lakh tonnes of inert material from Delhi's landfill sites have been utilised in the embankment construction of UER-II and DND–Sohna corridors, supporting sustainable waste utilisation.

The review also covered major decongestion projects including UER-II, Dwarka Expressway, DND–Sohna Expressway and Delhi–Dehradun Expressway, which are helping to reduce traffic congestion and vehicular emission in Delhi-NCR. Expeditious progress of proposed decongestion projects and prompt resolution of public complaints received through the Green Delhi app and Social Media platforms were also emphasised.

NHAI remains committed to reducing dust pollution, improving air quality and facilitating smoother traffic movement across Delhi-NCR in the winter season.

2326653.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Department of Rural Development Organises One-Day Health Check-up Camp under Special Campaign 6.0
More than 250 staff, including Safai Karamcharis, attend the camp for health check-up at Kartavya Bhavan
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, organised a One-Day Health Check-up Camp at Kartavya Bhavan, New Delhi, on 22 October 2026, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. More than 250 staff of the Department, including Safai Karamcharis, attended the camp for their health check-up.

The camp was organised as part of the series of activities being conducted by the Department under Special Campaign 6.0, which is being observed from 2 October to 31 October 2026. The camp mainly focused on outsourced staff, including Safai Karamcharis. The initiative aimed to promote health awareness and preventive healthcare, and to encourage regular health check-ups among employees.

The following health services were provided at the camp:

  • Blood Pressure Monitoring

  • Random Blood Sugar (RBS) Testing

  • General Eye Check-up

  • General ENT Examination

  • General Physician Consultation

During the campaign period, the Department is organising several activities focusing on cleanliness, disposal of pending matters, redressal of public grievances, better management of physical and digital records, and promoting Swachhata as a regular workplace practice.

The Department remains committed to the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0 by promoting a clean, efficient and people-centric workplace while supporting the well-being of its employees.

2326649.title: As A Follow-Up to The Departmental Summit on Water 2026, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organised Virtual Conference on Convergence of JJM 2.0 With 16th Finance Grants for Rural water Supply and Strengthening of O&M Systems
2326649.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
As A Follow-Up to The Departmental Summit on Water 2026, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organised Virtual Conference on Convergence of JJM 2.0 With 16th Finance Grants for Rural water Supply and Strengthening of O&M Systems
Secretary, DDWS calls for stronger Panchayat-led planning, interdepartmental coordination and sustainable financing of rural water supply infrastructure
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, today organised the fourth virtual conference with States and Union Territories as part of a series of thematic consultations being held in follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water 2026 held on 1-2 September 2026. The conference focused on strengthening convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and 16th Finance Commission to advance source sustainability, water security and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery.

The virtual conference brought together senior officials from State PHEDs/Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Departments and representatives from the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India and National Informatics Centre. States rural water supply departments including Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh shared best practices and field experiences on leveraging Finance Commission grants for strengthening rural water supply systems, improving O&M arrangements, enhancing community participation and strengthening local governance mechanisms.

Addressing in the conference, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, stated that with the extension of JJM 2.0, the focus now shifts from infrastructure creation to ensuring functionality, sustainability and quality service delivery. He emphasised that the true measure of success lies not merely in asset creation but in ensuring that rural households continue to receive reliable and safe drinking water through well-maintained and financially sustainable systems.

Shri Meena underlined the pivotal role of Gram Panchayats in rural water governance and noted that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment places drinking water and sanitation among the key responsibilities of local self-governments. He stressed that Gram Panchayats must take leadership in preparing comprehensive annual O&M plans, mobilising local resources, managing service delivery and ensuring accountability for water supply infrastructure created under JJM and other programmes.

Referring to the 16th Finance Commission framework, he highlighted that tied grants provide a significant opportunity to strengthen the sustainability of drinking water and sanitation services at the grassroots level. He noted that of the total Rural Local Body (RLB) grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, a substantial share has been earmarked for water and sanitation-related activities. He emphasised that these grants should be utilised primarily for operation and maintenance, source sustainability, water quality management, service delivery improvements and strengthening local institutional capacity rather than creation of new infrastructure where existing assets require maintenance and support.

The Secretary focused on three key pillars of sustainable financing for rural water supply systems such as effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, ii. convergence with other available programmes and iii. schemes, and progressive strengthening of user-charge collection mechanisms.

Referring to successful examples from several States, he encouraged States and Gram Panchayats to adopt sustainable revenue models that support recurring O&M expenditure and reduce dependence on a single funding source. He also stressed the growing role of Gram Panchayats in the management of sanitation and solid waste systems and highlighted the need for local bodies to plan comprehensively for both drinking water and sanitation services. He noted that adequate provisions must be made for repairs, leak management, pump maintenance, chlorination, water-quality surveillance, electricity expenditure and staffing arrangements required for uninterrupted service delivery.

Emphasising capacity building as a critical requirement, Shri Meena called upon States to utilise resources available under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) and other programmes for training Panchayat representatives and local functionaries. He urged States to translate and disseminate Operation and Maintenance Manuals in local languages and ensure that Panchayats clearly understand the permissible activities, funding mechanisms and reporting requirements under the Finance Commission framework.

He called upon to strengthen coordination between Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural Development Departments at the State, district and Gram Panchayat levels. He noted that the simultaneous implementation of JJM 2.0, VB-G RAM G, and the 16th Finance Commission cycle provides a unique opportunity to institutionalise sustainable water governance through integrated planning and coordinated implementation.

Ms. Kritika Kulhari, Deputy Secretary, NJJM made a detailed presentation on the 16th Finance Commission Grants and utilisation of tied grants for water and sanitation, outlining the grant structure, release conditions, reporting requirements, permissible activities and planning framework. Participants were informed that the total Rural Local Body allocation under the 16th Finance Commission exceeds ₹4.35 lakh crore, with nearly ₹1.74 lakh crore earmarked for water management and sanitation over the award period. The presentation highlighted that priority should be accorded to operation and maintenance of existing assets, lifecycle-based planning, preventive maintenance, community ownership and digital accountability through prescribed platforms.

Shri Vipul Ujwal, Director, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, made a detailed presentation on GPDP planning, release modalities and utilisation of Finance Commission Grants for rural water supply O&M. He emphasised that sustainable service delivery requires integration of three critical elements - Requirements, Resources and Responsibilities (RRR). He explained how Gram Panchayats should identify service gaps, estimate annual O&M requirements, assess available financial resources and integrate these priorities into the Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP). He further highlighted the growing importance of Own Source Revenue (OSR), user-charge collection and performance-based grants in strengthening Panchayat finances and ensuring sustainable service delivery.

The conference also featured a technical presentation by NIC, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, on the eGramSwaraj portal and its reporting modules. The session explained how Gram Panchayats can integrate planning, implementation, geo-tagging, expenditure reporting, asset management and monitoring through the digital platform. The presentation highlighted the integration of eGramSwaraj with the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and various departmental databases, enabling improved transparency, accountability and real-time monitoring of Finance Commission-funded activities.

During the State experience-sharing session, Karnataka presented its integrated approach to rural water supply management through innovations such as Jala Sankalana, JalaAasthi and Jeevajala, which combine GIS-based asset management, real-time monitoring, community participation and evidence-based O&M planning. The State highlighted its experience in water budgeting, volumetric tariff collection, preventive maintenance and strengthening community ownership of drinking water systems. Further the state shared its experience of institutional convergence under the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj framework, where Rural Water Supply, Panchayati Raj and Rural Development functions operate in close coordination and highlighted how this integrated administrative structure has enabled better planning and utilisation of Finance Commission grants, strengthened Gram Panchayat participation in operation and maintenance planning, water budgeting and tariff collection, and improved coordination between technical departments and local self-governments. Karnataka emphasised that sustained community engagement, clear delineation of responsibilities and convergence of financial resources have been central to strengthening the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water services.

Odisha shared its institutional model built around close convergence among Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and Drinking Water departments. The State presented its integrated O&M framework, bottom-up budgeting process, digital monitoring systems, local mechanic training programmes and technology-driven interventions such as solarisation, automation and IoT-based monitoring systems aimed at ensuring long-term sustainability of drinking water services. The State highlighted how coordinated planning, bottom-up budgeting and convergence of Finance Commission grants, State resources and community contributions have helped strengthen operation and maintenance systems. Odisha also underscored the importance of Gram Panchayat participation, local capacity building, digital monitoring and clearly defined accountability mechanisms in ensuring reliable service delivery and sustainable management of rural water supply infrastructure.

Madhya Pradesh highlighted its recently notified O&M Rules, 2026, which enable Gram Panchayats to utilise multiple funding streams for water supply and sanitation activities. The State showcased simplified procurement processes, district-level WASH technical committees, structured training programmes, digital systems for user-charge collection and extensive efforts to build technical capacity among Panchayat representatives and engineers. The State highlighted how multiple funding streams, including Finance Commission grants, State grants, user charges and other local resources, are being brought together to support sustainable operation and maintenance.

In his concluding remarks, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM reiterated that Finance Commission grants should be viewed as an opportunity to institutionalise sustainable rural water governance and strengthen Panchayat ownership of water supply systems. He urged States to complete pending compliance requirements, strengthen GPDP-based planning, improve user-charge collection mechanisms, and ensure effective utilisation of both 15th and 16th Finance Commission grants for sustaining rural water supply infrastructure.

Shri Soan also called upon States to organise intensive training and capacity-building programmes for Panchayat representatives, Panchayat Secretaries, Sarpanches and technical personnel over the coming months and ensure timely resolution of eGramSwaraj login and reporting issues. He informed participants that two regional conferences are planned in November 2026 to review preparedness, address implementation challenges and strengthen convergence among departments responsible for drinking water, sanitation, Panchayati Raj and Rural Development.

The conference concluded with a shared commitment by the Centre and States/UTs to strengthen Panchayat-led planning, improve financial sustainability, enhance interdepartmental convergence and ensure that the substantial investments made under Jal Jeevan Mission translate into reliable, continuous and sustainable drinking water and sanitation services for rural households across the country.

2326639.title: World Entering an Era of AI-Guided, Gene-Driven Precision Medicine; India Emerging Among Frontline Providers: Dr. Jitendra Singh at SRIHER Convocation, Chennai
2326639.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
World Entering an Era of AI-Guided, Gene-Driven Precision Medicine; India Emerging Among Frontline Providers: Dr. Jitendra Singh at SRIHER Convocation, Chennai
Young Doctors Will Have the Privilege of Using Enabling Technologies, along with the Challenge of Integrating Them Optimally with Clinical Practice: Dr. Jitendra Singh
India’s Advances in Indigenous Vaccines, Gene Therapy and Medical Research Reflect Growing Healthcare Capabilities, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Rising Lifestyle Diseases Among Young People Make Prevention a Critical Healthcare Priority: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Invites Sri Ramachandra Institute to Expand Collaboration in Genomics, Biomanufacturing and Nuclear Medicine
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh, who is also a Professor of Medicine and Diabetes, today said that the world is entering an era of AI-guided, gene-driven precision medicine, with India emerging among the front-line providers of advanced healthcare solutions.

Addressing the 42nd Convocation, as chief guest, before awarding Medical degrees at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (SRIHER), Chennai, he said the next generation of medical professionals would have the privilege of using enabling technologies while facing the challenge of integrating them optimally with clinical practice. He stressed that the future of medicine would depend on combining technological advances with sound clinical judgement, while strengthening preventive healthcare to address the growing incidence of lifestyle diseases among younger people.

The Minister addressed the graduating students, faculty members and other dignitaries in the presence of Chancellor V. R. Venkatachalam, Pro-Chancellor R. V. Singhrutawarand other senior members of the institution. Congratulating undergraduate, postgraduate and super-specialty graduates, as well as gold medallists, Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed satisfaction at the institution’s growth and its contribution to medical education and research. He also conveyed his wishes for the speedy recovery of Vice-Chancellor Dr. Uma, who was unable to attend.

Drawing on his experience as a clinician spanning nearly four decades, Dr. Jitendra Singh traced the transformation of medical practice, from an earlier focus on communicable diseases to the growing burden of lifestyle-related disorders such as diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. He said that both communicable and non-communicable diseases continue to challenge healthcare systems, even as increasing life expectancy brings new medical demands. The emergence of chronic conditions at younger ages makes prevention, early intervention and long-term disease management increasingly important.

The Minister said that Diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, once more commonly associated with older age groups, are increasingly affecting younger people. A person developing diabetes at the age of 30 may have to live with its consequences for several decades, he said, making the protection of vital organs and prevention of complications essential responsibilities for doctors, families and patients. He stressed that preventing long-term disorders among young people is critical to protecting India's human potential and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Referring to the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, genomics and other frontier technologies, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that tomorrow’s medical professionals would practise in an environment increasingly shaped by AI-assisted healthcare and gene-driven precision medicine. He said these technologies would open new possibilities for diagnosis, treatment and personalised care, while placing a corresponding responsibility on doctors to integrate them effectively into clinical practice. The challenge, he said, would be to make optimal use of emerging technologies while preserving the clinical orientation and judgement essential to patient care.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India has made significant progress in indigenous medical research and is increasingly contributing to global healthcare innovation. Referring to India's development of an indigenous DNA vaccine against COVID-19, he spoke about the country's growing capabilities in vaccine research, including ongoing work on diseases such as dengue and malaria. He also referred to advances in gene therapy for haemophilia, demonstrating how Indian research institutions are contributing to the development of solutions for complex medical conditions.

The Minister also referred to indigenous drug development, including nafithromycin for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, and advances in nuclear medicine research involving conditions such as acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and fatty liver disease. These developments, he said, reflect the expanding capacity of India's scientific and medical institutions to pursue new therapeutic approaches and strengthen the country's contribution to healthcare research.

Emphasising the importance of translating scientific advances into clinical outcomes, Dr. Jitendra Singh invited SRIHER to expand its engagement with national research initiatives in emerging fields such as genomics, biomanufacturing and nuclear medicine. He said collaboration between government research institutions, universities, hospitals and industry can help combine scientific expertise with clinical experience, accelerate innovation and facilitate the development of effective and affordable healthcare solutions.

The Minister referred to the growing opportunities for research and innovation in advanced scientific fields, including nuclear medicine, and encouraged the institution to build on its research capabilities, clinical expertise and startup ecosystem. He said closer collaboration between researchers, medical professionals and technology developers would be important in advancing new therapies, medical technologies and precision healthcare.

Speaking about the potential of genomics, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that integrating genomic information with clinical outcomes could help doctors increasingly tailor treatment to individual patients, taking into account their genetic profiles, lifestyles and environmental factors. As precision medicine advances, he said, medical professionals would need to combine emerging scientific knowledge with clinical experience to ensure that new technologies translate into meaningful improvements in patient care.

Concluding his address, the Minister stressed that preventing long-term disorders, particularly those increasingly affecting younger people, must become a collective national priority. Protecting the health and productive potential of India's youth will be essential to achieving Viksit Bharat 2047 of PM Narendra Modi's dreams, he said, calling for sustained efforts in prevention, medical research, technological innovation and responsible clinical practice.

Ministry of Defence
Defence Secretary inaugurates Hindi Library ‘GYANDEEP’ at Sena Bhawan in New Delhi under Special Campaign 6

Maintenance and cleaning of offices, segregation and disposal of e-waste, and related activities are also being carried out regularly across various offices and buildings of the Ministry of Defence, including Sena Bhawan, Kartavya Bhawan-II, Vayu Bhawan and KG Marg.

2326637.title: India Post Creates History, Crosses ₹4,000 Crore Revenue Mark for Two Consecutive Quarters
2326637.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
India Post Creates History, Crosses ₹4,000 Crore Revenue Mark for Two Consecutive Quarters
Department records 24% revenue growth in H1 FY 2026-27, reaching ₹8,212.7 crore; Parcels register 71% growth.
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia emphasises customer centricity, business diversification, innovation and digitisation to sustain India Post’s growth momentum.
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts has achieved a historic milestone by crossing the ₹4,000 crore quarterly revenue mark for two consecutive quarters for the first time. The Department recorded revenue of ₹8,212.7 crore during the first half of FY 2026-27 (April-September 2026), registering a year-on-year growth of 24% over ₹6,636 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

(L–R) Ms. Manisha Sinha, DGPS; Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union MoS for Communications and Rural Development; Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; and Shri Subrat Das, Secretary (Posts), during the Q2 Review Meeting in

New Delhi.

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region chaired the Second Quarter (Q2) Review at New Delhi, today. Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Shri Subrat Das, Secretary (Posts), Members of the Postal Services Board, Chief Postmasters General of all Postal Circles and senior officers of the Directorate attended the meeting.

The Department earned ₹4,201.5 crore in Q2 (Jul-September 2026), registering year-on-year growth of 25% and an increase of 5% over Q1.

Growth Across Business Verticals

All six business verticals recorded year-on-year growth. PLI/RPLI grew by 44%, Mails by 36%, Post Office Savings Bank (POSB) by 18%, International Relations & Global Business by 38%, and Parcels by 71%.

The Parcels vertical generated ₹318.9 crore in Q2, with Kerala, North East, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar exceeding their quarterly targets. Mails revenue increased by 26% over Q1, with 12 Postal Circles achieving or exceeding their Q2 targets. POSB contributed ₹1,987 crore, while PLI/RPLI achieved 92% of its quarterly target.

Postal Circle Performance and Efficiency

Seven Postal Circles achieved 90% or more of their proportionate Q2 targets. Bihar led with 97.15%, followed by West Bengal at 97.07% and North East at 94.79%. For H1, West Bengal recorded 95.72% achievement, followed by Bihar at 95.12% and Andhra Pradesh at 94.63%.

Eighteen of the 23 Postal Circles improved their target achievement over Q1. The Expenditure Cost Ratio reached 42% including pension expenditure and 62% excluding pension expenditure. Twenty-two Circles improved their ratios over Q1.

Recognition of Outstanding Postal Circles

In recognition of their performance during the first quarter(April–June 2026), Andhra Pradesh Postal Circle was awarded and  Bihar Postal Circle was awarded for the second quarter(July–September 2026), for their achievement against their respective proportionate business targets. Bihar Circle achieved 97.15%, followed closely by West Bengal Circle at 97.07% and North East Circle at 94.79%. Their performance reflects focused business efforts and progress towards the Department’s revenue objectives. The recognition also underscores the importance of sustained performance, effective business planning and continued efforts to strengthen revenue generation across Postal Circles.

Ministers Emphasise on Sustainable Growth

      

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region congratulated officers and employees on the achievement and emphasised the need to sustain growth through customer acquisition, service excellence and customer retention. He called for greater business diversification, stronger leadership, innovation and a customer-centric approach, including flexible pricing for bulk customers, subject to applicable policies and approvals. He also emphasised the need to accelerate the digitalisation of services offered by India Post to enhance customer experience, improve operational efficiency and strengthen the Department’s competitiveness.

Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development highlighted India Post’s substantial growth potential and stressed the importance of workforce empowerment, accountability and improved service delivery. He called for standardized procedures and real-time monitoring to address parcel delivery delays and enhance customer satisfaction.

The Ministers directed Postal Circles to sustain growth momentum during the festive and peak parcel season, strengthen Parcels and International Relations & Global Business, accelerate the onboarding of Citizen-Centric Services in collaboration with State Governments, and maintain expenditure discipline. The review also emphasized a cluster-based approach focusing on Agro-Logistics and International Business; MSMEs, ODOP and Tourism; and Citizen-Centric Services, Financial Inclusion, Insurance and Rural Logistics. Guided by the spirit of Jan Seva, the Department will leverage its extensive network and workforce to unlock new business opportunities, enhance operational efficiency and advance towards financial sustainability.

A historic Q2 for @IndiaPostOffice, after a historic Q1. Growth momentum continues, with Q2 revenue at ₹4,202 crore, up 25% year on year, led by: Parcel: +71% PLI/RPLI: +44% IR & GB: +38% Chaired the Quarterly Business Review with all 23 circles, where 19 crossed 80% of their Q2 targets. Reaffirmed our commitment to working as one India Post family, with greater synergy and a unified focus on scaling up and serving our customers to the best of our ability. #DakSewaJanSewa

2326629.title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to be Held in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on 26–27 October 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker
2326629.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to be Held in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on 26–27 October 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker
The Prime Minister of India will grace the forum and meet the leaders of visiting delegations: Lok Sabha Speaker
Presiding Officers of Parliaments, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries from BRICS member and partner countries to deliberate on strategic priorities for parliaments: Lok Sabha Speaker
Global parliamentary leaders to assemble in New Delhi for the conference being hosted under India's chairship on the theme of people-centric development: Lok Sabha Speaker
Deliberations to cover parliamentary functioning in relation to institutional resilience, ethical AI and digital transformation, global governance reforms and sustainable development: Lok Sabha Speaker
International Affairs Committees of BRICS member and partner countries to discuss parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices: Lok Sabha Speaker
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Parliament of India will host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on 26 and 27 October 2026 in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan. The conference will be inaugurated on 26 October.

Addressing a press conference at Parliament House today, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla said that the conference marks a new chapter in the history of India's parliamentary diplomacy. It will bring together Presiding Officers and parliamentary leaders from BRICS member and partner countries, Union Ministers, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh, Presiding Officers of State Legislatures, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries.

The Lok Sabha Speaker stated that the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi would grace the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations.

He further stated that the conference would feature bilateral and multilateral interactions with the leaders of visiting delegations and parliamentary friendship groups. A meeting of the Secretaries of the delegations will be held on 25 October 2026 to finalise the Joint Statement of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.

Highlighting the central theme of the programme, he said that the Forum would deliberate on the overarching theme of “Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development.”

He added that, building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum would facilitate consensus-based dialogue through the following four high-level sessions:

(i) Resilience: The critical role of parliaments in strengthening institutions to ensure a better future.

(ii) Innovation: Promoting human-centred innovation in artificial intelligence and digital technologies through parliaments.

(iii) Cooperation: Ensuring a more representative system of global governance through parliamentary cooperation.

(iv) Sustainability: The role of parliaments in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for our countries.

In addition, a special meeting of the Chairpersons of the International Affairs Committees of the parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices.

Shri Birla further stated that, alongside high-level plenary sessions, parallel meetings and bilateral exchanges, the conference would also feature a cultural programme. The Vice-President of India will host a banquet in honour of the distinguished guests.

Members of the delegations will visit the Parliament of India and also enjoy cultural visits in Delhi. The conference will conclude on 27 October.

भारत की संसद द्वारा 26 और 27 अक्टूबर 2026 को आयोजित होने जा रहे 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum से पूर्व आज संसद परिसर, नई दिल्ली में प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस को संबोधित किया। इस ऐतिहासिक सम्मेलन में ब्रिक्स के 11 Member Countries तथा 10 Partner Countries की संसदों के पीठासीन अधिकारी और संसदीय शिष्टमंडल भाग लेंगे। इस अवसर पर माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी की गरिमामयी उपस्थिति रहेगी। प्रधानमंत्री जी कार्यक्रम में सहभागिता करेंगे तथा आगंतुक अतिथियों के साथ संवाद करेंगे। 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय फोरम का मुख्य विषय “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development” है। इसके अंतर्गत Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability जैसे महत्वपूर्ण विषयों पर विचार-विमर्श होगा। सम्मेलन में ब्रिक्स सदस्य एवं भागीदार देशों की अंतरराष्ट्रीय मामलों संबंधी संसदीय समितियों के अध्यक्षों की विशेष बैठक, द्विपक्षीय एवं बहुपक्षीय संवाद तथा विभिन्न देशों के साथ गठित Parliamentary Friendship Groups की बैठकें भी आयोजित की जाएँगी। माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में सितंबर 2026 में आयोजित ब्रिक्स शिखर सम्मेलन सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न हुआ, जिसमें सभी सदस्य देशों ने भाग लिया और महत्वपूर्ण घोषणाएँ की गईं। 12वाँ ब्रिक्स संसदीय फोरम इसी दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है, जो विभिन्न देशों के बीच संसदीय सहयोग को सुदृढ़ करने और साझा वैश्विक चुनौतियों के समाधान हेतु संवाद को आगे बढ़ाएगा। मुझे विश्वास है कि यह सम्मेलन लोकतांत्रिक परंपराओं को सशक्त करने, जनता के प्रति जवाबदेही बढ़ाने, संवाद के माध्यम से सहमति बनाने, संसदीय संस्थाओं में तकनीक के उपयोग को बढ़ावा देने तथा वैश्विक चुनौतियों के समाधान में संसदीय सहयोग को नई ऊँचाइयों तक ले जाने का मार्ग प्रशस्त करेगा। #BRICS2026 #BRICSParliamentaryForum

2326612.title: Department of Science and Technology (DST) intensifies Special Campaign 6 with significant mid-campaign achievements (till 16th October, 2026)
2326612.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Department of Science and Technology (DST) intensifies Special Campaign 6 with significant mid-campaign achievements (till 16th October, 2026)
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Science and Technology (DST) has been implementing Special Campaign 6 in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign has witnessed active participation from the Department, its Autonomous Institutes, Subordinate Offices, Field Offices, Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs), Missions and other affiliated organisations.

At the commencement of the campaign, 315 cleanliness campaign sites were identified. Subsequently, on October 5, Joint Secretary (Administration) & the Nodal Officer for Special Campaign 6 chaired a review meeting with all Autonomous Bodies, Subordinate Offices, Field Offices, TIHs, Missions and other affiliated organisations. During the meeting, all organisations were encouraged to actively participate in the campaign and utilise the opportunity to undertake cleanliness drives, dispose of pending records and scrap, resolve public grievances and improve overall workplace management.

As a result of these sustained eﬀorts, the number of identified cleanliness campaign sites increased significantly from 315 to 401. Out of 401 sites, till date 397 sites have already been conducted which reflects the Department's proactive approach and enhanced participation across its organisations.

The campaign is expected to gain further momentum during the remaining period. The cumulative number of cleanliness campaign sites is anticipated to reach nearly 800 by the end of the campaign on 31st October 2026.

Significant progress has also been achieved in reducing pendency. Out of 135 public grievances, 99 have been disposed of, while 9 out of 23 public grievance appeals have been resolved. Further, 7 out of 12 references received from Members of Parliament have been disposed of.

Under record management, 6,280 out of 7,000 physical files due for review have been reviewed, and 2,598 identified files have been weeded out. In respect of e-files, 1,791 out of 1,900 files put up for review have been reviewed, of which 949 e-files have already been closed.

Through disposal activities and cleanliness campaigns undertaken during Special Campaign 6, a total of 61,888 square feet of space has been freed, while revenue amounting to ₹8,25,696 has been generated through the disposal of scrap.

Focused and sustained eﬀorts are being made to complete all the remaining campaign activities within the stipulated timelines. The Department is closely monitoring the progress of the campaign and remains committed to ensure timely completion of all identified activities and achievements of the campaign targets by the conclusion of Special Campaign 6.

The above achievements represent the progress made during the mid-campaign period. With all constituent organisations continuing to undertake campaign activities and additional cleanliness sites being identified on a regular basis, the Department expects to further improve its performance during the remaining period.

In order to generate awareness and increase public outreach under Special Campaign 6, DST has issued 03 Press Information Bureau (PIB) Statements and shared 72 tweets showcasing the campaign's progress, achievements through X (formerly Twitter). Besides X, public outreach platforms like Facebook and LinkedIn have also been eﬀectively leveraged to maximise the reach of the campaign.

2326606.title: PM to Inaugurate Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on 23 October
2326606.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM to Inaugurate Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on 23 October
Programme marks culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at 11 AM on 23 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

The three-day Sammelan, being held from 23 to 25 October 2026, will bring together over 9,000 participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951 to make the wisdom of Vedanta and the Bhagavad Gita accessible to all. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.

The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita, produced by Chinmaya Mission with music by Ilaiyaraaja, at Gangaikonda Cholapuram in Tamil Nadu. Several initiatives and events were organised during the year, including mass havans at multiple locations, consecration of the Maa Soundarya Chinmayi Temple in Tripura, and Chinmaya Gita Samarpanam under which over 1 lakh people across the world chanted the 15th chapter of the Bhagavad Gita together online. A major initiative of the celebrations was Gita Panchamrit, centred on five select verses of the Bhagavad Gita.
