2326609.title: Ministry of Tourism Undertakes Special Campaign 6.0 to Promote Cleanliness and Expedite Disposal of Pending Matters
2326609.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
Ministry of Tourism Undertakes Special Campaign 6.0 to Promote Cleanliness and Expedite Disposal of Pending Matters
Ministry identifies 5,654 targets under Special Campaign 6.0, with 3,563 activities completed so far
62,691 sq. ft. of space freed and revenue of ₹64.58 lakh generated through scrap disposal
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tourism is actively implementing the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6.0, aimed at promoting cleanliness, improving workplace efficiency and expediting the disposal of pending matters across its offices and institutions.

The campaign is being undertaken by the Ministry in coordination with its India Tourism Offices, Institutes of Hotel Management (IHMs), Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM), India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) and various Programme Divisions.

As part of the campaign, the Ministry has identified a total of 5,654 targets, which have been uploaded on the SCDPM portal. In this, 212 sites have been identified for cleanliness activities, while more than 3,006 physical files and 2,366 e-office files have been identified for review.

So far, 3,563 activities have been completed under the campaign. These efforts have resulted in the freeing up of 62,691 sq. ft. of office space and the generation of ₹64,58,145 in revenue through scrap disposal.

The progress of the campaign is being regularly monitored and updated on the SCDPM portal maintained by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

The Ministry of Tourism, along with its field offices and institutions, is also regularly highlighting activities undertaken under Special Campaign 6.0 through social media platforms to promote awareness and encourage wider participation in cleanliness initiatives.

2326360.title: Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to Focus on Investment, Value Addition and Export Opportunities in Inland Fisheries
2326360.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2326360.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to Focus on Investment, Value Addition and Export Opportunities in Inland Fisheries
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 8:16AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India (GoI) are organising Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to be held on 23 October 2026 in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. The Conclave aims to strengthen linkages between inland fisheries production and investment, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, value addition and export markets. It seeks to encourage a shift from a predominantly production-oriented approach towards an integrated value-chain model, with a focus on improving market access and returns for fishermen and fish farmers.

The Conclave will bring together investors, exporters, fishers, more than 1,000 fish farmers from various parts of Madhya Pradesh, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs), entrepreneurs, start-ups, processors, financial institutions, research organisations and other stakeholders. Deliberations will focus on enterprise development, access to finance, market linkages and opportunities for collaboration across the inland fisheries value chain, with particular emphasis on integrating inland States into the fisheries investment and export ecosystem.

A key feature of the Conclave will be the release of the MADHYA PRADESH FISHERIES INVESTMENT AND EXPORT GUIDELINES, 2026. Madhya Pradesh has been notified by the Center as a Reservoir Fisheries Cluster.  The policy is intended to facilitate investment across key segments of the fisheries value chain, including hatcheries, fish seed and feed, reservoir and cage fisheries, aquatic animal health, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, logistics, value addition and market development.

The programme will also feature the release of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) on the export potential of inland States, the virtual inauguration of Integrated Cage Culture Units.  During the event, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj will hand over the Administrative Approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in Madhya Pradesh. These initiatives are expected to support investment in inland fisheries, promote the productive utilisation of water resources and encourage enterprise development.

The Conclave assumes significance in the context of India's expanding fisheries sector and its growing contribution to food security, livelihoods and export earnings. India’s fish production reached 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024–25, of which 151.60 lakh tonnes came from inland fisheries, accounting for nearly three-fourths of the country's total fish production. India's seafood exports were valued at ₹73,890 crore in 2025–26. These figures highlight the importance of strengthening infrastructure, processing capabilities and market linkages to realise the potential of inland fisheries.

Madhya Pradesh, with nearly 4.50 lakh hectares of water area, offers considerable potential for inland fisheries development. The Conclave seeks to connect the State's production base, along with that of other inland States, with investment, processing, value addition and domestic and export markets.

The Conclave will be graced by Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; and Shri Narayan Singh Pawar, Hon’ble Minister, Department of Fisherman Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh.

Through stakeholder engagement and deliberations on investment and market development, the Conclave seeks to promote more competitive and market-oriented inland fisheries value chains, expand opportunities for enterprises and exporters, and strengthen livelihood and income opportunities for fishermen and fish farmers.

2326359.body_html:

Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:49AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, highlighting the importance of remaining humble over limited success and the constant need to learn and grow.

 

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

 

"खद्योतो द्योतते तावद् यावन्नोदयते शशी।

उदिते तु सहस्रांशौ न खद्योतो न चन्द्रमाः।।"

 

A firefly appears to shine only in the absence of the moon. But when the sun rises, neither the firefly's glow nor the moon can be seen. Likewise, the significance of a lesser achievement lasts only until something greater comes along. Therefore, one should remain humble rather than become arrogant over limited success and continue to learn and grow.

2326255.title: Union MoS Raksha Khadse, Guest of Honour at Chhattisgarh Hockey League Opening Ceremony, Calls It a Major Step Towards Strengthening Grassroots Hockey
2326255.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2326255.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union MoS Raksha Khadse, Guest of Honour at Chhattisgarh Hockey League Opening Ceremony, Calls It a Major Step Towards Strengthening Grassroots Hockey
Following Khelo India Tribal Games, Chhattisgarh Hockey League marks another sporting milestone for the state; inaugural edition features six franchises and 132 players
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse was the Guest of Honour at the opening ceremony of the inaugural Chhattisgarh Hockey League (CHL) at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Hockey Stadium in Raipur on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.

On Building Sporting Momentum in Chhattisgarh

Following the Khelo India Tribal Games, the Chhattisgarh Hockey League marks another significant sporting milestone in the state’s journey towards becoming a stronger sporting hub. While the Khelo India Tribal Games showcased the sporting talent of tribal communities, the league builds on this momentum by creating a dedicated platform for hockey players, strengthening grassroots competition and expanding opportunities for young athletes. Together, these initiatives reflect Chhattisgarh’s growing commitment to sports development and its potential to make a greater contribution to India’s sporting future.

Organised by the Department of Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Chhattisgarh, and sanctioned by Hockey India, the league brings together six franchise-based teams representing different regions of the state. The inaugural season will run from 21 October to 1 November 2026 at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Hockey Stadium, Raipur.

On Strengthening Grassroots Hockey

Addressing the occasion, Union MoS Raksha Khadse highlighted the importance of creating structured sporting opportunities for young athletes and strengthening sports development at the grassroots. She emphasised that leagues such as the Chhattisgarh Hockey League can help bridge the gap between grassroots participation and higher levels of competition by enabling young players to compete alongside experienced national and international talent.

She underscored that developing sporting talent requires sustained efforts across the entire ecosystem, including quality coaching, competitive opportunities, sports infrastructure and institutional support. Providing young athletes with the right platforms to demonstrate their abilities is essential to building a stronger sporting culture and expanding India’s talent pool.

Union MoS Raksha Khadse also highlighted the importance of strengthening sports participation among youth in tribal and rural regions. Chhattisgarh has significant potential to contribute to India’s sporting future, and initiatives that connect local talent with established athletes can help young players gain experience, confidence and exposure to higher standards of competition.

On Cultural Identity and Celebrations

The league features six teams: Rajdhani Royals, Nyayadhani Knights, Sanskardhani Strikers, Chakradhar Champions, Bailadila Bulls and Mainpat Titans. Each team comprises 22 players, including 18 players from Chhattisgarh and four players from outside the state. The squads also feature former Olympians as marquee players, bringing experience and competitive quality to the tournament.

A total of 132 players will participate in the inaugural season, including 108 players from Chhattisgarh and 24 guest players. The tournament will feature 18 men’s matches, followed by semi-finals and the final scheduled for 1 November. A women’s exhibition match will also be organised, providing an opportunity to showcase women’s hockey and encourage wider participation in the sport.

Shri Sardar Singh, Olympian and former captain of the Indian hockey team, is the league ambassador. His association with the league is expected to inspire young players and strengthen their connection with India’s hockey legacy.

The league’s identity is rooted in the culture and spirit of Chhattisgarh. Its mascot, Baghwa, draws inspiration from the tiger, while the tagline, “Chalo Re Sangi, Hockey Khelbo”, reflects the local character of the initiative and encourages people across the state to embrace hockey.

The opening ceremony also celebrates Chhattisgarh’s cultural heritage through performances showcasing the state’s traditions, alongside entertainment and sporting tributes. Punjabi singers Jassi Gill and Babbal Rai are among the featured performers.

The tournament offers a total prize pool of ₹21 lakh, with ₹11 lakh for the winning team and ₹6 lakh for the runners-up. Individual awards will also recognise outstanding performances throughout the competition.

All matches will be played at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Hockey Stadium, Raipur. Entry for spectators is free, and matches will be streamed live on JioHotstar, enabling hockey fans across the country to follow the competition.

The Chhattisgarh Hockey League reflects a broader effort to build a stronger sporting ecosystem by bringing together government support, sporting institutions, experienced athletes and emerging talent. By creating more opportunities for local players to compete and learn, the league seeks to strengthen Chhattisgarh’s contribution to Indian hockey and inspire the next generation of athletes.

2326348.title: 33rd EDITION OF SINGAPORE-INDIA MARITIME BILATERAL EXERCISE (SIMBEX-2026) COMMENCES AT VISAKHAPATNAM
2326348.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
33rd EDITION OF SINGAPORE-INDIA MARITIME BILATERAL EXERCISE (SIMBEX-2026) COMMENCES AT VISAKHAPATNAM
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

The 33rd edition of the Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise (SIMBEX-2026) is being held at Visakhapatnam from 21 to 26 Oct 2026. Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) ship RSS Supreme arrived at Visakhapatnam on 21 Oct 2026 to participate in the exercise.

The opening ceremony of SIMBEX-2026 was held on 21 Oct 2026 onboard INS Nilgiri and INS Kamorta. The ceremony was attended by the Chief Staff Officer (Operations) of the Eastern Naval Command, the Fleet Commander of the RSN, and other senior officers from both Navies.

Since its inception in 1994 as Exercise Lion King, SIMBEX has evolved into a significant bilateral maritime engagement between the Indian Navy and the RSN. Over the years, the exercise has expanded in scope and complexity, strengthening professional ties, mutual understanding and operational interoperability between the two Navies.

The exercise will be conducted in two phases. The Harbour Phase, from 21 to 23 Oct 2026, will include professional interactions, Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-deck visits, sporting engagements, and planning conferences. The Sea Phase, scheduled from 24 to 26 Oct 2026 in the Bay of Bengal, will feature maritime operations and tactical exercises, including Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), anti-surface and anti-air warfare drills, seamanship evolutions, and tactical manoeuvres.

SIMBEX-2026 reaffirms the longstanding maritime partnership between India and Singapore and their shared commitment to enhancing interoperability, addressing common maritime security challenges, and promoting peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

2326184.title: INDIAN AIR FORCE ENGAGES INDUSTRY OUTREACH PROGRAMME ON UNMANNED AND AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS ROADMAP ON 21 OCT 26
2326184.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN AIR FORCE ENGAGES INDUSTRY OUTREACH PROGRAMME ON UNMANNED AND AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS ROADMAP ON 21 OCT 26
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Air Force (IAF) conducted an Industry Outreach Programme at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, on 21 October 2026, to engage with stakeholders, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), startups and industry partners to share IAF's long-term capability requirements in the field of unmanned and autonomous systems. The programme was chaired by Air Marshal Premkumar K, VM, VSM, Director General (Weapon Systems), Air Headquarters. Around 100 representatives from various drone companies and affiliated industry partners participated, reflecting the growing engagement between IAF and India's unmanned ecosystem.

The programme provided a formal Platform for IAF to articulate its operational requirements and technological priorities, building on the ‘IAF Unmanned and Autonomous Systems Roadmap’, released during IAF Dronathon 2026 at Pokhran on 14 September 2026. Today's event marked an engagement, where IAF not only elucidated their future requirements, but also distributed 'IAF's Roadmap booklet' to the industry partners.

This would enable a better understanding of the IAF's operational requirements in the domain of unmanned and autonomous systems. Recognising the rapid evolution of air power, the roadmap envisages a layered and networked family of unmanned systems. The emphasis is on developing operationally relevant, reliable and resilient indigenous capabilities that complement existing and future manned platforms.

 It was emphasised in the event  that Aatmanirbharta in unmanned systems is an operational necessity, not merely an aspiration. Also, Indigenous propulsion, autonomous software, resilient navigation and standardised interfaces are among the critical technology areas that require focused attention to reduce dependence on external sources and strengthen the domestic defence ecosystem.

Through sustained engagement with industry, MSMEs, startups, and academia IAF aims to accelerate innovation, encourage collaborative development and translate emerging technologies into credible operational capabilities and  aims to build a robust domestic ecosystem capable of supporting and contributing to India's Atmanirbharta in defence technology.

Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 8:17PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Secretary Shri Govind Mohan addressed a Press Conference in New Delhi today on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas 2026 and Bharat Parv 2026 celebrations to be held in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat.

Briefing the media, Union Home Secretary said that this year’s Ekta Parade will be more vibrant, diverse and attractive. The main function will commence on 31st October 2026. Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi will pay tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the ‘Statue of Unity’ in the morning. Ekta Parade will be held in the evening. The Parade will lay emphasis on the massive achievement of getting India rid of armed Naxalism in 2026.

Shri Govind Mohan said that the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations at Ekta Nagar have been envisioned keeping two purposes in mind. The first purpose is to bring to the attention of the nation, the extraordinary work being done by the Police forces, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Central Police Organisations (CPOs) of the country. The second purpose is to invite the people from all parts of the country to witness and enjoy the local surroundings of Ekta Nagar, along with the largest statue in the world of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He said that several other attractions have been created around Ekta Nagar, which has now emerged as one of the most prominent and most attractive tourist destinations in the country.

Union Home Secretary said that during the Ekta Diwas parade, we will be celebrating the end of armed Naxalism in the country. He said this will be done through three different and unique performances:

  1. This year’s parade contingents will include State Police forces and CAPFs who have been at the forefront of the country’s fight against armed Naxalism. During the passage of each of these contingents before the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 31st October, 2026, a short film will be displayed on several LED screens, summarizing the salient features of their singular achievements.
  2. National School of Drama (NSD) will present with an array of around 2,000 artists, drawn from 126 districts of the country, which at some point have witnessed menace of armed Naxalism. These artists will, through their performances, showcase the struggle they have gone through when armed Naxalism was rampant and their lives and properties were threatened.
  3. Around 5,000 people from these 126 districts have been invited. These will be spectators for all performances and they will also, through their interactions, recount their experiences during the era of armed Naxalism.

Union Home Secretary said that through these three elements, we will witness India's struggle against armed Naxalism, the fact that it has now been eradicated and most importantly in place of militancy and violence, today these districts are experiencing a wave of development.

Shri Govind Mohan said that the theme of cultural items in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations is Vande Mataram. He said that this is the 150th year of Vande Mataram and many newly introduced features during this year’s parade have been drawn from Vande Mataram.

Home Secretary said that another new feature of this year’s celebrations is that the parade and all the performances will be held in the evening. He added that due to high temperatures during the daytime, it has been decided to hold the events in the evening, to make it more enthralling.

Union Home Secretary said that normally, the tableaus are made and designed by either government ministries/departments or by the state governments or other government entities. This time it has been decided to invite designs and features for the tableau through national competitions which were run on MyGov at the national level and also in every district of Gujarat.

Shri Govind Mohan said that weaving together all the themes and designs received from the national and the state-level competitions, a total of 15 tableaus will be made based on these designs. These designs will be made entirely by the public, without any involvement of any government ministry or department. Shri Mohan added that we are moving to the idea when tableau at important events will incorporate the aspirations of the common people of India rather than the structured themes of government entities and state governments. First time, a people's tableau will be witnessed in Ekta Nagar.

Union Home Secretary said that another important departure that we have made is on the cultural program. Until now, the cultural program was done by the culture ministry, but this time we have involved the people of Gujarat. In Gujarat, there are groups of people who come from different states of the country and have been living there for generations and they have made Gujarat their home. We reached out to these different groups and requested them to curate their own cultural performances, basis the performances emanating from the states to which they belong. Weaving together around 50 such elements, we have created a cultural performance, having about 5,000 artists. This is a great example of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat, which will also be on display.

Shri Govind Mohan said that since last year, we have been hosting a large play, curated by the National School of Drama. Last year the theme was on Sardar Patel. This year being the year of Vande Mataram, the theme will be Anandamath, a path breaking novel of Shri Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyaya. This play will be based on Anandamath novel. However, the play will also be based on the abiding philosophy of Ananadamath, that every Indian has a responsibility towards building a bright future for the country, has to be aware of our cultural heritage and has to be a willing partner in fulfilling the nation's aspirations.

2326148.title: CAQM holds meeting with Delhi Government agencies to review Dust Pollution issues and strengthen Air Pollution Mitigation
2326148.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2326148.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM holds meeting with Delhi Government agencies to review Dust Pollution issues and strengthen Air Pollution Mitigation
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

A review meeting was held today under the Co-Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), and the Chief Secretary, GNCTD, with concerned agencies of the Delhi Government to review dust pollution issues and strengthening coordinated action for effective air pollution mitigation in Delhi in the coming days.

The Commission emphasized that all concerned agencies must strictly comply with its Statutory Directions issued from time to time and ensure their strict implementation. MCD was specifically directed to strengthen dust mitigation measures on roads and open areas under its jurisdiction.

The review was held in continuation of the Commission’s ongoing assessment of dust mitigation measures in Delhi. Earlier, vide Notice dated 07.10.2026, MCD had been directed to appear before the Commission along with all its Deputy Commissioners on 12.10.2026 and submit a detailed zone-wise presentation on efforts undertaken/being undertaken for removal of dust and garbage from roads.

During today’s meeting, DPCC was directed to ensure close coordination among all concerned agencies for effective air pollution mitigation. Further, it has come to the notice that many agencies and departments involved in construction across Delhi are not ensuring dust mitigation measures like installation of wind barriers, dust screens, etc. and most importantly for digging work which leads to accumulation of dust. The concerned departments were directed to take prompt action on identified dust pollution issues and take strict action against the concerned officials and project proponent/ implementing agencies in cases of violation and ensure compliance.

The Commission reiterated that strict action would be taken against officials failing to implement the Statutory Directions, particularly with regard to dust mitigation measures. The District Magistrates of GNCTD would monitor compliance and ensure that measures are implemented on the ground in their respective jurisdictions.

2326147.title: National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme) strengthens MSMEs through Capacity Building, Entrepreneurship Development and Digital Empowerment
2326147.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme) strengthens MSMEs through Capacity Building, Entrepreneurship Development and Digital Empowerment
11,032 executives from 150 countries trained through 550 international programmes; 17,672 programmes conducted in India benefiting 6,07,497 participants
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme), an autonomous Institute under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, plays a significant role in promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening managerial capabilities and supporting the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) across the country. Through special training programmes, research, consultancy, capacity building and institutional partnerships, the Institute contributes to building a competitive, skilled and innovation-oriented MSME ecosystem.

The institute accredited with “UTKRISHT / उत्कृष्ट” 3-Star Rating by the Capacity Building Commission (CBC). The 66 years old institute plays a pivotal role in promoting innovation, entrepreneurship, and capacity building for MSME development by fostering a pro-business environment. Over the decades, it has evolved to address the changing needs of entrepreneurs, policymakers, government institutions and industry stakeholders, with a focus on capacity building, sustainable enterprise development and enhanced competitiveness.

Legacy of Enterprise Development

The Institute was established in 1960 as the Central Industrial Extension Training Institute (CIETI) in New Delhi. It shifted to Hyderabad in 1962 and was registered as the Small Industry Extension Training Institute (SIET). Following the enactment of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, the Institute was renamed the National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme) in 2007.

The Institute covers enterprise creation, finance, marketing, international trade, digital transformation, technology adoption and sustainable business practices, supporting employment generation, productivity and inclusive economic growth.

Key Achievements of ni-msme

  • International Training: Conducted 550 international programmes, training 11,032 executives from 150 countries.
  • National Training: Organised 17,672 programmes, benefiting 6,07,497 participants.
  • Skill Development: Conducted 6,840 programmes, training 2,10,062 youth.
  • MSME Cluster Development: Implemented 27 MSME cluster projects.
  • IPFC Services: Provided 235 services through Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres (IPFCs).
  • Research and Studies: Completed 962 research studies to support MSME development and policymaking.

Supporting Innovation and Emerging Enterprise Needs

As businesses increasingly adapt to digital technologies, changing market expectations and evolving production systems, ni-msme continues to engage with emerging areas of enterprise development. Its programmes and institutional activities encompass subjects such as digital marketing, e-commerce, artificial intelligence, technology-enabled manufacturing, intellectual property rights, green energy and sustainable enterprise practices. These areas are increasingly relevant to MSME seeking to improve operational efficiency, develop new products, expand their market reach and remain competitive.

In March 2026, the Institute organised a national conference on Digital Marketing, AI Automation and e-Commerce, followed by a national conference on Digital Enabled Factories with Industry 5.0, focusing on artificial intelligence, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and cloud technologies. These engagements provided platforms for discussing the application of emerging technologies in enterprise development and manufacturing. Through such knowledge-sharing initiatives, ni-msme contributes to raising awareness of new business opportunities and encouraging MSME to explore technology-driven approaches to growth.

Success Stories Reflect ni-msme’s Transformational Impact:

(a) Weaving New Markets: A Traditional Silk Enterprise Goes Digital

Mr. Mahankali Chandra Sekhar’sAmarchintha Handloom Weavers Producer Company Ltd., Wanaparthy, Telangana, is weaving a new success story through digital transformation.

In 2024–25, with support from NABARD, the company’s marketing executive underwent a five-day training programme at ni-msme, Ministry of MSME, followed by one year of handholding to strengthen digital branding and market outreach.

 

By leveraging Instagram, WhatsApp Business and Google Business Profile, the company secured a landmark ₹16 lakh order through Google, while its annual turnover surged to ₹2.8 crore. Amarchintha’s journey is a testament to how digital adoption can expand market access, empower traditional artisans and drive MSME growth.

(b) From Millets to Markets: A Woman Entrepreneur’s Growth Story

Smt. SunkishalaSwarupa, a woman entrepreneur from Shayampet, Telangana, transformed her millet food business through digital marketing. Under a NABARD-supported project implemented by ni-msme, Ministry of MSME, she underwent a five-day training programme on digital branding and marketing, followed by one year of handholding support.

By leveraging Instagram, Google My Business and Canva, she enhanced her online visibility, expanded her customer base and strengthened the promotion of her millet products.

 

The Impact:

  • 10-fold growth in monthly turnover, from ₹20,000 to ₹2 lakh.
  • Employment created for local women.

Her journey showcases how digital empowerment can transform women-led enterprises and drive inclusive MSME growth.

Ni-msme: Empowering MSME, Enabling Growth

Through its sustained efforts in entrepreneurship development, capacity building, research and digital empowerment, ni-msme continues to strengthen India’s MSME ecosystem and foster inclusive economic growth. Its achievements in training lakhs of participants, supporting enterprise development and enabling success stories demonstrate its commitment to empowering entrepreneurs, enhancing competitiveness and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities. By equipping enterprises with the skills, knowledge and tools to adapt to a changing business environment, ni-msme remains a key contributor to building a self-reliant, innovative and globally competitive MSME sector in India.

For more information visit at: http://www.nimsme.gov.in/

2326141.body_html:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Women and Child Development to Organize Dedicated Nationwide Drive on 30th October Under Special Campaign 6
Special focus on public grievance redressal through Grievance Redressal Chaupals and e-Chaupals for Poshan Tracker and PMMVY beneficiaries
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Women and Child Development, including all Autonomous/ Statutory Bodies under its administrative control, has initiated efforts and finalised action plans & targets to implement Special Campaign 6 for improving Swachhata and disposal of pending references from 2nd October - 31st October, 2026, on the lines of the Special Campaigns held in the preceding 5 years.

As part of the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, Ministry of Women & Child Development will be organising a dedicated one-day event on 30th October, 2026 by undertaking various activities in the field institutions functional under the schemes of the Ministry all over the country. In this regard, a VC meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Additional Secretary(WCD) and Nodal Officer for Special Campaign on 21.10.2026 at 04.00 P.M. with States/UTs to finalise the action plan for the dedicated one-day event. All the Joint Secretaries and Directors/Deputy Secretaries dealing with the Schemes and  94 Officers from the States/UTs participated in the VC. It was decided that following activities would be undertaken in all States/UTs as part of special campaign 6 and  the dedicated one-day event:

  • Cleanliness Drives at Field-Level Institutions-Regular activity and to be organized at large scale on 30th October 2026
  • Effective Public Grievance Redressal and organizing Grievance Redressal Chaypal/e-Chaupals: All the Grievances received through Poshan Tracker and PMMVY to be addressed till 30th October 2026  and for the pending grievances Grievance Redressal Chaupal /E Chaupal to be organized by the designated Grievance Redressal Officer(s) (GROs)

2326129.title: Deep Cleaning Exercise under Special Campaign 6.0
2326129.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Deep Cleaning Exercise under Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, is strengthening its commitment to cleanliness, sustainable waste management, and environmental responsibility through activities undertaken under Special Campaign 6.0 and its broader initiatives to promote textile waste collection and circularity. As part of these efforts, a deep cleaning exercise was conducted at GPOA, Tower-3, 5th Floor, New Delhi, to promote workplace hygiene, efficient utilisation of office space, and a clean and healthy working environment. The activity focused on the thorough cleaning and upkeep of workstations, common areas, and other office spaces, along with the removal of dust and unwanted materials. Emphasis was also placed on proper waste management, organised workspaces, and the effective utilisation of available office space.

The initiative seeks to encourage employees to adopt good housekeeping practices and take collective responsibility for maintaining a clean, hygienic, and well-organised workplace. It reflects the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0, which places emphasis on cleanliness, space management, disposal of redundant materials, and sustainable practices in government offices. Through such activities, the Ministry aims to foster a culture of cleanliness and environmental awareness while contributing to a healthier and more productive working environment.

Key Highlights of the Deep Cleaning Exercise & Review Process:

  • High-Level Review Meetings: Continuous monitoring by higher officers before and after the drive to ensure rigorous standards of cleanliness and effective execution.

2326124.title: National Action Plan For Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR)
2326124.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Action Plan For Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR)
Supporting South Delhi’s Rahul Kumar’s Journey Towards Emotional Stability And Rehabilitation
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

Access to appropriate treatment, psychological care and structured rehabilitation help individuals overcome personal challenges and work towards a healthier and more stable life.

The journey of Rahul Kumar (name changed), a 32-year-old beneficiary from South Delhi, Delhi, highlights the importance of institutional support in improving emotional well-being and helping individuals work towards fulfilling their family responsibilities.

Rahul Kumar was receiving support at SPYM IRCA Dakshinpuri, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) in South Delhi. Before the intervention, he faced challenges in managing anger and maintaining emotional balance. The limited availability of consistent family support, coupled with financial dependence during rehabilitation, contributed to his stress. Despite these difficulties, he aspired to become more responsible towards his family and contribute to their financial and emotional well-being.

A significant step towards recovery began when Rahul Kumar received assistance under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). Through the intervention, he received in-patient treatment, medical care, psychological support and structured rehabilitation. Counselling and a supportive care environment helped him focus on his recovery and work towards better emotional regulation and behavioural management.

Following the intervention, Rahul Kumar reported feeling better during treatment and demonstrated improvement in his psychological well-being. He is now more emotionally stable and better able to manage his behaviour and thoughts. The treatment and rehabilitation support have helped him develop greater control over his emotions and strengthened his motivation to take responsibility for his family.

Although specific changes in income have not been reported, Rahul Kumar ’s improved emotional stability and readiness to support his family represent important progress in his rehabilitation journey. His experience highlights how access to medical treatment, psychological care and structured rehabilitation can help individuals address personal challenges and work towards greater independence and social well-being.

Supported on 27 April 2026, Rahul Kumar ’s journey reflects the importance of the NAPDDR scheme in facilitating access to treatment and rehabilitation services. Through institutional care, counselling and psychological support, the intervention has helped him move towards improved emotional health, greater self-confidence and a more stable future. His experience underscores the value of sustained rehabilitation support in helping individuals rebuild their lives and strengthen their relationships with their families and communities.

2326117.title: CONCLUSION OF THE NINTH EDITION OF INDIA-BRAZIL-SOUTH AFRICA MARITIME EXERCISE (IBSAMAR IX 2026)
2326117.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
CONCLUSION OF THE NINTH EDITION OF INDIA-BRAZIL-SOUTH AFRICA MARITIME EXERCISE (IBSAMAR IX 2026)
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

The ninth edition of the India-Brazil-South Africa Maritime (IBSAMAR) Exercise 2026 concluded at Simon’s Town, South Africa, on 20 Oct 2026. It brought together the Indian, Brazilian and South African Navies for a series of professional interactions and maritime evolutions aimed at enhancing interoperability, strengthening operational cooperation and fostering greater mutual understanding among the three maritime forces.

The closing ceremony marked the culmination of ten days of joint activities conducted during the harbour and sea phases. Participating personnel engaged in professional exchanges, operational interactions and joint training, gaining valuable insights into each other’s procedures, capabilities and methods of operating at sea. These activities helped build familiarity and confidence among the participating Navies, enabling them to work together with enhanced synergy in the maritime domain.

Addressing the gathering at the closing ceremony, the Commanding Officer of INS Tarkash highlighted that exercises such as IBSAMAR provide a unique platform for translating longstanding diplomatic relationships into meaningful naval cooperation. He underscored that the true strength of such exercises lies not only in conducting joint evolutions at sea but also in the relationships forged among personnel through shared experiences, professional exchanges and mutual learning.

IBSAMAR exemplifies the enduring maritime relationship between India, Brazil and South Africa. Located across three continents and connected by the maritime domain, the three nations share a common interest in safe, secure and stable seas. The trilateral exercise provides an avenue for their Navies to address common maritime challenges, exchange best practices and strengthen their ability to operate together, thereby contributing to a peaceful maritime environment.

The exercise also reaffirmed the importance of jointmanship at sea, with interoperability developed through repeated interactions, common training and a shared understanding of maritime operations. Professional bonds forged among the crews of participating assets endure beyond the exercise, strengthening institutional linkages and laying the foundation for future cooperation.

The successful conclusion of IBSAMAR IX 2026 underscores the shared commitment of India, Brazil and South Africa to strengthening maritime cooperation and enhancing interoperability in support of safe, secure and open seas underpinned by a rules-based order.

2326116.title: Hon’ble President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu presents 65th National Exhibition of Art and 3rd Print Biennale India awards to artists, celebrating India’s rich artistic heritage and contemporary creativity
2326116.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Hon’ble President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu presents 65th National Exhibition of Art and 3rd Print Biennale India awards to artists, celebrating India’s rich artistic heritage and contemporary creativity
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat graces the event organised by Lalit Kala Akademi
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today graced the award   ceremony of the 65th National Exhibition of Art and the 3rd Print Biennale India 2026, organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism and Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, were present on the occasion, along with senior officials, artists and members of the cultural fraternity.

The award ceremony recognised the outstanding contributions of artists to India’s rich cultural heritage and contemporary visual arts, with awards presented to selected artists as part of the 65th National Exhibition of Art and the 3rd Print Biennale India 2026.

The Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, welcomed the Hon’ble President and presented her with a Gond painting as a token of gratitude, reflecting the richness of India’s indigenous artistic traditions. A special film showcasing the journey of the Lalit Kala Akademi and the evolution of the National Exhibition of Art since its inception in 1955 was also screened on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble President, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, highlighted India’s rich and diverse artistic heritage, describing art as a mirror of the country’s culture, traditions and civilisational journey. She emphasised the importance of preserving traditional art forms and highlighted printmaking as a significant tradition of artistic expression.

The Hon’ble President also highlighted the role of exhibitions and biennales in encouraging dialogue and the exchange of ideas among artists. She appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Culture in creating opportunities for the promotion and wider reach of artworks and integrating artists into the creative economy.

Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi for providing a national platform for artists to showcase their work and celebrate India’s artistic diversity. He highlighted the distinctive vision and creative expression reflected in every artwork, representing the artist’s unique perspective and imagination. He emphasised that this diversity of artistic expression enriches the world of art and strengthens India’s vibrant creative traditions.

Drawing on his experience of witnessing printmaking practices during the inauguration of the Print Biennale, the Union Minister highlighted the significance of printmaking as a medium that combines technical expertise with artistic innovation. He noted that platforms such as the National Exhibition of Art and the Print Biennale support artistic exchange, strengthen international connections and enhance the global visibility of Indian art.

Linking India’s cultural growth with the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, Shri Shekhawat underscored the importance of Sanskriti Samriddhi and Indian creativity in the country’s development journey. He also highlighted the integration of artwork sales into the programme as an important step towards expanding opportunities for artists, strengthening their livelihoods and advancing India’s creative economy.

In his address, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, traced the journey of the Lalit Kala Akademi since its establishment in 1954 and the evolution of the National Exhibition of Art, which began at Jaipur House in 1955 with approximately 1,200 entries.

Highlighting the scale of the 65th National Exhibition of Art, he noted that this year's edition received 6,175 artworks from 2,495 artists representing 27 States and Union Territories. A total of 270 artworks were selected for exhibition, and 20 artists were chosen for the Awards.

Shri Aggarwal also highlighted the importance of the Print Biennale in promoting printmaking, encouraging experimentation and facilitating interaction between Indian and international artists. He emphasised the Akademi’s continued efforts to expand public engagement with art, nurture emerging talent and create opportunities for artists to connect with wider audiences.

The Ministry of Culture will organise India Biennale 2026 from December 4, 2026, to March 21, 2027, across monuments and heritage sites in Delhi. The initiative will provide a platform for artistic expression and engagement with India’s cultural heritage, bringing contemporary creativity into dialogue with the country’s historic spaces.

The Biennale will further strengthen opportunities for artists to showcase their work, promote creative exchange and enhance public engagement with art and heritage.

The award ceremony reaffirmed the importance of preserving India’s diverse artistic traditions while encouraging contemporary creativity, wider recognition for artists and the integration of art into the country’s cultural and creative economy.

2326107.title: DRI seizes more than 9 kg methamphetamine in intensified crackdown on synthetic drug trafficking in Bhopal; One held
2326107.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes more than 9 kg methamphetamine in intensified crackdown on synthetic drug trafficking in Bhopal; One held
Major seizure at Bhopal ISBT highlights growing threat of synthetic narcotics
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant crackdown on synthetic drug trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 9.139 kg of methamphetamine and arrested one person at the Inter-State Bus Terminal (ISBT), Bhopal, on 20th October 2026. The seizure highlights DRI’s sustained efforts to disrupt the movement of dangerous synthetic drugs through the country’s inter-city transport networks.

 

Acting on specific intelligence, officers of DRI intercepted an Indian male passenger travelling by bus from Delhi to Bengaluru upon the bus’s arrival at Bhopal ISBT. Examination of the passenger’s baggage led to the recovery of 11 plastic packets containing crystalline methamphetamine, weighing 9.139 kg, concealed inside packets of salwar suits and carried in two mid-sized trolley bags. Field testing confirmed the presence of methamphetamine in the recovered substance, which was seized and the passenger was arrested under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

This seizure comes amid growing concerns over the trafficking of synthetic drugs in the country. In recent major operations, DRI seized 231.8 kg Meth tablets in the North-Eastern region, suspected to have been smuggled from Myanmar and 137 kg suspected crystal methamphetamine in Tamil Nadu, where the consignment was allegedly intended for onward smuggling to Sri Lanka through maritime route. These operations underscore the scale and varied routes of synthetic drug trafficking, spanning inter-city transport networks, cross border and coastal corridors.

Through sustained intelligence-led enforcement, DRI remains committed to dismantling narcotics trafficking networks and preventing dangerous drugs from reaching illicit markets.

2326056.title: 8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Begins in Guwahati Today
2326056.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Begins in Guwahati Today
75 Artisans, Including 31 Women, to Showcase Around 40 Varieties of Handloom and Handicraft Products
Mela to Promote Market Access, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods for Artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi

The 08 days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 began in State Capital Guwahati of Assam, today. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, until October 28 Wednesday.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors will explore the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

He said the Mela is bringing together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, to showcase India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.

The Official said a total of 75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.

He said the event is providing participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach. By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.

The Official said the Guwahati edition features a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India. The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added. He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

The Official further said a key focus of the Mela will be the promotion of BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms. By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative seeks to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings. It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).

The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”, the Mela seeks to promote the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs). It provides a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela will help create awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations. The initiative seeks to complement financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.

It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of communities having financial constraints, by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.

The Mela is expected to enhance the visibility of participating artisans, expand awareness of their products and encourage greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

2326043.title: India and New Zealand sign Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on Electronic Origin Data Exchange to Facilitate Bilateral Trade Under the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA)
2326043.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
India and New Zealand sign Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on Electronic Origin Data Exchange to Facilitate Bilateral Trade Under the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA)
India-New Zealand MoC will deepen Customs cooperation and support effective implementation of trade facilitation measures
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), India, and the New Zealand Customs Service (NZCS) signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) concerning Electronic Origin Data Exchange of Trade in Goods.

The MoC marks an important step towards strengthening customs cooperation and facilitating bilateral trade between the two countries. The MoC was signed under the India-New Zealand FTA which entered into force from 20th October, 2026.

The MoC was signed on 19th October 2026 by Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, and Ms. Christine Stevenson, Comptroller and Chief Executive, New Zealand Customs Service.

The MoC reflects the shared commitment of India and New Zealand to leverage digitalisation and enhanced information exchange for more efficient, secure and predictable cross-border trade. By enabling the advance electronic exchange of origin data on trade in goods, the arrangement will deepen customs cooperation and support the effective implementation of trade facilitation measures.

The initiative also reflects a forward-looking approach to align bilateral customs cooperation with evolving international practices in digitalisation, information exchange and trade facilitation. The electronic exchange of origin data is expected to improve operational efficiency, reduce information gaps and provide greater certainty to traders engaged in bilateral trade.

Importantly, the arrangement will support the effective utilisation of trade preferences under the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and help ensure that the benefits negotiated under the Agreement reach eligible businesses in both countries more efficiently and with greater certainty.

2326032.title: Pulsing signals reveal hidden structure around a famous neutron star
2326032.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Pulsing signals reveal hidden structure around a famous neutron star
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi

Scientists have discovered that one of the brightest X-ray pulsars, Centaurus X-3 is gobbling up material through an accretion disk, which is rare for pulsars of its kind.

The study will not only have implications in developing better-informed models of the system, which is one of the most widely studied binary pulsars that has drawn the attention of scientists because of its intense brightness, but also lead to enhanced understanding of binary pulsars in general.

An X-ray binary pulsar consists of a pulsar— a highly magnetised neutron star, and a Sun-like star bound in a gravitational dance. A neutron star is a celestial body with the mass of our sun crunched into a ball the size of Bangalore. In an X-ray binary, the pulsar’s extreme gravity pulls in material ejected by its companion star, and the pulsar starts accreting material from it, shooting out X-rays in the process.

Centaurus X-3, a high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) where the companion is more than 10 times the Sun’s mass, was one of the first X-ray pulsars to be discovered, and the third X-ray source to be discovered in the constellation Centaurus, 24000 light years away.

Pulsars emit radiation from their magnetic poles, known as the primary emission. As the pulsar spins, this radiation sweeps past any satellite waiting to detect it. This radiation also falls around the neutron star. Structures in its wider environment (such as the pulsar’s surface, the surface of its companion star, stellar wind blown out from the companion star), absorb and re-emit this radiation, which scientists call the secondary radiation. Studying these structures is important to understand the system’s physical parameters, such as its orientation and magnetic field strength, leading to enhanced understanding of binary pulsars.

Fig 1. An artistic impression of the high-mass X-ray binary system Centaurus X-3. Not to scale.

The problem in studying these intricate structures is that X-ray binaries are so distant that they appear as point sources. The secondary radiation is a promising tool to study these structures.

Earlier studies have found that the intensity of secondary emission lines varied with pulsar rotation. Now scientists from the Raman Research Institute (RRI), an autonomous institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), led by Kinjal Roy, researcher at RRI, investigated four secondary emission lines in depth and found that the structure responsible for the varying lines must be co-rotating with the pulsar.

Like a sleuth trying to deduce facts from observational evidence, Roy detected that it is the accretion stream, which is a structure that channels material from the accretion disk towards the pulsar, that is causing the variability in the secondary emission lines.

An accretion stream can exist only if there’s an accretion disk. The accretion stream ushers material from the accretion disk, which gets funnelled into the pulsar’s poles following its magnetic lines. When the accretion stream obscures the satellite’s view of the pulsar while rotating, the primary emission from the pulsar decreases and the secondary emission from the accretion stream increases.

So, accretion in this system occurs through an accretion disk, which is rare in high-mass binaries. In HMXBs, accretion in general happens through direct capture of stellar wind.

“Accretion disk is not expected to occur in [HMXBs] So, if an accretion disk is forming in this system, emission models have to be modified,” says Roy. “When Centaurus X-3 modelling happens in future work, emission from the disk must be accounted for,” he added.

Fig 2. The accretion stream falling onto the neutron star along its magnetic field lines.

Publication link: DOI 10.3847/1538-4357/adf8e6

2326007.title: From Financial Hardship to Academic Aspirations
2326007.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Hardship to Academic Aspirations
Hanumakonda Telangana’s Arjun Kumar’s Success Story under the NFSC Scheme
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance plays a vital role in helping aspiring scholars overcome economic barriers and pursue higher education.

The journey of Mr. Arjun Kumar (name changed), a doctoral scholar from Hanumakonda district of Telangana, highlights how support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme can help students continue their research and work towards their academic aspirations.

Coming from a financially vulnerable family, Mr. Arjun Kumar faced significant economic and social barriers while pursuing his higher education. Limited financial resources made it difficult for him to sustain his studies and continue his research. Despite these challenges, he remained determined to complete his Ph.D. and fulfil his long-term aspiration of becoming a professor.

A significant change began in 2022, when he started receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme. The fellowship and contingency support helped him manage expenses associated with his doctoral studies and continue his research. This assistance eased the financial pressure that had threatened to interrupt his academic journey and enabled him to remain focused on his studies.

The support has also contributed to an improvement in his financial circumstances. Alongside pursuing his Ph.D., Mr. Arjun Kumar has been able to support his family, helping address an important concern that he faced before receiving the fellowship. The assistance has strengthened his ability to continue working towards his academic goals while contributing to his household’s needs.

The fellowship has brought positive changes to his academic and personal life by helping him continue his research despite financial constraints. It has provided greater financial stability and reinforced his confidence to pursue advanced studies. His experience illustrates how targeted educational support can help scholars navigate financial barriers and remain committed to their long-term goals.

Mr. Arjun Kumar continues to pursue his Ph.D. with the ambition of becoming a professor. His journey reflects the importance of sustained financial assistance in expanding access to higher education and research, while enabling scholars to contribute to their families and to the country’s academic and intellectual development.

2325966.title: Union Minister joins Dr Jitendra Singh joins an e-waste disposal activity at DoPT under Special Campaign 6.0
2325966.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2325966.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Union Minister joins Dr Jitendra Singh joins an e-waste disposal activity at DoPT under Special Campaign 6.0
e-Items disposed today include 152 desktops, 35 printers, 8 scanners, 3 photocopier machines, 59 UPS units, 52 air conditioners, 4 television sets, 5 refrigerators,17 water dispensers, 217 miscellaneous items etc, with base price of Rs 9 lakh
Special Campaign 6.0 is a dedicated one-month exercise to reinforce cleanliness practices and unlock the value of scrap: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Systematic disposal of electronic scrap through GeM Portal, Minister expresses confidence that revenue generated during the campaign will more than double by October 31
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State for PMO, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, today highlighted the importance of systematic disposal of electronic scrap and the need to recognise the residual value of obsolete office equipment, while participating in an e-waste disposal activity at the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) under Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0.

Describing the campaign as a dedicated one-month exercise, Dr. Jitendra Singh said its purpose is to reinforce cleanliness practices and renew commitment to the cause. He explained that the campaign, conducted from Gandhi Jayanti to Patel Jayanti, is not a substitute for cleanliness throughout the year, but an opportunity to reorient and strengthen these practices through focused action.

The Minister said that each successive campaign seeks to incorporate new elements based on the experience of previous editions. One important learning has been the value of scrap generated through the disposal of obsolete electronic equipment and other unused items, which can yield substantial revenue when handled systematically.

Referring to the experience of the current campaign, Dr. Jitendra Singh noted that approximately ₹490 crore had been generated through the disposal of scrap within the first 15–17 days. He expressed confidence that the figure would more than double by October 31.

Highlighting the change in the approach to disposal, the Minister said that scrap was earlier sent to the market without a uniformised process, whereas the present campaign has adopted the GeM Portal for the disposal exercise. This approach reflects the growing recognition that obsolete equipment should not simply be treated as waste, but that its residual value can also be realised.

Dr. Jitendra Singh drew attention to the common practice in offices of discarding an entire computer set when an individual component, such as a mouse or screen, becomes unusable, even when the remaining equipment is intact. He cited the example of 152 desktops and 52 air conditioners in the items identified for disposal, underlining the need to account for the value of equipment that has become obsolete or unused.

As part of the DoPT disposal exercise, three auction notices were floated on the GeM Portal on September 30, 2026, covering obsolete and unused IT items, electrical and electronic items, and furniture. The notices carry separate recommended reserve prices for the three categories.

The IT category comprises 152 desktops, 35 printers, eight scanners, three photocopier machines, 59 UPS units and 217 miscellaneous items, including keyboards and mice.

The electrical and electronic category includes 52 air conditioners, four televisions, five refrigerators and 17 water dispensers. The furniture category includes chairs, tables, almirahs, sofas, drawers and workstations, among other items. The three categories of obsolete items put together carry a combined recommended reserve price of about ₹9 lakh.

The disposal exercise forms part of the Department's activities under Special Campaign 6.0, combining the objective of cleanliness with the systematic disposal of obsolete assets and the realisation of their residual value. Secretary, DoPT, Ms. Rachna Shah, along with other senior officials of the Department, also participated in the event

Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Armed Forces Headquarters Association (AFHQ) appreciates timely promotions under PM Narendra Modi’s Leadership; Discusses employee issues with Dr Jitendra Singh
AFHQ thanks the DoPT Ministry for giving them appointment to convey their concerns even at a short notice whenever they ask for it
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh heard the issues raised by the Association and assured to address these through appropriate administrative channels
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 3:38PM by PIB Delhi

A delegation of the Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Association expressed appreciation for timely promotions being undertaken by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as well as for the opportunity provided to employee associations to present their service-related concerns regularly from time to time.

The delegation conveyed its appreciation during a meeting with Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, who heard the issues raised by the association and discussed their examination through the appropriate administrative channels.

Led by Pavan Kumar National General Secretary (Org) Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh, Pankaj Yadav, General Secretary of the AFHQ Association, affiliated with the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS) and GENC, the delegation raised issues concerning employees serving at Armed Forces Headquarters, particularly the Section Officer cadre, promotional avenues and compassionate appointments for eligible dependants of deceased employees.

The delegation stated that against the vacancies projected through the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the Section Officer cadre during 2018–2024, very few candidates had joined. Therefore, the delegation members proposed that this concern may be addressed after appropriate consideration.

Dr. Jitendra Singh asked that the feasibility of rationalising the existing recruitment quota be examined in consultation with the concerned officials, keeping in view actual recruitment patterns and the substantial number of vacancies remaining unfilled. The Minister asked that the matter be examined further before arriving at a view on the appropriate arrangement.

The delegation also raised concerns regarding compassionate appointments for eligible dependents of deceased employees, including delays in consideration of cases, the existing 5 per cent quota and the criteria used to assess eligibility. The discussion covered the difficulties faced by families awaiting appointments and the implications of the applicable restrictions. Dr Jitendra Singh discussed the need to consider the prescribed eligibility conditions and assessment criteria, while taking into account the administrative and legal implications of any proposed change.

The interaction focused on examining the issues raised by the AFHQ Association through the concerned authorities, particularly the recruitment arrangements affecting promotional opportunities and the implementation of compassionate appointment provisions. No final decision on changing the recruitment quota or compassionate appointment rules was announced during the meeting.

2325933.title: MOD INKS ₹ 770 Cr CONTRACT TO PROCURE IMPROVED LOW LEVEL LIGHT WEIGHT RADARS FOR INDIAN ARMY
2325933.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
MOD INKS ₹ 770 Cr CONTRACT TO PROCURE IMPROVED LOW LEVEL LIGHT WEIGHT RADARS FOR INDIAN ARMY
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Defence has signed a contract with M/s Bharat Electronic Limited (BEL) to procure Improved Low Level Light Weight Radar (LLLR-I) at a cost of approximately ₹ 770 Cr in the presence of the Defence Secretary, Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi on October 21, 2026.

The LLLR(I) system has the capability of detecting and tracking fighter size targets and mini/ micro drones, it has additional capability of prioritizing aerial targets. This will enable the Army to successfully counter the threat of the Unmanned Aerial System (UAS).

Aligning with the Government’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, the procurement is a significant step towards indigenization of Air Defence platforms with a boost to India’s Defence manufacturing ecosystem, including Micro Small & Medium Enterprises and building a resilient, self-reliant and globally competitive Defence Industry.

2325915.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS LALIT KALA AKADEMI AWARDS TO SELECTED ARTISTS OF THE 65TH NATIONAL EXHIBITION OF ART
2325915.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS LALIT KALA AKADEMI AWARDS TO SELECTED ARTISTS OF THE 65TH NATIONAL EXHIBITION OF ART
LET US PROVIDE AMPLE OPPORTUNITIES TO YOUNG AND EMERGING ARTISTS TO DEVELOP THEIR TALENT, EXPLORE NEW MEDIUMS, AND EXPAND THEIR CREATIVE POTENTIAL: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented Lalit Kala Akademi awards to selected artists of the 65th National Exhibition of Art in New Delhi today (October 21, 2026). She also felicitated Grand Prize winners and Honourable Mentions of the 3rd Print Biennale India, 2026.

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that this award presentation ceremony is a celebration of India’s artistic heritage, cultural diversity, and contemporary creativity. Through this event, we are celebrating the rich tradition of India’s diverse arts, its creative energy, and its ever-evolving artistic expressions.

The President said that art is not limited to paintings on a canvas, sculptures carved from stone, or works created through various other mediums. Art is a reflection of our culture. It reflects the memories, experiences of the present, and aspirations for the future. Art enables us to perceive and understand our times and society from a fresh perspective. She emphasised the need to equip traditional artists in remote areas with training in new technologies and contemporary art techniques, enabling them to showcase their skills and participate in competitions on a wider platform.

The President said that in today’s world, artists require not only creative opportunities but also financial support, access to a broader market, and connections with art collectors. She was happy to note that the Lalit Kala Akademi and the Ministry of Culture are making efforts to encourage the sale of artworks.

The President said that art should not be confined to art galleries. It should reach schools, universities, public spaces, and broader segments of society. She urged all stakeholders to provide ample opportunities to young and emerging artists to develop their talent, explore new mediums, and expand their creative potential.

Please click here to see the President’s Speech

2325911.title: ARMY COMMANDERS’ CONFERENCE COMMENCES TODAY
2325911.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
ARMY COMMANDERS’ CONFERENCE COMMENCES TODAY
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Army Commanders’ Conference, the apex-level biannual forum of the Indian Army, commenced today. Chaired by the Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), the conference is being held in New Delhi from 21 to 23 October 2026. It brings together the senior leadership of the Indian Army, to deliberate the evolving security environment, operational preparedness, capability development and future-ready transformation initiatives.

The conference will be addressed by Shri Rajnath Singh, the Hon’ble Raksha Mantri. Further, the Chief of Defence Staff, Chief of the Naval Staff, Secretary (Electronic and Information Technology), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology will deliver talks on contemporary security-related issues.

A key highlight of the conference will be the release of the Land Warfare Doctrine by the Hon’ble Raksha Mantri. The doctrine will provide an overarching framework to prepare the Indian Army to meet the challenges posed by the evolving character of warfare and future conflicts. The Hon’ble Raksha Mantri will also unveil the annual United Nations Journal and felicitate Indian Army personnel who have made notable contributions while serving as United Nations peacekeepers, recognising their exemplary service, professionalism and contribution to international peace and security under the United Nations banner.

To recognise excellence in environmental sustainability, resource management and the promotion of a strong aviation safety culture, the COAS will also confer awards for Green Military Stations and Aviation Flight Safety.

With its comprehensive agenda, the conference will provide an important forum for the senior leadership of the Indian Army to review ongoing initiatives, identify future thrust areas and formulate appropriate policy directions towards building a progressive, adaptive, technologically enabled and future-ready Indian Army.

2325908.title: Prime Minister condoles the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji
2325908.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister condoles the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today expressed deep sadness over the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji, who will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

Recalling the honour of meeting him in 2023 when the government gave the Sengol a place of pride in the new Parliament building, Shri Modi stated that his life and craftsmanship represent a remarkable connection between India's glorious traditions and the national journey, and extended his heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"Deeply saddened by the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji. Hailing from a distinguished family based in Tamil Nadu, he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to Former Prime Minister Nehru. Many years later, in 2023, it was our Government which had the honour of giving the Sengol a place of pride in the new Parliament building. During that time, I had the honour of meeting Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji and expressing gratitude for what he has done for our nation and culture. His life and craftsmanship represent a remarkable connection between India's glorious traditions and our national journey. My heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers. Om Shanti.

திரு உம்மிடி எத்திராஜ் அவர்களின் மறைவை அறிந்து மிகவும் வேதனையடைந்தேன். தமிழ்நாட்டை பூர்வீகமாகக் கொண்ட ஒரு பாரம்பரியமிக்க  குடும்பத்திலிருந்து வந்த இவர், முன்னாள் பிரதமர் நேருவுக்கு வழங்கப்பட்ட வரலாற்றுச் சிறப்புமிக்க செங்கோலை வடிவமைத்தமைக்காக என்றும் நினைவுகூரப்படுவார். பல ஆண்டுகளுக்குப் பின்பு, 2023-ல், புதிய நாடாளுமன்றக் கட்டடத்தில் அந்த செங்கோலுக்கு உரிய கௌரவத்தை வழங்கி சிறப்பிக்கும் வாய்ப்பு எங்கள் அரசுக்கு கிடைத்தது. அப்போது திரு உம்மிடி எத்திராஜ் அவர்களை சந்தித்து, நமது நாட்டிற்கும் கலாச்சாரத்திற்கும் அவர் ஆற்றிய பங்களிப்பிற்காக நன்றி தெரிவிக்கும் பாக்கியம் எனக்குக் கிடைத்தது. அவரது வாழ்க்கையும், கலைத்திறனும், இந்தியாவின் பெருமைமிக்க வளமான பாரம்பரியத்திற்கும் நமது நாட்டின் வளர்ச்சிப் பயணத்திற்கும் இடையிலான போற்றத்தக்க தொடர்பை பிரதிபலிக்கின்றன. அவரது குடும்பத்தினருக்கும், ஆதரவாளர்களுக்கும் எனது ஆழ்ந்த இரங்கலைத் தெரிவித்துக் கொள்கிறேன். ஓம் சாந்தி."
