2324489.title: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will confer the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025 on 19th October 2026 in New Delhi
2324489.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will confer the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025 on 19th October 2026 in New Delhi
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Government of India will confer the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025 to 106 young artists in the field of music, dance and drama on 19 October 2026 at 10 a.m. at Meghdoot Complex, Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi.

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, will be the Guest of Honour and Dr. Sandhya Purecha, Chairman, Sangeet Natak Akademi will preside over the award ceremony.

The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar was instituted by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2006 to recognize young artists up to the age of 40. Since then, these awards have been presented annually to young artists at a special ceremony.

 The General Council of Sangeet Natak Akademi, at its meeting held from 22-26 March 2026 at New Delhi unanimously selected 106 young artists for Sangeet Natak Akademi, Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for the years 2024 and 2025.   

The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar carries a purse money of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees twenty-five thousand only) besides a Tamrapatra and an Angavastram.

2324475.title: Two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms begins in Dharamshala
2324475.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2324475.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms begins in Dharamshala
Chief Minister, Himachal Pradesh, Secretary, DARPG & Chief Secretary, Himachal Pradesh address the Inaugural Session
Day One highlights Digital Innovation, Emerging Technologies and Citizen-Centric Governance
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms kick-started today in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh, bringing together representatives of the Central, State/UT Governments and experts to deliberate on digital transformation, innovative governance practices and technology-enabled public service delivery.

The inaugural session featured a welcome address by Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG, Government of India, followed by addresses by Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant, Chief Secretary, Government of Himachal Pradesh, and Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh. Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG, delivered the vote of thanks.

In his address, the Chief Minister said, the reforms must be brought about to ensure the welfare of the beneficiaries and modern technology can prove to be a key instrument in addressing the future challenges. He said that the state Government was focusing on good governance and the departments must make earnest efforts to provide quality services to the people of the State nearer to their homes. He applauded Union Minister of State (PP) Dr Jitendra Singh and DARPG for organising the conference in Himachal Pradesh.

Citing nominations received under National Awards for e-Governance and the Prime Minister's Awards, Secretary DARPG in her address highlighted the innovative work done by Districts, States and Ministries to make governance more robust and citizen centric. She underlined that the challenge before the government was to scale up such practices and to take an innovation that works in one place and make it work in many places. She emphasized that closing the distance between a successful pilot and a national practice was the objective of the National Conference.

Expressing gratitude to the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh and the state administration for their support and hospitality in hosting the conference, the Secretary noted the visionary leadership and continuous guidance provided by Union Minister of State (PP) Dr. Jitendra Singh in driving DARPG’s governance initiatives. Acknowledgment was also extended to Union Minister for Health Shri J. P. Nadda. Both the ministers have  conveyed their best wishes for the National Conference.

Chief Secretary of Government of Himachal Pradesh, Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant highlighted how e-governance is enabling citizens to access government services at their doorsteps. He outlined various initiatives undertaken by the Himachal Pradesh government and explained how digital governance is helping reduce procedural hurdles. He emphasised that the objective is to eliminate barriers, promote equality and ensure that public services reach people more efficiently.

The session brought together senior leadership from the Central and State Governments for deliberations on governance reforms and the role of digital innovation in public administration.

The Day One of the Conference showcased five key initiatives of the Government of Himachal Pradesh, including Him Parivar, Sukhashraya, Vidya Samiksha Kendra (VSK), Green Himachal and the Rajiv Gandhi Van Samvardhan Yojna. The presentations highlighted the range of governance initiatives being undertaken across sectors such as health, social justice, education, environment and forest conservation.

The other sessions featured presentations on award-recognised initiatives demonstrating the use of digital platforms, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in governance. The initiatives included AgriStack, e-Jagriti, the AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support System in e-Sanjeevani Telemedicine Service, the Multi Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System and iGOT Karmayogi. The presentations wer  also made on eAarogya Dhamni, the District Court Case Management System (DCMS), ICMR-MINDS, the India Hypertension Control Initiative and Digi Yatra.

Day Two of the conference, scheduled for 17 October 2026, will feature sessions on cybersecurity, best e-governance practices, replication, data analytics, and State-, district- and grassroots-level initiatives, followed by the valedictory session.

The National Conference on e-Governance Reforms seeks to strengthen the exchange of ideas and experiences among government institutions and promote effective, innovative and citizen-centric governance through digital transformation.

2324472.title: PM-AJAY Drives Inclusive Development Through Adarsh Grams, Socio-Economic Projects and Educational Infrastructure
2324472.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
PM-AJAY Drives Inclusive Development Through Adarsh Grams, Socio-Economic Projects and Educational Infrastructure
18,093 villages declared Adarsh Grams; Approximately Rs 1,730 Crore released under Grant In Aid directly to States And Districts
785 student hostels completed; Rs 61.46 Crore Allocated For FY 2026-27 for two hostel projects Accommodating 264 Boys/ Girls Students
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Adarsh Gram component of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, over 47,200 villages benefiting more than 47.79 lakh citizens across the country, have been covered. In addition, a total of 46,944 development works have been completed, while 27,032 Village Development Plans (VDPs) have been prepared, under the PM AJAY.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said as on September 8, 2026, 18,093 villages had been declared Adarsh Grams which reflects continued efforts of the Ministry to improve infrastructure, basic services and the quality of life in Scheduled Caste-majority villages.

He said the Scheduled Caste-dominated villages are being developed as model villages by addressing critical gaps in infrastructure and essential services and an ‘Adarsh Gram’ is envisioned as a village where people have access to basic services, the minimum needs of all sections of society are met and disparities are reduced to a minimum.

The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) implemented by the Ministry, is advancing the socio-economic and educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities through infrastructure development, livelihood promotion, education and improved access to basic services.

The Official informed that the Scheme has three components including development of Scheduled Caste-dominated villages into ‘Adarsh Grams’, Grants-in-Aid for socio-economic projects at the State and District levels, and construction and repair of hostels.

He stated that the Grants-in-Aid component provides financial assistance for district and State-level projects aimed at the socio-economic advancement of Scheduled Castes. It focuses on increasing the income of the target population through comprehensive livelihood projects, skill development and related infrastructure, he added.

He said it also seeks to improve socio-economic development indicators by creating adequate infrastructure in Scheduled Caste-dominated villages and to promote literacy and school enrolment among Scheduled Caste students through residential schools wherever required.

The Official said an approximately Rs 1,730 Crore was released directly to States under this component during FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26. The support has extended skilling and livelihood opportunities to more than 2.5 lakh individual and group beneficiaries, he added.

The Official further said under the PM-AJAY’s component of construction and repair of hostels, the Ministry pursues enabling and encouraging Scheduled Caste students to pursue quality education as these hostels are particularly beneficial for students from rural and remote areas by providing access to accommodation and educational opportunities.

He said as of September 2026, a total of 785 student hostels had been completed under the scheme. For FY 2026-27, the Government has allocated Rs 61.46 crore in central assistance for two hostel projects—one for girls and one for boys—which will provide accommodation for 264 students, he further said.

The Ministry Official further said a major step towards strengthening implementation and monitoring has been the launch of the PM-AJAY Mobile App and PM-AJAY Portal, facilitating a transition from paper-based workflows to end-to-end digital processing on a real-time basis.

He said technology-enabled governance is strengthening information access, monitoring and data-driven decision-making under the scheme while as the digital framework is also aimed at improving coordination, transparency, accountability and efficiency in the delivery of welfare interventions.

The Official further stated that PM-AJAY is a 100 per cent Centrally Funded Scheme, while States and Union Territories may supplement it with additional resources wherever required. Under the funding framework, up to 50 per cent of funds may be utilised for gap-filling activities in selected Adarsh Gram villages. Up to 5 per cent is allocated for setting up and operating Technical Support Groups and Project Implementation Units at the Central, State and District levels. Up to 2 per cent is earmarked for construction and repair of hostels, including support for Central Institutions, while the remaining funds are provided as Grants-in-Aid for projects at the District and State levels.

Grants-in-Aid allocations take into account factors including the Scheduled Caste population and the ratio of State SCSP to the Annual Plan in relation to the Scheduled Caste population of States and Union Territories. Following completion of infrastructure projects, their maintenance and operation are to be undertaken by the concerned State Governments or implementing agencies. Under the hostel component, the Government of India also provides central assistance for maintenance.

As India progresses towards Viksit Bharat @2047, ensuring that the benefits of development reach every section of society remains central to the nation’s development journey.

PM-AJAY contributes to this objective by addressing multiple dimensions of empowerment—from village infrastructure and basic services to livelihoods, skill development and access to education.

With greater use of technology, stronger monitoring mechanisms and focused last-mile delivery, the scheme continues to strengthen opportunities for Scheduled Caste communities to participate more fully in India’s growth and development. Its integrated approach is helping create the infrastructure, capabilities and enabling environment required for individuals and communities to realise their full potential.

2324455.title: ECL generates ₹2.21 crore through scrap disposal under Special Campaign 6
2324455.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
ECL generates ₹2.21 crore through scrap disposal under Special Campaign 6
62,720 sq. ft. of space cleared; over 3,000 e-files reviewed
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, has generated revenue of ₹2.21 crore through scrap disposal and cleared 62,720 square feet of space under Special Campaign 6, aimed at improving workplace cleanliness, resource utilisation and administrative efficiency.

According to the progress report for October 2–16, the Coal India subsidiary disposed of 413.5 metric tonnes of scrap against an identified quantity of 850 metric tonnes. The disposal of iron scrap on October 14 generated ₹2,21,31,359, contributing to resource recovery and the productive utilisation of obsolete materials.

The company has undertaken cleanliness activities at 10 identified locations, clearing 62,720 sq. ft. of space against a target of 2,08,052 sq. ft., achieving around 30 per cent of the targeted area.

On the administrative front, ECL reviewed 647 physical files against a target of 1,200 and weeded out 567 obsolete files against a target of 1,000. The exercise aims to reduce redundant records, optimise office space and strengthen records management.

Significant progress was also recorded in digital file management, with 3,098 e-files reviewed against a target of 3,800, representing over 81 per cent achievement. Of the 3,600 e-files identified for closure, 2,148 have been closed, achieving nearly 60 per cent of the target.

The campaign forms part of ECL's broader efforts to institutionalise cleanliness, streamline administrative processes and promote the efficient utilisation of resources across its establishments.

2324440.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and inhuman treatment of a woman by her husband and family members enraged by her living with another man in Surendranagar district, Gujarat
2324440.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and inhuman treatment of a woman by her husband and family members enraged by her living with another man in Surendranagar district, Gujarat
Notices issued to the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Sundranagar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include the status of the victim's health and compensation, if any, paid to her
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a married woman, who had been living with another man, was subjected to cruel and inhuman treatment by her husband and family in Surendranagar district, Gujarat. Reportedly, the woman and the man were tracked and brought back under the guise of conducting a 'purification ritual'. The woman was beaten with sticks, kicked and tied to a tree. The accused also allegedly forced the man accompanying her to rape her.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Accordingly, it has issued notices to the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Surendranagar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the status of the victim's health and compensation, if any, paid to her.

According to the media report, carried on 8th October 2026, the incident came to light when the video of the incident was circulated on social media.

2324436.title: NHRC, India takes <i>suo motu<i/> cognizance of the reported injuries to three students after a portion of the ceiling plaster of a classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government school in Udaipur district, Rajasthan
2324436.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported injuries to three students after a portion of the ceiling plaster of a classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government school in Udaipur district, Rajasthan
Issues a notice to the Udaipur District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include the health status of the injured students
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that three students, aged 7 to 8 years, were injured when a portion of the ceiling plaster of their classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government primary school building in Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Reportedly, the victims sustained head injuries and teachers were not present in the school when the incident occurred. The injured students walked home on their own and their family members subsequently took them to the hospital for treatment.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Udaipur District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the health status of the injured students.

According to the media report carried on 7th October 2026, the school was ordered to close after the incident and alternate arrangements are being made by the authorities for conducting classes. Reportedly, the school building was last repaired in 2020.

2324416.title: NHAI Successfully Defends Arbitration Case in Chittorgarh–Udaipur National Highway Project to Safeguard Public Funds
2324416.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Successfully Defends Arbitration Case in Chittorgarh–Udaipur National Highway Project to Safeguard Public Funds
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

Achieving a significant legal victory, NHAI has successfully defended its contractual position in an arbitration case against concessionaire Uchit Expressway Private Limited, promoted by TRIL Roads Pvt. Ltd. for six-laning of the 93.5 km long Chittorgarh-Udaipur section of NH-76 in Rajasthan. The Arbitral Tribunal substantially upheld the position of NHAI, thereby safeguarding public resources and reaffirming the contractual framework governing National Highway projects.

The three-member Arbitral Tribunal under the Society for Affordable Redressal of Disputes (SAROD), examined claims and counterclaims arising out of the concession agreement for the project. The Tribunal rejected overall concessionaire claims of Rs. 366.53 crores, which included Rs. 238.18 crore of prolongation cost claim tied to COVID-19 by the concessionaire. After detailed consideration, the Tribunal rejected the claim for prolongation cost and allowed claims amounting to only Rs. 14.51 crore along with conditional refund of Rs. 2.82 Crores to the concessionaire. 

In addition, the Tribunal awarded Rs. 33.54 crore (principal) in counter-claims to NHAI. This ruling in favour of NHAI includes Rs. 27 crore for recovery of work dropped from the project scope, Rs. 4.03 crore toward failure to maintain the highway and Rs. 2.51 crore towards unauthorized toll collected after the completion date of the project, in March 2021.

In a series of recent notable legal wins, NHAI has successfully defended various arbitration cases. In July 2026, NHAI successfully defended claims of around Rs. 3,177 crores in the arbitration proceedings pertaining to Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL).Similarly, in June 2026, arbitration case related to Tumkur–Chitradurga 6 laning Project in Karnataka, was awarded in favour of NHAI for Rs. 1,202 crores. Also in April 2026, two arbitration cases in Panipat–Jalandhar Highway Project involving Concessionaire’s claims of around Rs. 8,375 Crores and counterclaims of NHAI for Rs. 2,888.64 Crores were settled for Rs. 819.96 Crores in favour of NHAI. Similarly in May 2026, arbitration case related to 6 laning of Kamrej–Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat in which claims of around Rs. 174.49 crore raised by the contractor, was settled for only Rs. 54 lakhs by the Arbitral Tribunal.

The successful resolution of arbitration cases reflects NHAI’s commitment to sound contractual management and effective legal strategy. It also reaffirms NHAI’s focus on the proper utilization of public funds, while upholding transparency, accountability and contractual discipline in the development and management of National Highway infrastructure.

2324413.title: Ministry of Mines Showcases Sustainable Best Practices during the First Fortnight of Special Campaign 6
2324413.body_html:
Ministry of Mines
Ministry of Mines Showcases Sustainable Best Practices during the First Fortnight of Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Mines and its field offices have undertaken several initiatives during the first fortnight of Special Campaign 6, launched on 2 October 2026, to promote sustainability, cleanliness and responsible resource management. With a focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, the Ministry and its field organisations are making concerted efforts to adopt environmentally sustainable practices and innovative approaches to resource conservation.

During the first fortnight, organisations under the Ministry implemented several noteworthy best practices to advance environmental sustainability and workplace excellence. Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) inaugurated a rainwater harvesting initiative at Khetri Copper Complex (KCC), Rajasthan, to promote water conservation and sustainable water management. A plantation drive was also undertaken at Indian Copper Complex (ICC), Jharkhand, under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative to enhance green cover and promote environmental protection. The Geological Survey of India (GSI), Central Headquarters, Kolkata, has discontinued the use of single-use plastic water bottles in all official meetings, conferences and videoconferencing halls, replacing them with reusable stainless-steel or metal water bottles and glass jugs. National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO) introduced a Clean Desk & Workplace Excellence Competition among employees to promote workplace cleanliness and organised workspaces, along with the One Employee, One Green Initiative to encourage individual participation in environmental conservation. The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) undertook various Waste-to-Wealth/art initiatives including transforming barren and unutilised space near hospital into attractive green spaces and gardens and promoting the productive use of available resources.

As part of the e-waste management drive, the Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research Development and Design Centre (JNARDDC), in association with the Materials Recycling Association of India (MRAI), is facilitating e-waste collection drive across various locations. So far, 3,020 kg of e-waste has been collected, and ₹3,07,855 has been disbursed by recyclers. E-waste collected at various participating locations will be channelled for responsible recycling and recovery of critical minerals through appropriate mechanisms, thereby promoting the circular economy and ensuring environmentally sound disposal of discarded electronic equipment.

The progress achieved during the first fortnight of Special Campaign 6.0 reflects the collective efforts of organisations under the Ministry to promote sustainable workplace practices, strengthen environmental responsibility and contribute to a cleaner and greener future.

Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Mid-Campaign Progress of Department of Food and Public Distribution under Special Campaign 6

2324400.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah says Punjab is today grappling with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism and organized crime
2324400.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah says Punjab is today grappling with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism and organized crime
The biggest question before the Punjab government is - who will ultimately take responsibility for the security of Punjab's people
In Dirba, a father consuming poison under pressure, and the broad daylight murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota, who had been raising his voice against drugs in Mansa, have raised serious questions about the law & order situation in Punjab
Parvinder’s father has levelled serious allegations against the Punjab government and their MLA; MHA will seek response from the state government on both these incidents
Drug trade is flourishing in Punjab, the threat of organised crime is rising, and questions are being raised about the safety of those who speak out against drugs
There should be a decisive crackdown on the drug network and an impartial probe into any political patronage being extended to criminals
Our goal is clear – crackdown against drugs, protection of our youth's future, strict action against criminals, and a fear-less Punjab 
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah has said that Punjab is today grappling with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism, and organized crime.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah in a post on X said that Punjab is today grappling with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism, and organized crime. The biggest question before the Punjab government is - who will ultimately take responsibility for the security of Punjab's people? In Dirba, a father taking poison under pressure, and in Mansa, the broad-daylight murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota, who had raised his voice against drugs, have raised serious questions about law & order in Punjab. Parvinder's father has levelled grave allegations against the Punjab government and their MLA. The Ministry of Home Affairs will also seek responses from the Punjab government on both these incidents. In Punjab, the drug trade is flourishing, the threat of organized crime is growing, and questions are being raised about the safety of those who speak out against drugs. Mr. Chief Minister, the people of Punjab do not want publicity - they want answers; not announcements, but results; decisive crackdown against drug networks, and an impartial probe into any political patronage provided to criminals. Our goal is clear – crackdown against the drug trade, protection of our youth's future, strict action against criminals, and the rule of law in such a way that no citizen is forced to live under the shadow of fear. 

पंजाब आज नशे, गैंगस्टरवाद व संगठित अपराध के बढ़ते खतरे से जूझ रहा है। भगवंत मान सरकार के सामने सबसे बड़ा सवाल है कि आखिर पंजाब की जनता की सुरक्षा की जिम्मेदारी कौन निभाएगा? दिरबा में एक पिता का दबाव में जहर खा लेना और मानसा में नशे के खिलाफ आवाज उठाने वाले परविंदर सिंह झोटा की दिनदहाड़े हत्या ने पंजाब की कानून-व्यवस्था पर गंभीर सवाल खड़े कर दिए हैं। परविंदर के पिता ने AAP सरकार और उनके विधायक पर गंभीर आरोप लगाए हैं। गृह मंत्रालय भी इन दोनों घटनाओं पर पंजाब सरकार से जवाब माँगेगा। पंजाब में नशे का कारोबार फल-फूल रहा है, संगठित अपराध का खतरा बढ़ रहा है और नशे के खिलाफ आवाज उठाने वालों की सुरक्षा पर सवाल खड़े हो रहे हैं। भगवंत मान जी, पंजाब की जनता को प्रचार नहीं, जवाब, घोषणाएँ नहीं, परिणाम, नशे के नेटवर्क पर निर्णायक प्रहार और अपराधियों को मिलने वाले किसी भी राजनीतिक संरक्षण की निष्पक्ष जाँच चाहिए। मैं आज पंजाब की जनता के सामने अपना संकल्प दोहराता हूँ कि पंजाब में हमारी सरकार बनने पर हम नशामुक्त, गैंगस्टरमुक्त और सुरक्षित पंजाब बनाने के लिए पूरी ताकत से काम करेंगे। हमारा लक्ष्य स्पष्ट है - नशे के कारोबार पर प्रहार, युवाओं के भविष्य की रक्षा, अपराधियों पर कठोर कार्रवाई और कानून का ऐसा राज, जिसमें कोई भी नागरिक भय के साये में जीने को मजबूर न हो।

2324393.title: DFS Organises Workshop on Reservation Policy for Public Sector Banks, Public Sector Insurance Companies and Public Financial Institutions
2324393.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DFS Organises Workshop on Reservation Policy for Public Sector Banks, Public Sector Insurance Companies and Public Financial Institutions
Over 100 participants from PSBs, PSICs, PFIs and Sectoral Regulators Participate in Deliberations on Uniform Implementation of Reservation Policies
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, convened a two-day workshop on the implementation of the Government of India's Reservation Policy in Public Sector Banks (PSBs), Public Sector Insurance Companies (PSICs), Sectoral Regulators and Public Financial Institutions (PFIs) on 15–16 October 2026 at the Punjab National Bank Staff Training College, Panchkula.

The workshop was organised in association with Punjab National Bank with the objective of strengthening institutional capacity to ensure the uniform and effective implementation of reservation policies and promote welfare measures across public financial institutions.

The workshop was attended by over 100 participants, including senior Human Resource functionaries and CLOs/LOs from various organisations under DFS, including all Public Sector Banks, Public Sector Insurance Companies and Public Sector Financial Institutions, as well as representatives from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), and Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI).

Functional experts on reservation matters addressed the workshop, and the deliberations included practical aspects and issues faced in the implementation of the reservation policy. The workshop concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session, allowing participants to deliberate on actionable measures for the uniform implementation of reservation policies across the financial services ecosystem.

2324319.title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Commissions Indian Navy’s First Indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel INS Samarthak at Karwar
2324319.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Commissions Indian Navy’s First Indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel INS Samarthak at Karwar
INS Samarthak, with over 75 per cent indigenous content, reflects India’s growing self-reliance in defence manufacturing: Vice-President
“Indian Navy Stands Ever-Vigilant and Combat-Ready to Safeguard India’s Maritime Interests”: Vice-President
“INS Samarthak Reflects the Growing Role of India’s Private Shipbuilding Industry”: Vice-President
“Karwar Symbolises Both India’s Glorious Maritime Heritage and Its Maritime Future”: Vice-President
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today commissioned INS Samarthak, the Indian Navy’s first indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel, at Karwar, Karnataka. The commissioning marks a significant milestone in India’s journey towards self-reliance in defence manufacturing and the development of advanced indigenous naval capabilities.

 

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today commissioned INS Samarthak, the Indian Navy’s first indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel, at Karwar, Karnataka. With over 75% indigenous content, INS Samarthak reflects India’s growing self-reliance in defence manufacturing and will support trials of next-generation weapons, sensors and unmanned systems. A significant milestone towards a stronger, technologically advanced and Aatmanirbhar Indian Navy.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 16, 2026


Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that INS Samarthak, with more than 75 per cent indigenous content, reflects the growing strength of India’s industrial, technological and shipbuilding capabilities. He observed that self-reliance in defence is no longer merely an aspiration but an emerging reality, contributing to India’s strategic autonomy and the vision of a Viksit and Aatmanirbhar Bharat articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Highlighting India’s rich maritime heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the naval traditions of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and the Chola dynasty, which extended India’s maritime influence across the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia.

The Vice-President commended the Indian Navy for its distinguished service in safeguarding national sovereignty and maritime interests. He also appreciated its role as a first responder and a preferred security partner in the Indian Ocean Region, including anti-piracy operations, the evacuation of Indian citizens and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief missions.

Highlighting the significance of INS Samarthak, the Vice-President said that the vessel will serve as a versatile platform for trials and evaluation of next-generation weapons, sensors and emerging technologies. Its capabilities will also support maritime surveillance and reconnaissance, offshore patrolling, launch and recovery of targets, operations involving unmanned systems, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. He observed that such a platform would enable the Navy to adapt more rapidly to emerging technological developments and translate indigenous innovation into operational capabilities.

Referring to Karwar’s strategic importance, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that its deep natural harbour and proximity to the Arabian Sea make it a vital component of India’s maritime security architecture. He highlighted the ongoing development of modern naval infrastructure under Project Seabird, which is enhancing the Navy’s capacity to base and sustain ships and submarines while generating wider economic opportunities for the region.

The Vice-President also underscored the growing partnership between the Indian Navy, defence public sector undertakings, private shipyards, DRDO, academia, MSMEs and start-ups in strengthening India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem. Appreciating Larsen & Toubro (L&T) for its contribution to the project, he acknowledged the efforts of naval designers, production authorities, shipyard professionals, engineers, technicians, suppliers and ancillary industries in building indigenous naval capabilities.

Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff; Vice-Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief; Vice-Admiral Sanjay Sadhu, Controller Warship Production and Acquisition; Rear Admiral Vikram Menon, Flag Officer (Karnataka); retired Rear Admiral G. K. Harish, Head of Shipbuilding, L&T; Commander Sushil Kumar Singh, Commanding Officer of INS Samarthak; senior officers of the Indian Navy and Ministry of Defence, and other distinguished guests were present on the occasion.

2324307.title: TDB-DST signs agreement with QNu Labs for ₹150 crore RDI support to strengthen India’s indigenous quantum-secure technology ecosystem
2324307.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST signs agreement with QNu Labs for ₹150 crore RDI support to strengthen India’s indigenous quantum-secure technology ecosystem
Project to advance a sovereign technology stack for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks, targeting TRL-9
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 2:50PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening India’s capabilities in quantum technologies and secure communications, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with QNu Labs Private Limited, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹150 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.

The project, with a total cost of ₹300 crore, aims to develop an indigenous technology backbone for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks (IQSN). The programme will advance a portfolio of technologies from Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 4–5 towards TRL-9, supporting the development, integration and validation of a sovereign quantum-security and sensing technology stack. The financial support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).

As digital infrastructure becomes increasingly interconnected, securing the authenticity of devices, the integrity of navigation systems, the reliability of time synchronisation and the confidentiality of communications is emerging as a critical technological priority. Quantum technologies offer new approaches to addressing these challenges, particularly in applications where conventional security mechanisms may face limitations from evolving cyber and technological threats. QNu Labs’ proposed programme seeks to address these requirements through an integrated framework built around four pillars: identity security, location integrity, network security and time integrity. The programme brings together complementary capabilities to establish a unified foundation for sovereign security and sensing infrastructure.

Under the identity security pillar, the programme envisages quantum-secure physical unclonable functions (PUFs) and quantum-safe trusted platform modules (TPMs) to support hardware-based device identity, authentication and cryptographic security. These technologies are intended to strengthen trust at the device level and reduce vulnerabilities associated with compromised or replicated identities. The location integrity pillar focuses on technologies designed to support trusted navigation and detect attempts to manipulate or spoof positioning systems. The proposed work includes compact quantum magnetometers for electromagnetic tampering detection and GPS-denied navigation capabilities, with potential applications in defence and other mission-critical platforms.

Under network security, the programme seeks to advance a quantum-secure communications ecosystem through chip-based quantum key distribution (QKD), satellite-based QKD and supporting technologies such as quantum-secure communication modules and encryption systems. The objective is to develop deployable capabilities for secure communications across terrestrial and long-distance networks.

The fourth pillar, time integrity, focuses on indigenous high-precision timing infrastructure, including atomic clock technology and secure time synchronisation using QKD-authenticated distribution. Reliable and tamper-resistant time synchronisation is essential for telecommunications, financial systems, critical infrastructure and defence applications. Together, these four pillars are intended to contribute to an integrated quantum trust framework supporting device authenticity, secure communications, trusted navigation and tamper-resistant timing. The programme will involve further research, engineering refinement, system integration and validation to progress the technologies towards higher levels of readiness and deployment.

Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said: “Quantum technologies are opening new possibilities for addressing complex challenges in cybersecurity, communications, navigation and critical infrastructure. Building indigenous capabilities across these interconnected domains is important for strengthening India’s technological self-reliance and long-term security. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting the development and maturation of advanced technologies that require sustained investment to progress from research and engineering to integrated, deployable systems.”

Founder of QNu Labs Private Limited said: “Quantum technologies will shape how nations protect their communications, devices, navigation and timing systems. TDB’s support under the RDI Fund allows us to accelerate our R&D roadmap beyond quantum security stack. Our work will focus on four connected areas: device identity, location integrity, network security and time integrity, so that trust is built into infrastructure from the hardware upwards. This programme extends quantum security foundation into chip-based and satellite-based QKD, quantum sensing and AI. We see this partnership as a responsibility: to deliver indigenous capabilities that India’s defence, telecom, financial and critical infrastructure sectors can rely on, and to strengthen the wider quantum ecosystem through collaboration with academia, startups and industry.”

2324293.title: Ayush Innovation Sees Eightfold Rise in Patent Filings
2324293.body_html:
AYUSH
Ayush Innovation Sees Eightfold Rise in Patent Filings
Report on Ayush inventions highlights rapid growth in innovation and Intellectual Property activity
Maharashtra Leads Ayush Patent Activity with 744 Filings and 142 Grants
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi

Ayush-related innovation and intellectual property activity in India has witnessed a significant expansion over the past decade, with 4,077 patent applications filed and 711 patents granted between FY 2014–15 and FY 2025–26, according to the Status Report on Ayush Related Inventions in India (2014–2026) released during the celebrations of the 11th Ayurveda Day.

Published by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trademarks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, the report provides an overview of the evolution of Ayush-related inventions and intellectual property activity in India over the period.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, reiterated, “The substantial growth in Ayush-related patent filings and grants reflects the increasing focus on research, innovation and intellectual property in the Ayush sector. The Government is committed to creating an enabling ecosystem where traditional knowledge, scientific research and contemporary innovation can contribute to new products, technologies and solutions while ensuring that India’s rich knowledge systems are appropriately protected.”

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, emphasised, “The steady expansion of patent activity demonstrates the growing research and innovation base of the Ayush sector. The increasing participation of individuals, universities, research institutions, startups and industry is encouraging and will help strengthen the translation of research into innovative solutions. The Ministry will continue to support evidence generation, research collaboration and innovation across the Ayush ecosystem.”

The report highlights a sharp increase in patenting activity, with annual filings rising from 63 applications in FY 2014–15 to 590 applications in FY 2025–26, representing a growth of around 836.5 per cent. Patent filings peaked at 606 applications in FY 2022–23, then fell to 299 in FY 2023–24 before recovering to 590 by FY 2025–26. Annual patent grants also increased substantially, from 3 in FY 2015–16 to 204 in FY 2023–24.

The post-COVID period witnessed a particularly strong acceleration in patent activity. Between FY 2020–21 and FY 2025–26, 2,854 applications, or 70 per cent of total filings, were recorded, compared with 1,223 applications during FY 2014–15 to FY 2019–20. Similarly, 657 patents, accounting for 92.4 per cent of all grants, were awarded during the post-COVID period.

The expanding innovation ecosystem is reflected in the diversity of applicants. Natural persons accounted for 2,113 applications, or 51.9 per cent of total filings, and 398 grants, while educational institutions contributed 995 applications and 88 grants. Together, natural persons and educational institutions accounted for 76.3 per cent of total filings. Corporate and other entities accounted for 700 applications and 176 grants, while small entities and startups contributed 144 and 125 filings, respectively.

The findings of the report underline the growing integration of research, innovation, entrepreneurship and intellectual property protection within the Ayush ecosystem, with increasing participation from individual innovators, educational institutions, research organisations, startups and industry.

2324289.title: BHASHINI and IISc Bangaluru : Text-to-Speech Model for Sourashtra Language
2324289.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
BHASHINI and IISc Bangaluru : Text-to-Speech Model for Sourashtra Language
New AI-based Speech Technology Supports Digital Access, Preservation and Wider Use of a Low-Resource Indian Language
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening language technology for low-resource Indian languages, the Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, has developed Text-to-Speech (TTS) models for Sourashtra, a minority Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by the Sourashtra community in Tamil Nadu.

The initiative aims to expand the availability of speech technology for languages that have limited digital resources and support their use in digital applications, language learning, accessibility solutions, documentation and research.

The newly developed models use the VITS (Variational Inference with adversarial learning for end-to-end Text-to-Speech) architecture and are capable of generating Sourashtra speech directly from text. The models include male and female voices, with each voice available for text written in both Tamil script and Sourashtra script. This enables users to work with Sourashtra in the scripts used for the language.

The models have been trained using a dedicated Sourashtra speech corpus developed at the SPIRE Lab, Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. The corpus contains more than 28 hours of gender-balanced speech recordings, including recordings from one male and one female voice artist. The corpus includes composed sentences as well as sentences drawn from literature, with transcriptions available in both Sourashtra and Tamil scripts.

AIKOSH: BHASHINI’s AIKOSH platform provides access to language datasets and resources that support the development of Indian language technologies. The SPICOR TTS 3.0 Sourashtra Corpus is now available on AIKOSH, offering 28+ hours of gender-balanced Sourashtra speech data developed at IISc Bengaluru. The corpus includes diverse and literary content in both Sourashtra and Tamil scripts, supporting the development of Sourashtra language technologies.

The male voice model was trained on approximately 10,000 utterances, while the female voice model was trained on approximately 11,400 utterances. The speech corpus and associated text data were carefully prepared and cleaned to support the development of the TTS models.

The models generate audio at 22,050 Hz and operate directly on character-level text, eliminating the need for a separate phonemizer. The four models comprise two speaker voices, each available in Tamil-script and Sourashtra-script versions.

Sourashtra, spoken by around 2.48 lakh people according to the 2011 Census, has a relatively limited digital presence and fewer available speech technology resources. The development of these models goes beyond language preservation by helping bring Sourashtra into the digital ecosystem. The technology can benefit the Sourashtra-speaking community by enabling access to digital content in their language, support students and language learners through speech-enabled learning tools, and improve accessibility for users who rely on spoken digital content. At the same time, the availability of the models and underlying speech resources provides researchers, developers and institutions with a foundation to build further Sourashtra language technologies and applications across education, accessibility and other public-facing digital services.

The models can support applications including reading Sourashtra text aloud, language learning, accessibility solutions and research in low-resource speech synthesis, while contributing to the broader development of digital resources for Sourashtra and other underrepresented Indian languages.

Through collaborations with academic and research institutions, BHASHINI continues to strengthen the ecosystem for Indian-language datasets, speech technologies and AI-based language solutions, particularly for languages that remain underrepresented in the digital domain.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is building a national ecosystem for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, and enables the integration of Language AI capabilities across government and public-facing digital services. Its ecosystem includes technologies for translation, speech recognition, speech synthesis, transliteration and other language services, helping make digital information and services more accessible across India's linguistic diversity.

2324281.title: NFSC Fellowship Empowers Ajay Kumar to Pursue His PhD
2324281.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NFSC Fellowship Empowers Ajay Kumar to Pursue His PhD
A Scholar from Kangra, Himachal Pradesh Advances His Academic Aspirations
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 1:54PM by PIB Delhi

A Scholar from Kangra Himachal Pradesh, Ajay Kumar’s journey reflects the determination of students who continue to pursue higher education despite financial challenges.

Ajay Kumar, a 33-year-old scholar is pursuing his Ph.D. with the aspiration of achieving academic excellence, building a successful career and improving his socio-economic circumstances.

Before receiving assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Ajay faced financial constraints and difficulties in meeting educational expenses. His family had limited resources to support the costs associated with higher education, making it challenging to manage the financial requirements of doctoral studies while pursuing his academic goals.

The NFSC Scheme has provided Ajay with financial assistance to support his Ph.D. studies. His fellowship assistance commenced in January 2024 and includes fellowship, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency support. The reported amount of assistance availed is Rs 40,700.

The support has helped address financial constraints, educational expenses and limitations in accessing the resources required for research. With this assistance, Ajay has been able to devote greater attention to his research and academic responsibilities, easing some of the financial pressure associated with pursuing doctoral studies.

Since receiving support under the scheme, Ajay reports improvements in his academic performance and his ability to focus on research. The assistance has also strengthened his confidence and improved his outlook towards future career opportunities. It has helped him continue working towards his long-term goal of completing his PhD and building a successful professional career.

Ajay Kumar’s experience highlights the importance of financial assistance in enabling scholars from financially constrained backgrounds to pursue advanced education. By helping reduce economic barriers, the NFSC Scheme supports students in continuing their academic journeys and working towards their aspirations in research and higher education.

His journey reflects how targeted educational support can help scholars remain focused on their studies, strengthen their confidence and move closer to their academic and professional goals.

2324270.title: First-Ever Kanda Express to Reach Agartala to Strengthen Onion Availability in the North-East
2324270.ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
2324270.body_html:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
First-Ever Kanda Express to Reach Agartala to Strengthen Onion Availability in the North-East
Over 2,800 MT of Buffer Onion Dispatched Across the North-East through Two Kanda Express Rakes and 44 Truck Consignments
Buffer Onion Consignment of Around 440 MT Expected to Reach Agartala by 18th October 2026
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 1:23PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening onion availability and ensuring affordable prices ahead of the festive season, the Department of Consumer Affairs is expanding the distribution of buffer onions under the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF), with the first-ever Kanda Express movement to Agartala, Tripura. The consignment, carrying approximately 440 MT of onions, is expected to reach Agartala by 18th October 2026.

The initiative marks a further expansion of the Government’s onion distribution network in the North-East, following the successful movement of buffer onions to Assam through Kanda Express. The dispatch to Agartala reinforces the Government’s commitment to expanding supply outreach, improving last-mile availability and ensuring timely access to affordable onions across consumption centres in all regions of the country.

Kanda Express to Strengthen Onion Distribution Across Tripura

The intervention is expected to enhance market coverage across seven of Tripura’s eight districts: Dhalai, South Tripura, Khowai, Unakoti, West Tripura, Gomati and Sepahijala.

So far, two Kanda Express rail rakes, carrying 840 MT and 452 MT of onions, respectively, and 44 truck consignments carrying a total of 1,513.46 MT have supplied buffer onions across the North-East. The distribution has covered key locations in Assam, Tripura and Nagaland, including Kamrup, Guwahati, Gomati, Dimapur, Sepahijala, Kohima, Niuland and Chumoukedima.

The expansion of rail-based and road-based distribution is aimed at improving the reach of buffer stocks and supplementing market supplies in key consumption centres across the region.

Fresh Kharif Arrivals Improve Market Availability; Mandi Prices Moderate

With fresh Kharif arrivals gathering pace, onion mandi prices have moderated across major markets. The All-India average mandi price declined from a peak of approximately ₹3,600 per quintal in September to around ₹3,300 per quintal in October.

The calibrated releases from the onion buffer continue to supplement market supplies, improve availability and help moderate retail prices. The Department of Consumer Affairs is continuing these interventions in response to prevailing market conditions to support consumer access to onions at affordable prices.

Retail Onion Prices Decline in 211 Cities; Regional Price Differences Narrow

Over the past two weeks, 211 cities have reported a decline of ₹1–₹13 per kg in retail onion prices. The moderation has been observed across major consuming States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Odisha, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.

In Assam, retail onion prices have also moderated in recent weeks, with around 12 centres in the State recording a decline ranging from ₹1 to ₹8 per kg.

The disparity between Assam’s average retail onion prices and the All-India average has narrowed significantly over the past two years. Two years ago, the average retail price in Assam stood at ₹61.96 per kg, compared with the All-India average of ₹54.13 per kg, representing a difference of ₹7.83 per kg. Currently, Assam’s average retail price is ₹54.30 per kg, while the All-India average stands at ₹53.07 per kg, reducing the difference to ₹1.23 per kg.

This convergence indicates a substantial narrowing of the regional price differential, with retail onion prices in Assam now broadly aligned with the national average.

Onion Buffer Disposal to Continue Based on Market Conditions

The Government continues to closely monitor onion prices, market arrivals and supply conditions across the country. Disposal of onions from the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF) buffer stock is guided by prevailing market conditions, price trends and availability requirements.

Further releases will be undertaken, as required, in accordance with approved operational decisions to ensure adequate market availability and help moderate undue price volatility.

***

2324240.title: Polish Youth Delegation Completes Second Edition of Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme
2324240.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2324240.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Polish Youth Delegation Completes Second Edition of Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi

The second edition of the Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme was held from 7 to 14 October 2026. A 19-member Polish youth delegation visited Gujarat, Maharashtra and New Delhi. The programme comprised of visits to sites of shared historical significance, cultural engagements, visits to institutions showcasing India’s scientific, economic and cultural development and interactions with senior Indian leadership.

The programme was announced by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during his State visit to Poland in August 2024 and forms part of the Five-Year Action Plan (2024–2028) for the India–Poland Strategic Partnership. It envisages an annual exchange of Polish youth to India, providing participants with opportunities to explore the country’s history, culture, institutions and contemporary development.

A major highlight of the programme was the visit to the Balachadi Polish Children’s Camp Memorial in Jamnagar, Gujarat, which commemorates the humanitarian contribution of Maharaja Jam Saheb Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji Jadeja. During the Second World War, the Maharaja provided refuge, education and medical care to Polish children displaced by the war. His compassion earned him the enduring recognition of Dobry Maharaja, or the Good Maharaja, in Poland. The visit offered the delegation an opportunity to learn about this remarkable chapter of shared history and the enduring bonds between the two countries.

Thereafter, the delegation visited the Valivade Polish Refugee Camp Memorial in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, which commemorates the refuge provided to thousands of Polish refugees during and after the Second World War.

The visits to Balachadi and Valivade highlighted India’s humanitarian support to the Polish people during a difficult period and reinforced the historical foundations of India–Poland friendship.

In New Delhi, the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, hosted the Polish youth delegation for an interaction over dinner. The engagement provided an opportunity for the visiting youth to interact with the Minister, exchange perspectives and learn about India’s approach to youth development and participation. The interaction underscored the importance of people-to-people exchanges in fostering mutual understanding and strengthening ties between India and Poland.

The delegates expressed their gratitude for the opportunity to explore India’s rich history and cultural heritage over the course of seven-days. Visits to the Jamsaheb and Valivade camp memorials, Dandi Kutir in Gandhinagar and Kirti Mandir in Porbandar, the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, were among the memorable experiences of the programme. The delegates appreciated the warm hospitality extended to them and described the visit as an enriching experience that had deepened their understanding of India and strengthened their connection with the country.

The delegation also had the opportunity to call on External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and interact with him on matters relating to India–Poland relations and the role of youth exchanges in strengthening bilateral ties.

The successful completion of the second edition reinforces the importance of youth diplomacy in advancing India–Poland relations. By connecting young people with shared history and contemporary India, the programme carries forward the legacy of Maharaja Jam Saheb and strengthens the enduring friendship between the two countries.

***

Pawan Singh Faujdar

2324232.title: Navigating India’s Waterways: Building a Safer, Smarter Network
2324232.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Navigating India’s Waterways: Building a Safer, Smarter Network
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 12:07PM by PIB Delhi

India is building a safer and smarter inland navigation ecosystem as waterway traffic expands. Hydrographic surveys and fairway maintenance keep channels navigable, while India’s first riverine lighthouses on the Brahmaputra add long-range support for 24×7 navigation. Digital platforms provide real-time depth, route and weather information. Together, these interventions are strengthening navigation safety, improving predictability and supporting the growing movement of cargo across India’s waterways.

 

 Strengthening Navigation as Waterways Expand

India’s rivers and waterways are gaining a larger role in the country’s transport network. They are being energised as a force multiplier for the economy, offering a cost-efficient and cleaner mode for transportation. Moving a tonne of freight by water costs roughly one-third of road transport and half of rail. It also generates a fraction of the carbon emissions. This eases pressure on highways and reserves them for passengers and time-sensitive goods.

The country has 111 National Waterways (NW) to promote shipping and navigation. The total length of these waterways is 20,187 km, spread across 23 States and 4 Union Territories. Of these, 32 National Waterways are currently operational. The growing economic value of waterways is reflected in their rapidly increasing freight movement. Cargo movement on inland waterways rose from 29 million metric tonnes (MMT) in 2014–15 to 218 MMT in 2025–26. This represents a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 20.13%. The growth has already surpassed the target of 200 MMT set under Maritime India Vision 2030. Inland waterways are therefore moving from potential to performance.

This expansion of waterways is making it necessary to provide for safer and smarter navigation support and infrastructure that help understand river conditions and navigability across routes. Hydrographic surveys and fairway maintenance are being done to help vessels navigate changing river conditions. Digital platforms are providing information on depths, routes, vessel movement and weather. New navigation infrastructure, including India’s first riverine lighthouses, is adding further support for round-the-clock movement.

 

 Hydrographic Surveys: Knowing the Rivers

A river may appear unchanged from the surface, but the structure of its navigable channel is not visible from outside. Water levels also vary across seasons and river stretches. These changes can affect the route available to vessels. For this reason, inland waterway development requires continuous knowledge of river conditions.

 

Hydrographic surveys

Hydrography involves measuring and describing water bodies and their physical features, like structure of the bed, water depth, flow direction and possible hazards. The purpose is to support navigation and other activities like offshore operations, scientific research, environmental protection and forecasting services. A key objective of hydrographic surveys is to produce navigation charts and maps that provide a clear, comprehensive and updated picture of the surveyed area.

The Inland Waterways Authority of India conducts hydrographic surveys across National Waterways. These surveys measure and analyse river depths, bed profiles, shoals, flow characteristics and morphological changes affecting navigability. These include thalweg surveys that identify and monitor the deepest navigable channel along the river stretch. Terminal & jetty surveys assess depth and approach conditions near terminals and jetties, etc. Continuous hydrographic assessment supports navigational channel (fairway) development, dredging plans, navigational safety and informed decisions for inland water transport (IWT) infrastructure development across the country.

Dredging is the process of removing sediments from the bottom of water bodies. Dredging work is carried out across stretches of National Waterways in order to improve their navigability.

 

River conditions can change rapidly in some stretches. Survey frequency therefore varies according to the requirements of individual waterways. As of September 2026, regular thalweg surveys covered 22 National Waterways. Surveys are conducted weekly, fortnightly or monthly, depending on the waterway. The Indian portion of Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route was also covered under this monitoring system. This is an inland water transit network that enables cargo movement between India and Bangladesh through designated river routes.

Least Available Depth: A Critical Navigation Parameter

One of the most important outputs of hydrographic surveys is the Least Available Depth (LAD). LAD refers to the minimum depth of water available in a navigation channel. It is assessed for a particular stretch and a specific period. LAD directly influences vessel operations and navigation planning. It determines the permissible vessel draft and influences cargo-carrying capacity. It also supports route scheduling and seasonal navigation decisions.

 

 Aids to Navigation: Guiding Vessels Safely

Safe navigation depends on reliable systems that help vessels identify routes, hazards and changing conditions. Under the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021, these systems are formally recognised as Aids to Navigation (AtoN).

An AtoN is a device, system or service external to vessels that is designed and operated to enhance safe and efficient navigation of individual vessels and vessel traffic. These include lighted buoys, radar beacons, lamp posts, channel markers, lighthouses, lightships, etc.

 

Buoys- Floating objects anchored at a definite location to guide or warn mariners, to mark positions of submerged objects, or to moor vessels in lieu of anchoring. Type of buoys include lateral marks, cardinal marks, isolated danger marks, safe water marks, special marks, emergency wreck marking buoy.

Radar beacon (Racon)- Highly responsive, single piece device used by ports and harbor authorities to help mariners easily identify the location of fixed or floating Aids to Navigation. The device transmits in almost any type of weather, unaffected by fog or poor weather and sea conditions.

 

The Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL) is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of general AtoN along India’s coastline. It also serves as the national authority for training on AtoN and Vessel Traffic Services (VTS). India is a signatory to the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), which requires contracting governments to develop and operate appropriate aids to navigation. India also follows the recommendations and guidelines on Aids to Navigation (AtoN) issued by the International Organization for Marine Aids to Navigation (IALA).

Across the national waterways, IWAI maintains a robust system of AToN. Different waterways use different combinations of these aids based on navigation requirements. National Waterway-3 is a strong example of this infrastructure. NW-3, located in the State of Kerala, forms a critical component of the country’s inland water transport network. The West Coast Canal system, connects Kottapuram to Kollam and extends through the Champakkara and Udyogamandal Canals. The entire navigable stretch is equipped with AtoN to support 24×7 navigation. A total of 312 solar-powered lighted FRP (Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic) buoys and 17 beacon lamp posts are deployed along this waterway.

 

 

 Riverine Lighthouses: Bringing 24×7 Navigation Support

India’s inland navigation system entered new territory in March 2026. India announced its first four riverine lighthouses on the Brahmaputra, designated as National Waterway-2. The development marks a significant step in strengthening Aids to Navigation on inland waterways. The four lighthouses are being established at Pandu, Bogibeel, Silghat and Biswanath Ghat. The ₹74-crore project will combine navigational guidance with modern monitoring capabilities.

  • The lighthouses will rise 20 metres above ground, providing prominent navigational reference points.
  • Their geographical range will extend to 14 nautical miles, supporting wider navigational visibility.
  • Their luminous range will extend between 8 and 10 nautical miles, aiding night-time vessel movement.
  • Powered entirely by solar energy, it will provide a clean and reliable source for lighthouse operations.
  • Weather-observation sensors will provide additional information relevant to navigation and safety.
  • The complexes will also feature museums, amphitheatres, cafeterias and landscaped public spaces.
  • Children’s play areas and souvenir shops will add public and tourism-oriented facilities.

Why This Matters for the Brahmaputra

The initiative marks the first deployment of lighthouse infrastructure on an inland waterway in India. It brings a new navigation-safety mechanism to a river corridor with growing transport activity. NW-2 connects Assam's Dhubri to Sadiya across a navigable length of 891 kilometres. It is the longest navigable stretch of any Indian waterway.

The waterway supports movement of cargo, passengers and tourists across the region. It also serves supply chains associated with tea, coal and fertiliser. Cargo movement on NW-2 increased from 0.90 million metric tonnes (MMT) in FY 2024–25 to 1.29 MMT in FY 2025–26. This reinforces the need for stronger navigational infrastructure along the waterway. The new lighthouses will support 24×7 navigation. The project therefore combines navigation safety, technological support and tourism development along the Brahmaputra.

 Digital Navigation & Real-Time Information

Technology is transforming how vessels navigate India’s inland waterways. Digital platforms bring together information on waterways, vessel movement, depth, weather and traffic. This enables mariners and authorities to access critical information when and where it is needed.

Digital Hydrographic Charts: Putting River Information on Screen

Navigation information is provided digitally to Mariners for enhanced safety through modern hydrographic charts. As of September 2026, Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs) have been prepared for 18 operational and tidal waterways. They are uploaded on portals like PANI and IWAI Vessel Tracker. Before 2014, this facility was available only on NW-1 (the Ganga - Bhagirathi - Hooghly river system between Haldia and Prayagraj). Its expansion represents a significant widening of digitally accessible navigation information. The charts complement physical surveys by translating river information into a navigation-ready format.

 

PANI and IWAI Vessel Tracker: Connecting Navigation with Real-Time Information

Navigation involves more than knowing channel depth. The Portal for Asset and Navigation Information (PANI) brings river navigation and infrastructure information on a single platform. PANI provides details about National Waterways and associated assets. These include fairways, infrastructure facilities and cross-river structures. The portal also provides jetty connectivity and emergency services for facilitating transportation of cargo.

The IWAI Vessel Tracker and PANI Portal together form a web and mobile-based e-navigation system. It provides real-time vessel tracking, updated navigation routes and depth information. These features support safe and efficient movement on inland waterways.

Naudarshika: Towards Integrated River Traffic Management

Naudarshika, the National River Traffic and Navigation System, has been launched in 2025 for safe, efficient and sustainable vessel movement. The system incorporates real-time Least Available Depth (LAD) information to support navigation. Alongside existing digital platforms such as PANI and LADIS, Naudarshika adds a dedicated system for river traffic and navigation management.

River Information Services: A Traffic Information Network

River Information Services take digital navigation a step further. RIS combines vessel tracking technologies, weather and water sensors and information technology systems. It provides real-time data to vessel operators and authorities. It also supports communication between vessels and control centres. This exchange supports better traffic management and faster operational decisions.

 

RIS on the Ganga

RIS has been implemented on National Waterway-1 (Ganga) across three stretches. These are Haldia–Farakka, Farakka–Patna and Patna–Varanasi. The system includes 4 control stations and 13 base stations. It incorporates Automatic Identification System (AIS)equipment and Very High Frequency (VHF) communication. Meteorological sensors are also part of the network. RIS consoles have been provided on 30 departmental vessels. Together, these components create a real-time traffic-monitoring system along NW-1.

 

 A Connected Approach to Safer Navigation

Safe navigation on India’s waterways is built on continuous knowledge, reliable infrastructure and timely information. Hydrographic surveys help understand changing river conditions, while navigation aids provide visible guidance on the water. Digital platforms are adding another layer of precision through real-time depth, route, weather and traffic information. Together, these systems are making inland navigation more predictable and responsive. As waterway traffic expands, this integrated approach helps create a stronger foundation for safe, efficient and round-the-clock vessel movement.

2324228.title: APEDA Facilitates Export of 1.755 MT of Organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder from Tamil Nadu to Bulgaria
2324228.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
APEDA Facilitates Export of 1.755 MT of Organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder from Tamil Nadu to Bulgaria
India’s Traditional Palmyra Jaggery Powder Enters Bulgarian Market
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 12:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, facilitated the flag-off of the maiden export consignment of 1.755 MT of NPOP- and EU-certified organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder (Palmyra Blossom Nectar) from Gobichettipalayam in Erode district of Tamil Nadu to Varna, Bulgaria, on 15 October 2026.

The consignment marks an important step towards introducing India’s traditional Palmyra-based products to international markets and diversifying the country’s organic export basket.

The consignment, manufactured and exported by M/s Wellbeing Foods, Erode, in collaboration with M/s Chetty Exports Private Limited, Chennai, will be shipped by sea through Chennai Port. The overseas importer and distributor is M/s Sow Life Ltd, Bulgaria, based in Bulgaria.

The initiative aims to strengthen market linkages for Tamil Nadu’s traditional Palmyra-based products and create new opportunities for producers engaged in organic cultivation. The initiative covers 137 acres under organic cultivation and is expected to benefit farmers through improved market access and export-oriented value chains. The reported price realisation is approximately 15-22% for farmers and 17% higher for the manufacturer, as compared to the domestic market, thereby offering an opportunity to improve returns for participating farmers and support sustainable livelihoods.

Palmyra Jaggery Powder, derived from Palmyra blossom nectar, is a traditional Indian sweetener with potential for value addition and wider international market acceptance. As an alternative to refined sugar, it offers potential nutritional benefits, including vitamins and minerals.

The ceremony was graced by Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev, who also flagged off the consignment. The ceremony was also attended by Secretary, APEDA, Dr. Saswati Bose; senior APEDA officials; representatives of the exporting companies; international partners; progressive farmers; and other stakeholders associated with the export value chain. Their participation highlighted the collaborative efforts to strengthen India’s agricultural exports.

Palmyra-based products are associated with traditional production practices and the use of the Palmyra palm, which has long been part of the agricultural and cultural landscape of Tamil Nadu. Developing export-ready products from this resource offers scope to expand market opportunities while supporting producers and the wider value chain.

APEDA continues to facilitate the export of certified organic and value-added agricultural products by supporting market development, quality compliance and linkages between Indian producers and overseas buyers. The maiden export of organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder to Bulgaria is expected to open avenues for further market expansion and strengthen the presence of India’s traditional products in international markets.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ C N Abhijith Narayanan/ Abhimanyu Panwar
