2323996.title: ‘Swachhata se Samman, Har Varg ka Utthan’
2323996.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Swachhata se Samman, Har Varg ka Utthan’
Senior Citizen Homes under AVYAY Undertake Swachhata Drive as Part of Special Campaign 6.0
764 Senior Citizen Homes Supported under IPSrC Directed to Undertake Cleanliness, Decluttering, Waste Management, Greening Activities; Active Participation of Elderly Residents Emphasized
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, is actively participating in Special Campaign 6.0, the Government-wide initiative aimed at institutionalizing Swachhata, promoting efficient management of public spaces and reducing pendency in Government offices and institutions.

In furtherance of the objectives of the Campaign, the Department, under its umbrella scheme Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), has directed all 764 Senior Citizen Homes supported under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) to undertake cleanliness and sanitation activities.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the initiative seeks to strengthen cleanliness practices in institutions providing care and support to senior citizens and to ensure that these facilities maintain a clean, safe, accessible and dignified living environment for elderly residents.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

He said the Campaign, coordinated by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), underscores the importance of cleanliness, systematic waste management, environmental sustainability and the development of a culture of continuous improvement across public institutions.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Senior Citizen Homes have been advised to undertake comprehensive cleanliness drives covering their premises, common areas and surrounding spaces, along with decluttering, appropriate waste segregation and disposal, removal of unwanted materials and greening activities. The emphasis is on ensuring that cleanliness becomes an integral part of the daily functioning of these institutions rather than remaining confined to a time-bound campaign.

 

 

 Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official said that building upon the momentum generated during the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6.0, the Senior Citizen Homes under AVYAY across the country have been undertaking a range of activities in accordance with the Campaign's theme, ‘Swachhata se Samman, Har Varg ka Utthan’. He said these activities reflect the importance of maintaining hygienic and orderly institutional environments, particularly in facilities where senior citizens reside and receive care and assistance.

 Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

He said the observance of the Swachhata Drive across the network of 764 IPSrC-supported Senior Citizen Homes also reflects the principle of Jan Bhagidari, recognising that sustainable improvements in cleanliness and public hygiene require the participation and cooperation of all stakeholders. The involvement of residents and caregivers helps strengthen collective responsibility for maintaining clean surroundings and encourages the adoption of good practices in everyday institutional life.

 Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official elaborated that the cleanliness drives include sweeping and cleaning residential premises, corridors, dining areas, kitchens, recreational spaces and other common facilities; cleaning approach roads and surrounding areas; removing litter, dry leaves, weeds and overgrown vegetation; and ensuring the proper collection, segregation and disposal of waste.

 

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

He added these Homes have also been encouraged to remove unnecessary and unused materials, organize storage spaces and maintain clear and accessible pathways to facilitate the safe movement of elderly residents.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official further said the greening and environmental improvement activities form an important component of the initiative adding that plantation of saplings, maintenance of gardens and green spaces, and efforts to improve the overall appearance of institutional campuses contribute to a healthier and more pleasant living environment. Such measures also encourage environmental awareness and promote the responsible use and maintenance of shared spaces, he said.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The Official said the initiative places particular emphasis on the active participation of senior citizens, staff members and implementing agencies. He added that by involving elderly residents in suitable cleanliness, gardening and campus-improvement activities, the Campaign promotes a sense of ownership, collective responsibility and community participation as the participation is encouraged in a manner appropriate to the health, mobility and individual capacities of residents, ensuring that the activities remain inclusive, safe and meaningful.

 

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

 

The participation of Senior Citizen Homes in Special Campaign 6.0 reinforces the Department's commitment to dignified ageing, improved institutional care and the promotion of active ageing.

Glimpses of the cleanliness drive at Senior Citizen Homes supported under IPSrC, AVYAY

The initiative is aligned with the broader objectives of AVYAY, which seeks to create an enabling environment for senior citizens through institutional and community-based support, improved access to services and the promotion of their well-being and dignity. Through the IPSrC component, the Department supports eligible implementing agencies in providing institutional care and essential services to senior citizens, particularly those who require continued care, protection and assistance.

The Senior Official said the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment will continue to encourage Senior Citizen Homes under AVYAY to sustain the practices adopted during Special Campaign 6.0 beyond the Campaign period. Regular cleanliness schedules, responsible waste management, periodic decluttering, maintenance of green spaces and active resident participation are expected to remain important elements of institutional management.

Through these efforts, the Department seeks to reinforce a culture of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and dignity in senior citizen care institutions, in keeping with the Government of India's commitment to cleaner, greener and more inclusive public institutions and to ensuring a safe, healthy and dignified living environment for senior citizens across the country.

A clean and well-maintained environment is an important component of the overall well-being of senior citizens, contributing to their comfort, safety, dignity and quality of life. Regular attention to sanitation, waste management and the upkeep of common areas can also help reduce avoidable environmental hazards and support the maintenance of healthier residential facilities.

2323959.title: Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
2323959.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
Event highlights the pivotal role of women farmers  in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat
Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra  highlights  invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors; emphasises  the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, celebrated Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 today (15 October 2026 ) at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The programme was organised to recognise the invaluable contribution of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their pivotal role in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.

 

Sh. Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in his address, highlighted the invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors, particularly in ensuring food security, sustaining rural livelihoods, managing natural resources and driving agricultural development. He emphasised the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture through various initiatives, including direct income support, affordable institutional credit, technology transfer, skill development, farm mechanisation and improved access to agricultural marketing infrastructure.

महिला किसान दिवस के अवसर पर अपनी सभी किसान बहनों को प्रणाम करता हूं। भारत गांव के बिना अधूरा है और गांव खेती के बिना और खेती महिलाओं के बिना नहीं हो सकती। अनादि काल से हमारी बहनें खेती में सबसे महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका का निर्वहन करती आ रही हैं। महिला किसान हमारी कृषि व्यवस्था की रीढ़ हैं और देश की खाद्य सुरक्षा एवं ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूती प्रदान कर रही हैं। बदलते युग और खेती के तरीकों में आज बहनों की भूमिका खेती में बहुत महत्वपूर्ण हो गई है। अब ड्रोन दीदी है जो दवाओं का छिड़काव करती हैं, कृषि सखी हैं जो किसानों को कृषि पद्धतियों की ट्रेनिंग देती हैं, बैंक सखी हैं जो बैंक से टाई-अप करती हैं, पशु सखी हैं जो पशुपालन और दूध उत्पादन के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है। किसान के कच्चे उत्पाद के प्रोसेसिंग का काम हमारी बहनें कर रही हैं और इन उत्पादों को लोगों तक पहुँचाने में हमारी बहनें किसान दीदियाँ FPOs के माध्यम से बहुत महत्वपूर्ण काम कर रही हैं। आइए, मेरी बहनों, महिला किसान दिवस पर हम यह संकल्प लें कि कृषि के हर आयाम पर हम काम करेंगे। हम खुद भी आगे बढ़ेंगे, खेती आगे बढ़ाएँगे, देश आगे बढ़ाएँगे। मुझे विश्वास है कि देश की नारी शक्ति आत्मनिर्भर कृषि, समृद्ध ग्रामीण भारत और विकसित भारत @2047 के संकल्प को साकार करने में निर्णायक भूमिका निभाएँगी। महिला किसान सशक्त होंगी, तो कृषि समृद्ध होगी; कृषि समृद्ध होगी, तो भारत विकसित होगा। सभी को महिला किसान दिवस पर हार्दिक बधाई एवं शुभकामनाएं!

— Shivraj Singh Chouhan (@ChouhanShivraj) October 15, 2026

The programme witnessed the participation of progressive women farmers, women agricultural extension workers and functionaries from various States/UTs, along with senior officers of DA&FW. The theme for Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 was “Role of Women Farmers in Building Developed Agriculture and a Developed India.” The theme underscores the vital role of women in strengthening agricultural productivity, promoting sustainable farming practices, conserving natural resources and contributing to rural prosperity.

 

As part of the programme, outstanding women farmers were felicitated in recognition of their achievements and contributions to agriculture and allied sectors. The felicitation acknowledged their dedication, resilience, innovation and leadership in agricultural activities and rural entrepreneurship. A book titled “Women Farmers of India: Journey from Challenges to Success” was also released during the event. This book is a compilation of inspiring success stories of women farmers, highlighting their remarkable contributions, achievements, innovations, and journeys from struggle to success in agriculture and allied sectors. It proudly showcases the vital role of women in agriculture, recognising their potential, leadership, and entrepreneurial spirit.

 

The programme also provided a platform for women farmers and extension functionaries to share their experiences and journeys. A few participants addressed the gathering and spoke about their personal experiences, challenges, achievements and contributions to agriculture. Their accounts highlighted the important role of women in adopting improved agricultural practices, strengthening rural livelihoods and inspiring other women to participate in agricultural development.

 

Women farmers make significant contributions across the agricultural value chain, including crop cultivation, livestock management, seed conservation, natural resource management, post-harvest activities and value addition. Their traditional knowledge, entrepreneurial initiatives and adoption of innovative and climate-resilient practices are essential to making Indian agriculture more productive, sustainable and inclusive.

Women agricultural officers and extension functionaries also play a crucial role in bridging the gap between agricultural research and farming communities. Through training, technology dissemination, awareness generation and guidance on government schemes, they facilitate the adoption of scientific agricultural practices and empower women farmers with knowledge and institutional support.

The celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to recognising women as key stakeholders in agricultural transformation. It highlighted the importance of strengthening women's access to technology, resources, capacity-building opportunities and institutional support, while encouraging their greater participation in decision-making and leadership across agriculture and allied sectors.

Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 is also being observed across States and Union Territories, Extension Education Institutes (EEIs), State Agricultural Management and Extension Training Institutes (SAMETIs) and MANAGE, with participation from women farmers and other agricultural stakeholders. Special emphasis has been placed on the participation of women farmers from tribal regions.

The celebration reinforced the message that empowering women farmers and recognising their contributions are essential to building developed agriculture, strengthening rural livelihoods and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.

2323953.title: TDB-DST supports Development and Commercialisation of Indigenous 32-Slice CT Scanner by Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
2323953.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST supports Development and Commercialisation of Indigenous 32-Slice CT Scanner by Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

Strengthening India’s indigenous medical device manufacturing capabilities under the Government of India’s Make in India initiative, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd., Malur, Karnataka, to support the development and commercialisation of an indigenous 32-slice Computed Tomography (CT) Scanner.

Panacea Medical Technologies, an Indian medical device manufacturer specialising in radiotherapy and radiology, has established capabilities in developing advanced technologies, processes, modules and products for medical imaging and cancer treatment. Building on its expertise in high-precision imaging, the company has undertaken the development of a diagnostic CT scanner to expand its portfolio into advanced diagnostic imaging.

The project envisages the design, development and deployment of a 32-slice CT scanner for diagnostic imaging across various clinical disciplines. CT scanners use rotating X-ray systems and digital detectors to capture cross-sectional images, which are reconstructed through computer algorithms to generate detailed images of internal body structures. Their development requires precise engineering, integration of imaging components and rigorous calibration to ensure imaging accuracy and patient safety.

India’s diagnostic imaging sector is witnessing growing demand for advanced technologies, driven by expanding healthcare infrastructure, the rising burden of chronic diseases and the need for timely and accurate diagnosis. Indigenous development of high-end medical equipment can contribute to strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and reducing dependence on imported technologies.

The Government of India has identified medical devices as a priority sector under the Make in India initiative. Through its support for indigenous technology development, TDB seeks to enable Indian enterprises to develop advanced medical technologies, strengthen domestic manufacturing and improve access to healthcare equipment.

Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “The development of an indigenous CT scanner aligns with the Government of India’s vision of strengthening domestic manufacturing of high-end medical devices under the Make in India initiative. TDB’s support aims to encourage medical technology companies to develop innovative indigenous solutions that can address the country’s healthcare requirements while creating opportunities for wider adoption in global markets. Such initiatives can contribute to building India’s capabilities as a manufacturer of advanced medical equipment.”

Promoter of Panacea Medical Technologies Pvt. Ltd., said, “We express our sincere gratitude to the Technology Development Board for its pivotal support. This collaboration will accelerate our efforts to develop indigenous diagnostic imaging technology and contribute to making advanced CT imaging more accessible across India.”

2323918.title: Raksha Rajya Mantri Chairs Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference of NCC in Guwahati, Assam
2323918.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Rajya Mantri Chairs Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference of NCC in Guwahati, Assam
Ministers from 7 NER states, Sikkim and West Bengal participated in the conference
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Rajya Mantri (RRM) Shri Sanjay Seth attended the Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference 2026 in Guwahati, Assam, organised by the National Cadet Corps (NCC) on October 15, 2026. The conference deliberated on the expansion, strengthening and effective functioning of the NCC in the North Eastern Region (NER), West Bengal and Sikkim.

Addressing the conference, RRM appreciated the participation of cadets from the North Eastern States in the Republic Day Camp (RDC) and the increasing enrolment of girl cadets, reflecting the NCC’s contribution to women’s empowerment. He emphasised the need to work towards the Prime Minister’s vision of expanding the NCC from its present strength of approximately 17 lakh cadets to 20 lakh. RRM stressed the importance of motivating and guiding the youth to imbibe the spirit of ‘Nation First’. He called upon all nine participating States to formulate and implement practical, actionable plans for NCC expansion, with particular emphasis on strengthening infrastructure and enhancing training facilities for cadets and reaffirmed the Government’s commitment towards it.

 

Quoting the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi "The NCC is a movement that empowers India's Yuva Shakti, making our youth confident, disciplined, and dedicated to the nation," RRM emphasised on ensuring effective training, adequate institutional support and improved coordination among stakeholders to strengthen the organisation’s outreach and functioning.

The conference provided a platform for strengthening coordination between the NCC and the State Governments, with deliberations focusing on expanding NCC coverage, cadet welfare, training infrastructure, institutional strengthening and addressing administrative challenges. It also emphasised the contribution of NCC towards social service and community development, character-building, leadership, national integration and the development of a spirit of service among young people.

The North Eastern Region NCC Directorate provides coverage across the seven States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura through nine Group Headquarters and 50 units. NCC is present in 1,645 educational institutions in the region, with a strength of approximately 1.25 lakh cadets. Similarly, the West Bengal & Sikkim NCC Directorate provides coverage through six Group Headquarters and 56 units, with NCC activities extending to 1,326 educational institutions and approximately 1.25 lakh cadets.

The conference, led by Director General NCC, Lt Gen Virendra Vats, was attended by Additional Secretary, Mrs Dipti Mohil Chawla, Ministers and senior officials from the participating States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, West Bengal and Sikkim and Senior officials from Ministry of Defence & NCC.

2323670.title: Lucknow to Host Third Regional Workshop on Training Institute Transformation on 23 and 24 October 2026
2323670.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2323670.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Lucknow to Host Third Regional Workshop on Training Institute Transformation on 23 and 24 October 2026
Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, to inaugurate the workshop in the presence of Dr Jitendra Singh; eight States and four Union Territories of the Northern Region to participate
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 10:56AM by PIB Delhi

The Capacity Building Commission (CBC) will hold the third regional workshop of Sādhana Śhrinkhla 2026 at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, on 23 and 24 October 2026. The two-day consultation will bring together States and Union Territories of the Northern Region to deliberate on how Government Training Institutes can grow into modern, competency-driven capacity building institutions under Mission Karmayogi.

The workshop will be inaugurated by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, in the august presence of Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon'ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

A Regional Series with a National Purpose

Sādhana Śhrinkhla, short for Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement, is a series of four regional consultative workshops. It carries forward the conversation on institutional reform that the Commission has led over the past year through Regional Task Force meetings, Sādhana Saptah from 2 to 8 April 2026, and the National Departmental Summit on Institutionalising Capacity Building in May 2026.

The series opened at Vijayawada on 29 and 30 September 2026, followed by the North Eastern Region workshop at Guwahati on 9 October 2026. Lucknow now takes the dialogue to the Northern Region.

Participating States and Union Territories

Hosted by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, the workshop will see participation from the States of Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand, and the Union Territories of Chandigarh, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh. Senior State officials will be joined by heads and faculty of Training Institutes, subject experts and industry partners.

With eight States and four Union Territories spanning the Himalayan region, the Indo-Gangetic plains and the desert State of Rajasthan, the Lucknow workshop brings together the widest range of administrative contexts in the series so far.

What the Workshop Will Address

Civil servants today are expected to keep pace with new technologies, changing citizen expectations and complex development priorities. Training Institutes are central to preparing them for this, and the workshop will focus on how they can respond more closely to what officials actually need in their roles.

Deliberations will cover four broad areas: institutional governance and leadership; operational effectiveness and collaboration between institutes; faculty and institutional competencies; and digital transformation, including the use of Artificial Intelligence in training. Each participating State and Union Territory will be supported in identifying its own priorities and drawing up a practical roadmap for reform.

UNNATI as the Common Platform

These reforms will be taken forward through the Unified New-Age National Training Initiatives (UNNATI) portal, launched during Sādhana Saptah 2026. UNNATI connects more than 700 Training Institutes on a single platform and links them to the competency needs identified in Capacity Building Plans, helping institutes share resources, collaborate and improve on the basis of data.

Shaping the Training Institute Transformation Framework

The outcomes of the Lucknow workshop, together with those from Vijayawada, Guwahati and the final regional workshop, will feed into the Training Institute Transformation Framework being developed by the Commission. The Framework will offer a common direction for reform while leaving room for each State's institutional realities.

Through Sādhana Śhrinkhla, the Commission aims to build a connected and responsive network of Training Institutes that equips civil servants to serve citizens better, in keeping with the vision of Mission Karmayogi and Viksit Bharat 2047.

****
